stories.title: ₹11,000 crore Noida Airport flooded after rain:Akhilesh asks, ‘Will boats run here?’ BJP MLA hits back, says he cannot see development
stories.summary: The Jewar International Airport, built at a cost of approximately 11 thousand crore rupees in Greater Noida, UP, could not withstand the first rain. Here, due to heavy rain on Tuesday, the path connecting the terminal and parking lot was waterlogged. Employees were seen mopping. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav on Wednesday, targeting the BJP government, said- You are building an airport, and it got waterlogged. You are building an expressway, and it developed potholes. Some similarities are visible between those who fly airplanes and those who run the state. Earlier, Akhilesh had posted a video on his X account. He wrote - 'Will boats now run at the airport? Where there is a BJP government, there is massive corruption.' Responding to the SP chief's taunt, BJP MLA from Jewar, Dhirendra Singh, retaliated. At 1 PM on Wednesday, he himself reached the spot where water had accumulated. He said - 'Those who cannot see the development of Jewar, only see potholes and water.' The first phase of Jewar Airport was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on March 28, 2026. Commercial flights began on June 15, 2026. It cost 11,200 crore rupees. See 3 pictures Now read the complete statement of Jewar MLA Jewar MLA Dhirendra Singh said- There was a time when Noida International Airport was limited only to papers and discussions. Now the same project is taking shape on the ground and Jewar is becoming a new identity of development. According to him, work is progressing rapidly in the area and the changes are clearly visible. He said- We are praying to Lord Indra for more and more rain, so that the water level can rise. I am standing at the place where pictures were posted yesterday (Tuesday) showing waterlogging at Jewar Airport. We are not denying waterlogging, but the water that came from above due to yesterday's torrential rain had filled this area. But it was drained out in 20 to 25 minutes. And this was the first rain after the airport started, so arrangements are being made to ensure that water does not accumulate here in the future. But those who see potholes and look for such shortcomings, they are not seeing the development of this Jewar. They are not seeing that where I stand today, it is one of the best and grandest airports in the world, which will give a huge gift to the economy of this entire country in the coming time. And this is a place that will bring countless opportunities for the youth of entire North India. Look, the thinking should be positive. During your time, the airport did not come to Jewar, during your time, our state's economy did not reach the second position, during your time, there was corruption, there was hooliganism on the streets. We understand, people understand. Akhilesh is not worried about water, but about the airport being built The MLA said - Your (Akhilesh Yadav's) concern is not about the waterlogging at the airport, but rather your concern is how Jewar Airport was built? And how Jewar has become the world's best destination for investment today? So I want to urge those brothers of mine that the unprecedented development that has taken place in this state, if they also showcase it from their handles, people will appreciate it. And it is a sign of their frustration that they only see potholes, they see broken roads. They do not see how a network of highways has been laid in this state, how large infrastructures have been provided for the prosperity of the people. Through this airport, I want to say that in the coming time, this Jewar Airport will be such a destination in the world. Now you see that people from Greater Noida reach here in 35 minutes and fly towards their destination. Such a facility that we had never even imagined. People from Agra will take flights from here, people from Bareilly will take flights from here. And when the Greenfield link of the Ganga Expressway is built, just imagine that all our districts and Uttarakhand in the foothills of the Himalayas, people from there will benefit from this Jewar Airport. Rajnath Singh gave the idea for a new airport in 2001

stories.title: UP women to get ₹50,000:₹20,000 first instalment before polls, followed by three ₹10,000 instalments
stories.summary: The UP government may implement a major scheme before the assembly elections to secure the women's vote bank. Under this, women will be provided financial assistance of ₹50-50,000. The first installment of ₹20,000 will be given before the elections. After the elections, if the BJP government is formed, 3 installments of ₹10,000 will be given. Deliberations on the scheme have begun in the government. Government will woo women before elections The Yogi government has started preparations for the assembly elections. Amid the Gen-Z movement, the government is considering a major scheme to secure the women's vote bank. A scheme is being considered for women's assistance, self-employment, and economic self-reliance. The scheme will be proposed through the Women Welfare Department. Under the scheme, consideration is being given to providing financial assistance of ₹50,000 to women. Priority to women from families below poverty line The government will prioritize women from SC, ST families along with women from BPL families and women from economically weaker families in the scheme. This may include women from families whose income does not exceed ₹12 lakh. The scheme will be a gamechanger Government sources believe that the cash incentive scheme for women could prove to be a game-changer in the assembly elections. Such a scheme was first implemented in Madhya Pradesh, then in Maharashtra and Bihar assembly elections. Due to those schemes, BJP governments were formed there. BJP's focus on women and elderly Just before the UP Assembly elections, the Yogi government is going to provide major relief to more than 1.18 crore pension beneficiaries. This includes the elderly, widows, destitute women, and persons with disabilities. The government is going to increase their pension schemes by ₹500 every month. Apart from this, a provision of ₹400 crore has also been made for distributing scooters to meritorious girl students. Girl students from families with an annual income of up to ₹12 lakh will get a helmet along with the scooter, 4 liters of petrol, free registration, and insurance.

stories.title: Man dances after stealing ₹5 lakh bike:Grooves at Varanasi agency; drinks coffee, stays in washroom
stories.summary: A second video has surfaced showing the man who allegedly stole a KTM Adventure 390 S bike worth around ₹5 lakh in Varanasi. He moved around the showroom without any apparent fear, drank coffee, used the washroom, and even played music while dancing with one hand raised in the air. The accused entered the dealership at around 11.30 pm on Monday. He used a glass cutter to cut through the glass at the main entrance. The video surfaced on Tuesday. According to the agency manager, the accused entered the showroom, lay down, and even took a nap. After stealing the bike, he initially tried to take it out through the broken glass, but there was not enough space. He then smashed the entire glass panel before fleeing with the bike at around 4 am. The accused spent nearly four and a half hours inside the showroom. The bike’s on-road price is around ₹4.71 lakh. See three pictures... Now read the complete matter There is a TRIUMPH bike showroom in the city's Manduadih police station area. Triumph is a British motorcycle company that manufactures premium bikes. The agency is named after this company. The general manager of this showroom is Rohit Kumar Singh. He said that on Monday, around 10 pm, we closed the agency, and the staff and I went home. I had parked my KTM bike at the agency itself. The key was left in it. I had bought it just three months ago. The manager said that at 5 am my guard called, saying the main door of the showroom was broken. On this, I immediately reached the agency. One part of the main gate was cut from below. The other part was broken. Its glass was scattered inside and outside the showroom. I reached inside the showroom. First, I counted the bikes kept in the showroom. I looked at the auto parts inventory. After that, I went to the back stockyard, where our bikes are kept. I checked the bikes there as well. I had parked my bike at that same place and gone home. When I checked, my bike was missing. From our accessories, besides a T-shirt and a cap of our brand, a vehicle cover was also missing. I immediately informed the police. The police agency arrived in 15 minutes. We checked the CCTV footage. The thief was caught on camera. The forensic team has taken fingerprints from the scene. Cut the door in 36 minutes, made a lungi from bike cover, danced Manager Rohit Kumar Singh said that, in the CCTV footage, at exactly 11:30, a young man wearing a white shirt and jeans appeared standing outside the agency. He had a photo of a goddess in his hand. Then, he pushed the agency's door. He peeked inside. After this, he started cutting the glass door with a cutter. Just then, heavy rain started, so he went to the back side. From there, he tore a board banner, brought it, and sat covering himself with it. Then he started cutting the door. At around 12:06 AM, he entered the showroom. He turned on the computer system kept at the reception. He sat on the chair and kept roaming around for a long time. After that, he opened and checked several bikes. He took out water from the mini fridge and drank it. After that, he made coffee from the coffee machine and drank it. He took a bath in the washroom. He spread his clothes on top of the bike. He tore the cover of a bike and made it like a lungi; he played songs and danced. He took the showroom's T-shirt and cap. After this, he took the bike and left. Regarding the incident, Manduwadih Inspector Ajay Raj Verma said- Accused's photo has been sent to all police stations through the control room. The description has been matched with a thief, and raids are being conducted to search for him. The location, IP address, and active number network of the accused are also being traced.

stories.title: Women to travel free on buses during Raksha Bandhan:UP government plans to run buses for 6 more days; employees' leave cancelled
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government is set to give women and girls the gift of free travel on roadways buses during Raksha Bandhan. The State Road Transport Corporation has sent a proposal to the government seeking approval for the free travel facility, which is expected soon. Meanwhile, Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh has directed officials to operate additional buses during Raksha Bandhan to meet the expected increase in passenger demand. The free travel facility will be available from 6 am on 27 August to midnight on 29 August. Last year, Raksha Bandhan was celebrated on 9 August, and the government had allowed women to travel free from 6 am on 8 August to midnight on 10 August. Additional buses will run from 26 to 31 August Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh has given instructions that more buses should be run from 26 to 31 August for the convenience of passengers on Rakshabandhan. During this period, all buses of the Transport Corporation will be operated. Instructions have been given for cleanliness and arrangement of clean drinking water at all bus stations. Instructions have also been given to improve the arrangement of lights and fans in the waiting rooms at bus stations. Along with this, the control room will remain operational 24 hours. Relaxation will be given on some routes Transport Corporation MD Prabhu N. Singh informed that there will be fewer buses going from Delhi to Ghaziabad, Meerut, Moradabad via Moradabad-Bareilly. Similarly, restrictions for Ghaziabad, Agra and Etawah via Delhi to Aligarh-Kanpur will be reduced. Not only this, if there are 60 percent passengers from the starting point for western regions, then additional buses will be run. No leave for 6 days MD Prabhu N. Singh informed that except for special circumstances like death in the family or one's own illness, no leave will be granted to officers, supervisors, drivers-conductors associated with bus operations. During this period, officers deployed in the area will not remain absent from workplace without permission. If found doing so, action will be taken as per rules. During this period, all contracted buses will be operated. They will also not be given leave. Additional services will be provided for Lucknow and Kanpur. Those who complete tasks will get bonus MD Prabhu N. Singh stated that drivers and conductors who complete 1800 km of operation during the 6 days of the festival will be given an incentive amount of 1200 rupees. Contract drivers and conductors who operate buses for more than 1800 km during this period will be given an incentive of 55 paise per kilometer. Technical staff of depots and regional workshops who remain present daily during this period will be given an incentive of 500 rupees. Rakshabandhan is on 28th August This time, the festival of Rakshabandhan is on 28th August. After 12 years, such an auspicious alignment is forming that this time there will be no shadow of Bhadra on Rakshabandhan. In such a situation, sisters can tie rakhi on their brothers' wrists throughout the day. Purnima on 27th August will start at 8:31 AM and will continue till 9:18 AM on 28th August. Rakhi can be tied during this time.

stories.title: Ravi Kishan praises Gen-Z amid trolling:Says, 'Young generation pulled him out of ‘abyss’, 'I’ve gone crazy, mind isn’t working'
stories.summary: Gorakhpur BJP MP and Bhojpuri actor Ravi Kishan, who was recently trolled on social media over his vow of silence and some of his statements, praised Gen-Z on Wednesday. Speaking at the Parliament complex, he said, “Gen-Z has left me speechless. I salute their intelligence. The love they have shown me is increasing every day.” Kishan added, “I was living in obscurity, but Gen-Z brought me out of it.” Meanwhile, a humorous reaction from his wife, Preeti Shukla, has also gone viral. Ravi Kishan himself shared the incident. According to the BJP MP, his wife told him that he goes viral on the internet every time he steps out of the house. She then jokingly told their children that he should be locked inside a room so he could not go outside and end up going viral on social media. Now, the complete story of Ravi Kishan I salute the brains of Gen-Z: These people have left me speechless. As far as I remember, I have never seen anything like this in this country. The immense love that Gen-Z has showered upon me has been historic, and it is not stopping. It is growing day by day. Therefore, I invite all those young people, all Gen-Z, who are the future of this country, who are destined to come to this Parliament one day. I salute your brains. The kind of creativity you people are showing is incredible. You people have made me, my style, my words, my name, and even my fame so big and immense. You people pulled us out of the abyss: Ravi Kishan said that young people make up 65% of the population and that Prime Minister Narendra Modi himself interacts with them on Instagram and listens to their views. He said, “Gen-Z gave me my name. They gave recognition to an unknown Ravi Kishan. Otherwise, I was living in the netherworld. You people brought me out of there.” No planning behind going viral: I myself don't understand how all this suddenly became so big. This is the blessing of Mahadev. Some different game is going on; this is madness. The month of Sawan is going on, and when Mahadev gives his blessings, this happens. This has never happened before with anyone in this country, whether an actor or a politician. It's madness. People say anything to become famous, and my vow of silence became even more famous. There was no planning behind me going viral. I didn't intentionally do anything to make his videos go viral. The most surprising thing is that many big social media handles are also making memes of me. See the most viral pictures Said by speaking: Today is our vow of silence; people called him Meme King Even though the monsoon session of Parliament was marred by uproar, Ravi Kishan remained in the discussion among Gen-Z. Clips like ‘Home from Work’, ‘Jaldi the Late’ and ‘NEET Akhbar’ were rapidly shared on the internet. On 4 August, Ravi Kishan was seen avoiding media questions outside the Parliament premises and gave such a smiling answer that the video went viral instantly. As soon as journalists tried to ask him questions, he replied with a smile, Today is a vow of silence. Today, Pandit ji told me to remain silent. What to do? Today is my vow of silence. Let me be quiet today. His style was recorded on camera, and the video quickly went viral on various social media platforms. People started calling him the Meme King. Ravi Kishan to appear in Mirzapur film Ravi Kishan is quite busy these days. Currently, he is in the news regarding 'Mirzapur' movie. His character 'Babban Babua' in the film is the most talked about. According to the affidavit filed for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, Ravi Kishan's total assets are approximately ₹43 crore. Ravi Kishan's immovable properties are worth around ₹27 crore, which include flats in Mumbai and Pune, a bungalow in Gorakhpur, and an ancestral house in the village. The value of movable properties is more than ₹15 crore. He also owns several luxury cars, including Toyota Innova, Fortuner, Mercedes, BMW, and Jaguar.

stories.title: Sanjay Nishad says, 'Fish cooked without onion-garlic is vegetarian':'Nishads are a warrior community, not traitors'
stories.summary: UP government Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad called fish vegetarian. He said- Fish prepared without garlic and onion is vegetarian. The symbol of the UP government and India's constitution is fish, arrow and bow. This is the symbol of the Nishad community, which we are proud of. Minister Sanjay Nishad made these statements at a media channel's program in Gorakhpur on Tuesday. He said that we take pride in the fact that even though Nishads received poverty in return, they are sons of loyalty. Nishads are not sons of traitors. We may be in huts, but the label of warrior community is definitely attached. 4 big statements of Minister Sanjay Nishad 1- Nishad has never betrayed the country and has stood with loyalty Sanjay Nishad said that we are not the ones asking now! We are the ones who give, the ones who ferry across. We are people who are loyal to the country and have nationalist thinking. In this country, the British were traitors; the Mughals were traitors. They had formed regiments and recruited traitors. We take pride that, in return, the Nishads may have received poverty, but they are sons of loyalty. Nishads are not sons of traitors. They are sons of nationalism. Today we may be landless. We may be in huts, but one label is definitely attached - of a martial community. 2. The emblem of UP is the emblem of King Guhyaraj Nishad Uttar Pradesh should be proud that the emblem of the state government - fish, bow-arrow, and water... This is the emblem of King Guhyaraj Nishad. Which we take pride in. One label is attached: Nishads have never betrayed the country; they have stood with loyalty. Sanjay Nishad said that PM Narendra Modi and UP Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stand with the Nishad community. He said, “You can see how much love Yogi ji gives us. The MLAs are also present here, so I am saying that at least keep feeding them fish. Anything prepared without garlic and onion is vegetarian.” 3. Once Britain was visible in India, today India is visible in Britain ''I had gone to London for the Amrit Mahotsav of Independence. Some officials were troublesome; they didn't want to let me go. But I spoke to Modi ji, and I went. Ravi Kishan bhaiya was also there. He entertained people by singing songs, but when we got the mic, we left everyone stunned. I said that there was a time when London was visible in India, as Britain ruled the country for 350 years, but today India is visible in London. He added that true Indianness would be achieved when an Indian-origin Prime Minister is formed in Britain too. 6 months later, Rishi Sunak became Prime Minister. He said, “Aren’t we fortunate?'' 4. Not vote theft, but note-job theft We say that ₹6.5 billion is being taken away by the bicycle and elephant people. ₹7.5 billion is being taken away every month by the bicycle people. ₹28 billion goes into salaries in Uttar Pradesh. First tell me this: ''Will this society only pay salaries and not build the future of its children? This pain is upon them. Whenever there is talk of “vote theft”, they should also talk about the alleged theft of money and jobs from the youth. Those who have taken away the money and employment opportunities of young people are responsible for their suffering. Referring to the principle that communities should get a share based on their population, he said the Nishad community has a significant population. Also referred to the community’s name as “Bansuti” and described it in the context of backward communities.''

stories.title: 'Mirzapur' movie cast arrives in Lucknow:Ali Fazal, Divyenndu, Jitendra Kumar share journey from series to film
stories.summary: The star cast of ‘Mirzapur: The Movie’ arrived in Lucknow on Wednesday to promote the film. The popular OTT series ‘Mirzapur’ had created a huge buzz among viewers. Following the success of the series, the makers announced that its story would now be taken to the big screen. The film’s trailer has also been released. Ali Fazal, who plays Guddu Pandit, Divyendu, who portrays Munna Bhaiya, and Jitendra Kumar, who plays the new Bablu, interacted with the media in Lucknow. They spoke about the journey of ‘Mirzapur’ from a web series to a feature film and the changes audiences can expect in the story. Ravi Kishan to play an important role Ali Fazal said the world of ‘Mirzapur’ is now moving from the series to the big screen. He said the film will offer a bigger spectacle, a more expansive world and higher stakes than ever before. ‘Mirzapur: The Movie’ will take the story forward from the series and bring several popular and iconic characters together once again, including Kaleen Bhaiya, Munna Bhaiya and Guddu Pandit. Meanwhile, Bablu Pandit will return in a transformed avatar. Actor Ravi Kishan will also feature in an important role in the film. 'Film to release on 4 September' Ali Fazal said that the film will release in cinemas on 4th September. We are all very excited about it. The Mirzapur web series has received so much love that there was a lot of pressure on us regarding this film. We started the film promotion from Lucknow; this is our home. Every single thing about this city is very lovely. Whenever we come with our friends, we roam around the streets here and try different foods. Film different from web series Divyendu (Munna Bhaiya) said that the film will have the same tadka (flavor) as the web series. A lot of new things have been tried in it; the audience will not get bored anywhere. Divyendu said that we are the heroes of Hindi films; we people are immortal. Strong dialogues and powerful characters will be seen on screen. I assure my audience that they will enjoy this film as much as they enjoyed the Mirzapur series. Jitendra Kumar in the role of Bablu Pandit Actor Jitendra Kumar is playing this role in the film in place of Vikrant Massey, who played the character of Bablu Pandit in the web series. Earlier, the makers had also released new posters of the film. These showed the amazing looks of Kaleen Bhaiya (Pankaj Tripathi), Munna Bhaiya (Divyendu), Guddu Pandit (Ali Fazal) and Bablu Pandit (Jitendra Kumar). Big starcast will be seen, with Ravi Kishan The film includes a large star cast in addition to the main characters. It features Ravi Kishan, Abhishek Banerjee, Rasika Dugal, Mohit Malik, Sheeba Chaddha, Rajesh Tailang, Pramod Pathak, Shriya Pilgaonkar, Harshita Shekhar Gaur, Shweta Tripathi, Sonal S. Chauhan, Anangsha Biswas, Shaji Chaudhary, Satyendra Soni, Kulbhushan Kharbanda, and Sushant Singh. The film has been written by Puneet Krishna, while Ritesh Sidhwani and Farhan Akhtar (Excel Entertainment) have produced it.

stories.title: Foreign sex racket operator arrested:Evaded police for a year; underwent 7 surgeries to look younger at 50
stories.summary: Lola Kayumova (50), a woman from Uzbekistan accused of running a sex racket in Lucknow, has been arrested after evading the police for a year. She was caught during a raid at the Omex R-2 building on Tuesday night (August 11). Police later handed her over to intelligence agencies. Last year, Lucknow police arrested two young women allegedly linked to her racket. Both were from Uzbekistan. During interrogation, they revealed Lola’s name, following which she went underground. The investigation found that Lola had undergone plastic surgery seven times on her face, lips, underarms, and private parts to maintain a youthful appearance. All the procedures were reportedly performed by Lucknow-based Dr. Vivek Gupta. Now, sequentially understand the entire case- On 21 June, 2025, police received information about a sex racket operating in Omex Hazratganj Apartment in Lucknow. In the raid, Holida and Nilofer from Uzbekistan were arrested. Both were staying here illegally. Police investigation revealed that the flat belonged to Dr. Vivek Gupta. Lola had brought these two young women to India. Holida and Nilofer told during interrogation that, through Lola Kayumova, they met Dr. Vivek Gupta, who runs Minerva Clinic in Patrakarpuram and Ahimamau. Dr. Vivek Gupta had performed plastic surgery on both of them. Base in Lucknow, service up to Delhi According to police sources, Lola had made her passport in September 2013 to come to India. Police investigation revealed that Lola and Dr. Vivek had met in Thailand. After that, Vivek brought Lola to India. Initially, she established a base in Delhi-NCR. There, she got connected to a sex racket through agents. After this, she met alleged journalist Trijin, a resident of Varenam, Kerala, in Lucknow. She came to Lucknow in 2014. With Trijin's help, she started working at a spa center. After that, she started living with Trijin in a live-in relationship at flat number 104 in Omex R-1. Gradually, she built her own sex racket. During this time, Lola realized that there was a demand for foreign young women in India. She made this the method of her racket. She started calling young women to India and involving them in her sex racket. She contacted young women from Uzbekistan and lured them with the promise of earning good money in India. Her racket operated from Lucknow to Delhi. She would send girls to spa centers, hotels, and flats in Lucknow and Delhi-NCR. Lola took commission from the girls associated with the racket. She made huge earnings from this. With this money, she had purchased flat number 1103 in Omex R-1. Dr. Vivek used to perform plastic surgery on girls associated with the racket According to the police, Dr. Vivek had also become an active member of the racket. He used to perform plastic surgery on girls associated with the racket, so that their look would appear Russian-like and they would look younger. DCP South Mohammad Mustak said- This case related to foreign women is about a year old. After the arrest of Lola Kayumova, it will help reveal how many people are connected to this syndicate.

stories.title: Gorakhpur BJP leader’s body kept for 17 hours:Family demands FIR against doctor before cremation
stories.summary: The body of a BJP leader has been kept at his home in Gorakhpur for 17 hours as his family refuses to perform the last rites until an FIR is registered against the doctor and hospital staff over alleged medical negligence. Rakesh Yadav, a BJP booth president from Semra village in the Chiluatal area, died during treatment at Shahi Global Hospital in Gorakhpur. His family staged a protest outside the hospital on Tuesday morning, alleging negligence by the doctor and hospital staff. Police and administrative officials reached the spot and assured the family of action. The protest ended after around two hours, following which police sent the body for a post-mortem. After the post-mortem, the body was brought to Rakesh's home in Semra village at around 5 pm. However, the family refused to perform the last rites until their demands were met. Officials continued trying to convince them, but they remained firm. Family demands FIR, financial assistance Rakesh's wife, Lakshmi Yadav, submitted a memorandum to the administrative officials, alleging that her husband died due to negligence by doctors and staff at Shahi Global Hospital. She demanded an FIR against those responsible and financial assistance for the family. She said she had been left with two children and no source of support. The family has also sought arrangements for the children's education and a monthly government assistance of ₹20,000 to help them meet their expenses. Family alleges treatment was delayed Rakesh's brother-in-law, Janardan Yadav, said the 35-year-old was admitted to Shahi Global Hospital on August 4 for an appendix operation. The family alleged that he was discharged against their wishes on August 6. When he developed severe pain at night, they took him back to the hospital. According to the family, the doctors failed to identify his condition and proper treatment was not provided. On August 10, tests showed that his condition had become more serious. At around 8 pm, Rakesh was placed in an ambulance to be taken to Lucknow for further treatment. However, he died inside the ambulance. The family then brought his body back and sat outside the hospital. On Tuesday morning, villagers reached the hospital and placed the body on the road, demanding action against those responsible. Police later took the body for a post-mortem and asked the family to submit a written complaint. Officials said further action would be taken after an investigation. Rakesh was the family's sole breadwinner Rakesh had been married for around 10 years and had a son and a daughter. He worked as a labourer to support his family, while his elder brothers live outside the area. His wife has been inconsolable since his death. The family continued to refuse the last rites on Wednesday morning, while officials resumed efforts to persuade them to end the protest.

stories.title: Ram Mandir CEO interviews continue for second day:11 candidates asked if they keep a 'Shikha' and wear 'Janeu'
stories.summary: The second day of interviews for the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) post at Ayodhya's Ram Mandir began on Wednesday, with 11 candidates called to appear. The interviews started at 11.30 am in the Green House within the temple complex and will continue until 6 pm. Candidates asked about faith and religious practices According to sources, each candidate is being interviewed for 40 to 50 minutes, covering questions on administrative experience, responsibilities, work in the religious sector, and their devotion to Lord Ram. Sources said candidates are being asked whether they keep a shikha (tuft of hair), wear a janeu (sacred thread), are strictly vegetarian or non-vegetarian, drink alcohol, and whether they consider themselves devout Hindus or ordinary believers. They are also being asked whether they are comfortable dressing according to Hindu religious traditions. Eight candidates interviewed on first day The interview process will run over four days and cover 18 candidates in total, from which three names will be finalised. These three will then be interviewed by the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, which will select one final candidate. More than 5,300 people had applied for the CEO post, but only 18 were shortlisted. The panel includes retired Justice Pramod Kohli, former scientist Dr Suresh Hawde and retired Lieutenant General Vishnu Kant Chaturvedi. On the first day, Tuesday, eight former officials were interviewed, including three former IAS officers, one former IPS officer and four former military officers. Among them were former IPS officer Rajesh Pandey, known as an encounter specialist with the UP Police, and Dinesh Chandra, former district magistrate of Jaunpur. Tuesday's interviews ran from 11.30 am to 2 pm. Over 5,300 applied, screened through 34 questions Following the Ram Mandir donation theft case, the Trust had invited applications for the CEO post between 13 and 18 July. Applicants were required to answer 34 questions via an online Google form. Based on these responses, the team screened 5,300 applications, of which 18 candidates were found eligible and subsequently called for interviews. Key eligibility conditions for applicants Applicants asked if they are devout or strict Hindus The Google form asked applicants for personal details including name, date of birth, age, address, city, state, pin code, mobile number, and email. It also included questions to assess their command of Hindi and English, along with details of their highest educational qualification and current or most recent employment. Applicants were asked how many employees they had led, with options ranging from 1,000 to 5,000 or more. They were also asked whether they had previously been associated with any social or religious organisation, monastery or temple, and if so, for how long. Additionally, applicants had to state whether they identified as a strict Hindu or a devout Hindu, and were asked to share their vision, action plan, and suggestions for the Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra.

stories.title: Man stabs married lover 17 times after she refuses marriage:Kills her, sits beside body
stories.summary: A 42-year-old man murdered his 38-year-old lover in Bulandshahr. According to police, the accused stabbed the woman 17 times in the chest, neck and face. When police arrived, he was found sitting quietly beside her body. Police investigation revealed that the accused had been pressuring his married lover to marry him, but she had refused. On Tuesday night at 10 pm, he called her to his home and pressed her to leave her family and marry him. When she refused, he flew into a rage and carried out the attack. The two had been in a relationship for around one and a half years. The accused's wife had left him three years earlier. The deceased woman had four children, and her husband runs a small utensil-making factory. The incident took place in the Khurja Nagar Kotwali area, around 25 km from the district headquarters. 2 pictures of the incident Lover lived 200 metres from her home The victim, identified as Baby, originally from Prem Nagar in Delhi, had married Pankaj of Bulandshahr 15 years ago. The couple had two sons and two daughters, aged between 8 and 13. The family lived in Shivlok Colony. The accused, Ajit Thekedar (42), lived in a rented room around 200 metres from their home. Originally from Nehrupur village, he worked at a utensil-making factory in Khurja. Police said Ajit's wife had left him, and his son no longer lived with him, leaving him isolated. He began growing close to Baby, often following her and trying to strike up conversation. Over time, the two began talking regularly, became friends, and eventually started a relationship. Baby began visiting his room frequently. Woman cut off contact after he pressed for marriage According to police, Ajit wanted to marry Baby, but she was unwilling. She gradually began distancing herself from him, stopping phone calls and meetings. Angered by this, Ajit allegedly planned the murder. Neighbours said they heard noise coming from Ajit's room on Tuesday night and alerted the police. When officers arrived and forced the door open, they found Baby's body on the floor, with Ajit sitting beside her and blood spread across the floor. Police rushed her to hospital, but she died on the way. Husband learnt of the incident after returning from work Baby's husband, Pankaj, alias Bhante, said he had gone to work on Tuesday and returned home at 11.30 pm to find his wife missing. His children told him she had gone to "Ajit uncle's" house. When he reached there, he learnt that Ajit had stabbed his wife to death. He has appealed to police to take the strictest possible action against the accused. Police confirm 17 stab wounds Station in-charge Ramphal Singh said the woman's body bore 17 stab wounds. Questioning of local residents revealed the two were in a relationship, and that the accused had been pressuring her to marry him. The body has been sent for post-mortem, and further action will be taken based on the husband's statement.

stories.title: Atiq Ahmed's son Abaan's car crash video surfaces:Car lost balance while overtaking, hit divider, flung 10 ft into air
stories.summary: A video has surfaced showing the accident involving Abaan, son of gangster-turned-politician Atiq Ahmed. It shows a speeding Creta car losing control after overtaking a pickup truck and crashing into a road divider. The impact was so severe that the car flew nearly 10 feet into the air. Footage recorded by dashcam of car behind The video was captured on the dashcam of a car travelling behind Abaan's vehicle. The accident took place on 6 August in the Poonchh police station area, around 70 km before Jhansi. Abaan and his friend Sonu died in the crash. Abaan had been on his way to Jhansi jail to meet his brother Ali. A Dainik Bhaskar reporter, Sonu, confirmed that the location shown in the video matched the accident site, noting a house visible nearby that corresponded to the actual scene. He had reached the spot soon after the accident and inspected it closely, which led him to conclude the footage was genuine. Internal injuries so severe that his mouth filled with blood Abaan was travelling from Prayagraj to Jhansi on the morning of Thursday, 6 August. Four friends were travelling with him in the Creta. Abaan was seated in the front passenger seat, with his friend Zaid driving and Sonu seated behind him. The car, travelling at around 120 km/h, struck the divider on the side where Abaan was sitting, which is why he suffered the most severe injuries. Both Abaan and Sonu died at the scene shortly after the collision. Eyewitness Deepak Yadav, the first person to reach the spot, said he ran towards the scene after hearing a loud noise and found the occupants in agony. He tried to open the car door, but it would not budge, so he fetched an iron rod from a nearby house to break it open. He pulled out one young man first, who had internal injuries with blood filling his mouth. The man said, "My name is Abaan, save me," before losing consciousness and dying shortly afterwards. Impact ruptured Abaan's liver and lungs According to the post-mortem report, the force of the collision ruptured Abaan's liver, lungs and spleen, and broke his ribs. He died from severe internal bleeding. Sonu, who was seated behind Abaan, died from a fractured skull.

stories.title: Teacher beaten to death in Lalitpur:Wife learns of husband’s death 12 hours later, while six-year-old daughter remains traumatised after witnessing attack
stories.summary: “My husband used to go to school to teach. They followed him as soon as he left. They covered his face and repeatedly hit him with sticks. They picked up my innocent daughter and threw her away. Since the incident, my child has gone into shock. She cannot speak and only keeps crying. My husband had been attacked twice before. I have two young daughters. Who will look after them now?” These are the words of the wife of a teacher who was allegedly beaten to death in Lalitpur. On Monday (10 August), 30-year-old teacher Abhay Lodhi was allegedly attacked in front of his six-year-old daughter in the Kachnonda police station area. His daughter was also injured in the assault. Abhay died while being taken to Gwalior for treatment. However, his wife and daughter were not told about his death for nearly 12 hours. When the body reached their village on Tuesday evening, his wife collapsed. First, see 2 pictures What happened? Abhay Lodhi, who lived in Jharkon village, taught at a private intermediate college. On 10 August, he was returning home on a scooter with his six-year-old daughter Bhagya Shri. According to the family, some men travelling in a pickup truck hit their scooter. Abhay and his daughter fell on the road. When he moved towards his daughter, the attackers allegedly began hitting him repeatedly with sticks and struck his head with a stone. When the girl started screaming, she was also allegedly beaten and thrown away, leaving her seriously injured. The attackers fled after people nearby started approaching the scene. Abhay and his daughter were taken to hospital. Given the seriousness of his condition, Abhay was first referred to Jhansi and then to Gwalior. He died on the night of 10 August before reaching Gwalior. His daughter was treated at the medical college in Lalitpur and was discharged on Tuesday evening. Daughter has stopped speaking after witnessing attack The family said Bhagya Shri was present when her father was brutally attacked. She has been in shock since the incident and is reportedly unable to speak or respond to questions. According to her family, she has only been crying. Abhay died during the night, but his wife Rajni, 27, and their daughter were not informed until Tuesday afternoon. They learnt about his death only after reaching their village with the body on Tuesday evening. Wife alleges long-running family dispute Rajni said her sister-in-law Manisha married Ramkumar, a resident of Serai, in 2022. After their marriage, the couple lived with Abhay and his family. She alleged that Ramkumar did not work and was addicted to alcohol, leading to frequent arguments between the couple. On 10 April 2023, Ramkumar allegedly assaulted Manisha and then left home. He later died by suicide after jumping into a well, according to the family. The family said they learnt about his death from villagers. ‘His brothers accused us of murder’ Rajni alleged that Ramkumar’s brothers, Devendra and Rajesh, accused her and Abhay of killing him and disposing of his body. An FIR was registered, but the investigation concluded that Ramkumar had died by suicide, the family said. Rajni alleged that the dispute continued after that and that Abhay had already been attacked twice. “Devendra and Rajesh carried out this attack with their associates,” she alleged. ‘Who will look after my two daughters?’ Rajni said her elder daughter had been going to school with her father for the past two years. “I have two young daughters. Who will look after them now? They did not spare my child either. They beat her brutally and threw her away. Since the incident, my daughter has not been able to speak. She does not respond to anything and only cries,” she said. “My only demand is that my husband’s killers should be punished.” Brother alleges two earlier attempts to run Abhay over Abhay’s elder brother Son Singh said the family had two brothers and two sisters. He alleged that Manisha’s in-laws had been troubling their family since her marriage. After Ramkumar’s death, his family allegedly filed a false case against them, accusing them of murder. Son Singh and his father Magan Singh were also jailed in connection with the case, he said. Son Singh further alleged that there had been two earlier attempts to run Abhay over with a pickup truck, but he escaped both times. “This time, they hit him with the pickup, then beat him and struck his head with a stone,” he alleged. Abhay’s brother-in-law Kehar Singh has filed a case against Tulsi, Chandan, Mor Singh, Manohar, Rajesh, Devendra and some unidentified people. Police say investigation is underway CO Sadar Ajay Kumar said police received information on 10 August that a man named Abhay Singh had been assaulted. “Abhay Singh died during treatment. The investigation found that both sides are related and that members of his brother-in-law’s family had assaulted him. Kotwali police have registered a case and further action is underway,” he said.

stories.title: UP’s ‘Hanuman Rath’ runs on water and land:Costs ₹3 crore, has night-vision cameras; to be used in floods for first time
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh has deployed the SHERP rescue vehicle to save people trapped in floods for the first time. Equipped with a host of features, the vehicle can rotate a full 360 degrees, reach speeds of 40 kilometres per hour on land, and travel at 5 kilometres per hour on water. It can operate continuously for 40 hours, rescuing stranded flood victims and transporting them to safety. The vehicle has been designed to carry eight to nine people to safety in a single trip. Costing around 3 crore rupees, it was donated to the Gonda district administration by BJP MLA Prateek Bhushan Singh. It has been named the "Hanuman Rath". Where boats get stuck, this vehicle can rescue SHERP is a specialised all-terrain rescue vehicle, built to operate in difficult terrain where ordinary vehicles, tractors and boats cannot function. During floods, boats can only travel through deep water and often get stuck in strong currents, water hyacinth or shallow water. Tractors and heavier vehicles, meanwhile, tend to sink into mud or deep water. The distinguishing feature of SHERP is its ability to move directly from land into water, and then from water into mud or marshland, without needing to stop when the terrain changes. No steering wheel — controlled by two levers The SHERP's control system is markedly different from that of ordinary cars and trucks. Rather than a conventional steering wheel, it is operated using two levers, much like a tank. By slowing or stopping the wheels on one side, the driver can turn the vehicle a full 360 degrees on the spot. Instead of a standard driveshaft, SHERP uses an oil-dipped chain drive system, which gives its large tyres greater grip. This allows the vehicle to move through mud, marshland and slippery clay with relative ease, reducing the likelihood of it becoming stuck. High-tech safety and surveillance systems During a disaster, reaching those trapped is only part of the task — keeping the rescue team safe and monitoring surrounding conditions matters just as much. SHERP is fitted with several safety features to support this. Specially trained operators Driving the SHERP is not as straightforward as driving an ordinary vehicle, and requires trained operators. Before the vehicle was handed over, lead operator Atulendra and his colleague underwent two weeks of specialised technical training in Chandigarh. Notably, the vehicle has been manufactured in India. It was built at a plant in Chandigarh through a partnership between the JSW Group and Archa Adventure, and is being presented as an example of the "Make in India" and "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiatives. Why it was named 'Hanuman Rath' The name carries particular significance in Gonda. According to belief, Lord Hanuman came forward to help people in times of crisis. In that same spirit, the vehicle is intended to reach those in need during floods — crossing water, mud and marshland to deliver relief and essential assistance when boats and other means fail. Flood-like conditions persist in Gonda, water levels near danger mark The Saryu river in Gonda flowed above the danger mark from 9 to 11 August, reaching 106.190 metres against a danger level of 106.070 metres — around 12 centimetres above the red mark. Near the Elgin Bridge in Karnailganj, the Ghaghra and Saryu rivers remain in spate. However, the river's water level dropped by 13 centimetres in the past 24 hours. On 11 August, 1,37,234 cusecs of water were released from Girja Barrage, 68,147 cusecs from Sharda Barrage, and 1,731 cusecs from Saryu Barrage, bringing a total of 2,07,112 cusecs into the river. According to the Gonda Flood Division, water levels in both the Ghaghra and Saryu rivers are steadily receding. However, the Saryu is causing rapid erosion in the Nawabganj area, which remains a source of concern. The district administration, health department and disaster relief teams are on standby to deal with any emergency, and weak embankments and vulnerable villages continue to be closely monitored.

stories.title: 31 houses swept into Ganga in Farrukhabad:Water enters homes in Meerut-Sambhal; flood alert in 16 districts, rain in 28 today
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is likely to receive rain in 28 districts on Wednesday, with heavy rain expected in Sonbhadra. On Tuesday, 10 cities, including Meerut, Sambhal, Bijnor and Muzaffarnagar, received heavy showers. Prayagraj also witnessed around 30 minutes of intense rain at about 11 pm. Water enters homes in Meerut, Sambhal Heavy rain turned streets and residential colonies in Meerut and Sambhal into pools of water. Water entered several homes and shops, reaching depths of up to one foot. In Muzaffarnagar, 2-3 feet of water accumulated along the Kanwar route and around Shiv Chowk. Amid the rain, District Magistrate Umesh Mishra and SSP Sanjay Verma stepped into knee-deep water to assess the situation. 31 houses washed away in Farrukhabad Heavy rain in the hills has pushed 10 rivers in Uttar Pradesh above danger levels, prompting a flood warning for 16 districts. In Farrukhabad, 31 houses have been swept away by the Ganga over the past eight days. Residents have been using boats to move their belongings to safer areas. Water reaches ghats in Varanasi, Mathura In Varanasi, water has submerged the steps of the ghats. The routes connecting all 84 ghats have also been inundated. In Mathura, the Yamuna has risen to the steps of the river ghats. According to the IMD's satellite imagery, only one pocket of cloud cover remains over Varanasi in eastern Uttar Pradesh. However, dense cloud cover persists across western Uttar Pradesh. Low-pressure area driving heavy rain Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said a low-pressure area extending up to the middle troposphere has formed over north-western Madhya Pradesh. The system is causing heavy rain in some parts of western Uttar Pradesh. However, the monsoon trough remains slightly south of its normal position. The trough extends from Bikaner through the centre of the low-pressure area, Siddhi, Ranchi and Digha towards the east-central Bay of Bengal. As a result, the decline in monsoon activity across most parts of eastern and central Uttar Pradesh is likely to continue until August 12.

stories.title: Will Akash calling rivals ‘uncles’ help BJP?:Why is his anti-UP govt push backfiring?
stories.summary: Mayawati’s nephew and Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) leader Akash Anand’s remarks calling Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi ‘uncles’ have sparked a political debate in Uttar Pradesh. Anand once again displayed the aggressive style seen during the 2024 Lok Sabha election campaign at a rally in Hathras on 10 August. Although he targeted the BJP and the Uttar Pradesh government most aggressively, political analysts believe his attacks could benefit the BJP more than the BSP. In today’s UP Explainer, we look at how Anand’s aggressive campaign against the BJP could end up helping the ruling party. Question 1: What did Akash Anand say in his speech? Answer: While referring to Akhilesh Yadav, Anand said: “Akhilesh uncle.” He explained that he was 30 years old while Akhilesh was around 50, so he would call him ‘uncle’ rather than ‘bhaiya’. When someone from the audience called Akhilesh ‘bhaiya’, Anand replied: “He is Akhilesh uncle.” He also attacked Akhilesh’s PDA formula — referring to the SP’s pitch of bringing together backward classes, Dalits and minorities. Anand questioned the meaning of the PDA formula and alleged that Akhilesh changed its meaning according to the political situation. Targeting Rahul Gandhi, Anand said the Congress leader carried a book and spoke about the Constitution. He claimed that if the book were opened, its pages would be found blank. Anand launched his strongest attack on the BJP government. He alleged that the Uttar Pradesh government had spent ₹7,000 crore over 10 years trying to hide its failures. He also referred to the deaths of newborn babies at a hospital in Jhansi and alleged that the government had little to offer apart from expressing regret. Anand claimed that the BJP government had shut more than 25,000 schools where children from Dalit communities studied. He also attacked the government over law and order, claiming that Uttar Pradesh had recorded the highest number of murders in 10 years. He alleged that more than 65,000 crimes against women, along with over 10,000 kidnapping and extortion cases, were reported every year. Anand questioned whether Uttar Pradesh had the rule of law or whether criminals were operating under police protection. Question 2: If Anand is attacking the BJP most aggressively, how can the BJP benefit? Answer: Political analysts believe that direct attacks can sometimes produce an outcome opposite to what the attacker intends. Anand’s attacks could divide the anti-BJP vote, particularly among young and Dalit voters who might otherwise support the SP-Congress alliance. This can be understood through four points. i) Anti-incumbency votes could split The equation: Voters unhappy with the BJP government over issues such as paper leaks and unemployment are likely to vote against the ruling party. Who stands to lose? Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal said that if the BSP remained inactive, a large part of the anti-BJP vote could have moved directly towards the SP-Congress alliance. How could BJP benefit? Anand is aggressively raising issues concerning young and Dalit voters while attacking the BJP. This could persuade some anti-BJP voters to support the BSP instead. That would divide the anti-BJP vote and could help the BJP retain seats that it might otherwise lose. ii) Anand could challenge the SP’s PDA formula The equation: In previous elections, the SP used its PDA formula to attract non-Jatav Dalits and a significant section of Muslim voters. Anand’s attack: At the Hathras rally, Anand directly targeted Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA narrative. He sought to project Mayawati and the BSP as the real political representatives of Dalits. How could BJP benefit? Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh said that if Anand succeeds in convincing Dalit voters, particularly young voters, that the SP cannot protect their interests, some of them could return to the BSP. It is difficult to say how many additional seats the BSP could win. However, the SP-Congress alliance could certainly lose votes. iii) A stronger BSP could help BJP retain close seats The equation: With Mayawati becoming less active, many contests in Uttar Pradesh had effectively become two-way fights between the BJP and the opposition. Anand’s return to active politics could turn some of these contests into triangular fights. The BJP’s core vote is considered relatively strong and consolidated. If the BSP brings back its traditional voters and attracts some young voters, it could split the opposition vote. This could help BJP candidates win closely fought seats where the winning margin is small. In the 2022 Assembly election, 43 seats were decided by margins of 5,000 votes or less. The BJP won 25 of these seats by fewer than 5,000 votes, while it lost 18 seats by a similar margin. iv) Anand’s attacks could weaken Rahul-Akhilesh’s political branding Suresh Bahadur Singh said Anand’s remarks about Rahul Gandhi’s ‘empty Constitution book’ and his description of Akhilesh Yadav as an ‘uncle’ and an opportunist challenged the image of the two leaders as the opposition’s ‘two boys’. If Anand succeeds in portraying the opposition’s biggest faces as old or ineffective, it could reinforce the perception that the BJP does not have a strong alternative. A decline in public confidence in the opposition could ultimately benefit the ruling party. Question 3: What should the BSP do to benefit itself rather than the BJP? Answer: The BSP will need to change its image before the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly election — from a party seen mainly as a ‘vote-cutter’ to one that voters believe can form the government. This can be understood through five points. i) Convince voters that the BSP is fighting to win What is the current situation? Ratanmani Lal said there is currently a perception that the BSP is contesting elections mainly to damage the SP or indirectly help the BJP. When voters believe a party is in third place, they often do not want to ‘waste’ their vote on it. What needs to change by 2027? The BSP will have to convince voters that it is not merely fighting to defeat the BJP or SP, but is seriously aiming to form a government with a full majority. If voters see the BSP as a genuine contender for power, some anti-BJP voters could shift towards it instead of the SP-Congress alliance. ii) Give young voters a clear jobs guarantee What is the current situation? Anand’s ‘uncle’ remarks have attracted the attention of young voters. However, converting that attention into votes will require concrete promises and a credible policy agenda. Young voters are concerned about paper leaks, unemployment and delays in government recruitment. What needs to change by 2027? The BSP will need to present a clear employment policy and promise to fill vacant government posts quickly if it comes to power. A credible jobs guarantee could help the party attract young voters beyond caste and religious loyalties. iii) Keep Akash Anand on the front foot What is the current situation? There is uncertainty among voters over whether Anand will remain active or could again be sidelined by Mayawati. What needs to change by 2027? Suresh Bahadur Singh said Mayawati would need to publicly declare that Anand will lead the party’s 2027 election campaign and represent its political future. Giving Anand clear authority could strengthen confidence among voters and party workers. A strong young leader with clear decision-making powers could help consolidate support among younger voters. iv) Build a broad social coalition What is the current situation? The BSP’s electoral position has weakened considerably in recent years. The party, which secured around 51% of the vote when it formed a majority government in 2007, received around 9% in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. Its traditional vote base has also faced competition from Chandrashekhar Azad. Non-Jatav Dalits and sections of other communities have shifted towards the BJP and SP. What needs to change by 2027? Ratanmani Lal said the BSP’s 2007 success came from bringing Dalits, Brahmins, backward classes and minorities together. The party will need to rebuild a similar broad-based social coalition. Leaders from different communities will need greater representation, while ticket distribution will also have to reflect the message that the BSP represents all sections. v) Consider alliances with smaller parties What is the current situation? The BSP risks being labelled a ‘vote-cutter’ when it contests elections alone. What needs to change by 2027? Alliances with influential regional parties could create the perception that the BSP is capable of forming the government or emerging as a kingmaker. An alliance with leaders and parties such as Pallavi Patel, Asaduddin Owaisi and the Mahan Dal could alter caste and religious equations across several constituencies. Muslim and Dalit voters influence the outcome in dozens of Uttar Pradesh seats. An alliance between the BSP and Owaisi could potentially divide the SP’s core Muslim support. Pallavi Patel’s Kurmi base and the Mahan Dal’s influence among Maurya and other non-Yadav OBC voters could also affect the traditional support bases of both the SP and BJP. However, such alliances are likely to work only if the BSP appears capable of forming the government. So, what is the larger political challenge for the BSP? If the BSP contests the 2027 election mainly on the strength of aggressive campaigning, it could divide the opposition vote and indirectly help the BJP. But if the party succeeds in presenting itself as a credible alternative to both the BJP and the SP-Congress alliance, voters currently supporting the SP could shift towards the BSP. For Akash Anand, therefore, the challenge is not simply to attack the BJP more aggressively. It is to convince voters that the BSP itself can win.

stories.title: 'Being called a rapist more painful than being shot':Brij Bhushan speaks after acquittal in wrestlers' sexual harassment case
stories.summary: The way I was called a rapist, it would have been better if they had just shot me. It wouldn't have been so painful then. Saying this, the former president of the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI), Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, became emotional while speaking on his acquittal in the wrestlers' sexual harassment case. On 3 August, the Rouse Avenue Court in Delhi acquitted him in the sexual harassment case of women wrestlers. In an exclusive interview with 'Dainik Bhaskar', Brijbhushan Singh spoke openly about his future political strategy, the allegations made by women wrestlers, and his testimony in court. He said, "It's difficult to fight such allegations. I was broken. The children who were lured into preparing for the case later exposed the truth themselves." Read Brijbhushan Singh's full interview… Two women wrestlers retracted their allegations in court, did this prove helpful? Brijbhushan: Yes, it helped a lot, because she herself was a victim. All the victims were from different places. But everyone's address somehow connects to one place. Everyone's address was Bajrang Punia's residence, Sonipat. The judge also asked why everyone's address was Sonipat? How many people live in one flat? They had no answer. Actually, lawyers used to sit at Bajrang Punia's residence, judges used to sit. They were trained, their statements were taken. All these things were presented before the judge and the court by two of those victims, who are players. You were called a rapist, politicians also targeted you by name? Brijbhushan: Look, this accusation that was made against me... (gets emotional). Karan Bhushan's (Brijbhushan's son) statement just came out, you must have seen it. How broken he was. We were also broken, but now that things have come to light, we had to fight them. I fought and today I have emerged spotless. But the way I was called a rapist, that was painful. A boastful MP (Chandrashekhar Azad) used to say that he would drag me from Bishnoharpur (Brijbhushan's village). Fortunately, the Khap Panchayat (Haryana) did not give the order, otherwise, the poor fellow would have dragged me away. So many big-mouthed people had come forward. Now someone should ask them if they will drag me or not. When you were acquitted by the court, 'Dabdaba Hai' (It's Dominance) posters were put up in Gonda, is that correct? Brijbhushan: It's not dominance... I studied in Gorakhpur. When I came to Ayodhya, I did student union politics. For 55 years, I have never turned away from the public and their problems. That was the result that people from all over the state came to meet me in two days. This is not dominance. This is my influence. Do you wish to go to Parliament again? Brijbhushan: Whatever I claim in politics, there is a sentiment behind it. I was removed, removed through a conspiracy. Therefore, I have a desire that the house from which I came, in a way, disgraced, I should go back to that house once with a clean slate. This is my wish. Now, whatever the rest of the party wishes, it will do. When the allegations were made, you were an MP from Kaiserganj. Will you contest the election from there again? Brijbhushan: Nothing is impossible in politics. If I have to contest the election, the party will decide. What is Mahadev Academy, who do you hold responsible behind the allegations? Brijbhushan: The masterminds, founders, and collaborators of the academy are Bhupinder and his son Deepender Hooda. No child was being prepared, so the guardian of each child was called and lured. Someone was promised to be made Deputy SP and someone was promised to be made Inspector. They were also given money. Later, the children realized that they were being fooled, and then some of these children exposed them. There are 50 wrestling academies (akhadas) in Haryana, but no child from any other akhada came. One family and one akhada. There were 44 people in the case, some came and some backed out? Brijbhushan: Still, 32 witnesses came. Dates were set for about 127 days. I did not submit an application on any date, saying I couldn't come. I was present on almost every date, and on one or two dates, I was present via video calling. Neither our lawyer nor we took a single opportunity. They took six-month opportunities. The main conspirators took dates. Even after at least three-four notices, they came and then made an excuse, saying they couldn't come for two months. The court heard their case with great patience. Because they wanted the case to drag on for a very long time, they knew the truth that this case would not stand in court, so they wanted to prolong it. Accusations were made against you, but the sports world was defamed? Brijbhushan: Although the accusation was against me, it was also against the world of sports. The incident was reported from India, but its impact was worldwide. Parents of every female wrestler, no matter which country they belonged to, were terrified because Olympic medal winners were calling themselves victims. A World Champion and a woman who was number one in the world was calling herself a victim. This created a tense atmosphere for female athletes and their families worldwide. After the judgment came, everything became clear. I stood by my word from day one, and today that word has proven true.

stories.title: Home Ministry seeks report on firing at Varanasi airport:Probe to be completed in a week, action against those responsible for security lapse
stories.summary: On the morning of August 16, two employees were injured when a pistol accidentally discharged while being checked at Varanasi's Lal Bahadur Shastri International Airport. The incident is being treated as a major security lapse. The Ministry of Home Affairs has now sought a detailed report on the matter. Central agencies are also investigating the incident. The report is expected to be prepared within a week and will identify those responsible for the security lapse. Further action against the officials concerned may then be decided. Shiv Sena leader detained after pistol goes off On August 16, Shiv Sena leader Kamlesh Rai, a resident of Azamgarh, arrived at the airport with his wife. During the security check, his pistol accidentally discharged, injuring two airport employees. The incident caused panic at the airport. Security agencies detained Kamlesh and later handed him over to the police. Following the intervention of the Ministry of Home Affairs, a detailed investigation is now under way. Everyone questioned separately, CCTV footage scrutinised Airport Director Puneet Gupta said investigating agencies were present at the airport the day after the incident. Airline officials, Airport Authority employees, those involved in the incident and security personnel were questioned separately. CCTV footage of the incident and the surrounding security process was also scrutinised. The biggest question being examined is how the passenger's licensed pistol was allowed to reach the point where it was being handled inside the airport despite the initial security checks. Security rules allegedly not followed while checking pistol According to the airport director, prescribed safety standards were not followed while the weapon was being handled. CCTV footage reportedly shows that, under the rules, the security personnel was supposed to check the pistol. Instead, Kamlesh himself took out the weapon and began checking it. Airport officials say private security personnel can sometimes come under pressure from influential individuals and may hesitate to enforce security protocols strictly. This has raised further questions about the security arrangements at the airport. What happened on the day of the incident? At around 9.30 am on August 16, Kamlesh Rai, an Azamgarh resident and Shiv Sena leader in Mumbai, was travelling to Mumbai with his wife on Air India Express flight IX-1810 from Varanasi airport. He had already declared the pistol he was carrying before boarding the aircraft. During the weapon inspection, a bullet entered the chamber. As the trigger was pressed, the pistol discharged. After receiving information from the Airport Authority, police reached the spot. They found a pistol and 21 cartridges in Kamlesh's possession. He was questioned for around five hours before Phulpur police took him to the police station. Bullet injures two airport employees The bullet initially struck the floor before hitting the thigh of Suman (32), a female employee from Gaya, Bihar, who was standing nearby. Bullet fragments then struck Rohit Raj's hand. Both employees were injured and covered in blood. They were immediately taken to hospital for treatment. Kamlesh is former Mumbai corporator Kamlesh Rai, who is from Azamgarh, is a Shiv Sena leader and former corporator in Mumbai. His social media profiles contain photographs with Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde and Dhananjay Singh. Airport was on high alert during Independence Day period Puneet Gupta, Director of Varanasi airport at Babatpur, said the airport authorities had been informed in advance that Kamlesh would be travelling with a pistol. The airport had been declared a high-alert zone from August 11 to 20 because of the Independence Day security arrangements. The incident has therefore raised questions not only about the handling of the weapon but also about the entire security process, the conduct of the personnel involved and the effectiveness of the investigation itself.

stories.title: Rain in 15 cities including Lucknow, schools shut in 7:Ratneshwar and Brahmeshwar Mahadev temples 70% submerged in Varanasi; alert in 75 districts
stories.summary: The monsoon spell continues across Uttar Pradesh. Intermittent rain has been falling in 15 cities, including Lucknow, Barabanki and Saharanpur, since 3 am on Tuesday. Dense, dark clouds have kept the skies gloomy, making it appear dark even in the morning. Schools in Prayagraj, Mirzapur, Kaushambi, Bhadohi, Hardoi, Amethi and Jaunpur have been closed today. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of the state. 3-4 feet of water fills Prayagraj colonies After heavy rain on Monday, colonies and lanes in Prayagraj's Kareli area were inundated with 3-4 feet of water. Cars and motorcycles were submerged. Police and NDRF teams rescued residents from the affected areas and moved them to safer locations. Meanwhile, more than 10 rivers, including the Ganga and Yamuna, are in spate across UP. More than 100 temples near Varanasi ghats submerged Water has entered more than 100 small temples located along the ghats in Varanasi. The Ratneshwar Mahadev Temple at Manikarnika Ghat and the Brahmeshwar Mahadev Temple at Dashashwamedh Ghat are around 70% submerged. Only their domes remain visible above the water. 500+ homes flooded in Kanpur and Unnao Areas along the Ganga in Kanpur and Unnao have been inundated, with water entering more than 500 homes. Residents have been forced to stay on rooftops. In Chitrakoot, rising water levels in the Mandakini and Bardaha rivers have submerged the steps at Ramghat. 10-metre-wide crater opens on Ganga Expressway On Monday, 65 cities, including Ghaziabad, Kanpur and Varanasi, received rainfall. In Unnao, a deep crater around 10 metres wide opened near milestone 421 on the Ganga Expressway at Sonik, on the Meerut-Prayagraj carriageway. The ground near the side railing also subsided. See pictures of rain- Rain to intensify from August 19 According to Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh- The monsoon has become active due to the formation of a low-pressure area, the northward shift of the monsoon trough and moisture coming from the Bay of Bengal. Monsoon activity is expected to intensify further between August 19 and 23. The rain spell will continue under the influence of the low-pressure system developing over the Bay of Bengal. Heavy rain is likely on August 20 and 21.

stories.title: Farmer's neck cut by Chinese kite string in Gorakhpur:7 stitches after string catches him while riding to buy vegetables
stories.summary: A farmer riding a motorcycle in Nausad, under the Gida police station area of Gorakhpur, suffered a deep cut to his neck after getting entangled in Chinese kite string on Monday evening . Blood began gushing from his neck following the accident. Despite the injury, the farmer managed to remove his T-shirt and tie it around his neck to control the bleeding. He then somehow reached a doctor at a nearby intersection, where he received seven stitches. Now know the full story Rampratap Nishad (55), a farmer from Nausad, was riding his bike to Haraiya market to buy vegetables at around 6.30 pm on Monday. While he was on his way, a Chinese kite string suddenly became entangled around his neck. The sharp string cut into his neck, causing him to fall from his motorcycle. Tied T-shirt around neck to stop bleeding Rampratap said that blood started gushing from his neck immediately after the accident. He quickly removed his T-shirt and tied it around his neck in an attempt to stop the bleeding. Despite his injury, he somehow managed to reach a doctor at the nearby intersection for treatment. Doctor puts seven stitches After examining Rampratap, the doctor treated the wound and put seven stitches on the cut area. His condition was subsequently reported to be stable. The incident has increased concern among local residents over the continued use of Chinese manjha. People have demanded an effective ban on the sale and use of the prohibited kite string.
