stories.title: MLA’s ‘conman’ son-in-law duped 44 women:Targeted divorced, widowed women; posed as his son’s brother before marriage
stories.summary: A father-son duo from Sitapur allegedly conned 44 women of around ₹100 crore after marrying them or promising to marry them, according to police complaints and statements by victims. Anuj Trivedi and his son Prakhar allegedly targeted mostly women over 40, including widows, divorcees and women with disabilities. To gain their trust, Anuj allegedly introduced Prakhar as his younger brother. The case came to light after BJP MLA from Sevta in Sitapur, Gyan Tiwari, filed an FIR against his son-in-law Prakhar and his father Anuj. The MLA alleged that his MBBS-qualified daughter was also a victim of the alleged fraud. How the alleged ‘groom gang’ came to light Anuj and Prakhar, residents of Chandrawal village in Sitapur, allegedly carried out the fraud between 2016 and 2022 across Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Delhi, Kolkata and Karnataka. The case first came to light on March 4, 2022, when 75-year-old Sarita (name changed) filed a complaint at Nayanagar police station in Thane. She said she had placed a newspaper matrimonial for her 45-year-old daughter Shubhangi, who was Manglik. Anuj allegedly contacted her using the name ‘Ajay Agarwal’ and claimed to be a builder from Kolkata. Shubhangi married him on March 1, 2019. According to Sarita, Anuj took Shubhangi to Delhi on February 22, 2022, where he allegedly removed her 39 tolas of gold and diamond jewellery. He then put her on a train to Mumbai and switched off his phone. Complaints from Ranjita (name changed) in Amravati and Leela Pratap Nair in Mumbai later emerged. After four FIRs were registered in Maharashtra, the investigation was handed over to the Mumbai Crime Branch. Seven women describe how they were allegedly trapped Anuj allegedly arranged four marriages for Prakhar in Mumbai and cheated the women of crores of rupees. On February 14, 2024, Prakhar married Pragya Tiwari, daughter of BJP MLA Gyan Tiwari from Sevta. Pragya is an MBBS doctor and the couple also have a son. After the family allegedly discovered the truth about Anuj and Prakhar, Gyan Tiwari and his daughter cut ties with them. On August 8, the MLA filed an FIR against both men. 1. Pragya: ‘Prakhar approached me at the gym’ Prakhar allegedly targeted Pragya at the gym she attended. He started visiting the same gym and, according to her family, used an expensive car to create an impression of wealth. He gradually became acquainted with Pragya and later proposed marriage. Pragya told her father about the proposal. Gyan Tiwari said he made enquiries about the family and was told that they were well-established and ran a real-estate business in Mumbai. Anuj had allegedly built a similar reputation in his village. He had opened a school in Prakhar’s name and built a roughly 6,000-square-foot house in Krishna Vihar, near Chhath Mile on the Sitapur Road. 2. Shubhangi: 455 grams of jewellery allegedly taken Shubhangi's mother Sarita had placed a matrimonial in 2018 because her daughter was Manglik and was finding it difficult to get married. Anuj allegedly responded using the name Ajay Agarwal and claimed to be a Kolkata-based builder. He later married Shubhangi and stayed in her three-bedroom flat during the Covid period. He allegedly assaulted her and pressured her family into selling the flat. According to the complaint, he took ₹82 lakh, including the proceeds from the sale. On February 22, he allegedly took Shubhangi to Delhi on the pretext of attending the wedding of his ‘younger brother’ Prakhar. There, he allegedly removed 455 grams of gold jewellery she was wearing. Shubhangi reportedly had a serious leg injury at the time. Her family alleged that she was kept without food before being put on a train to Mumbai. Her family is now facing financial difficulties. Her 82-year-old father still has to work in a private job, according to the family. 3. Pratima: Teacher allegedly loses ₹11 lakh and jewellery Pratima (name changed), a teacher from Jhunsi in Prayagraj, also came into contact with Anuj. She alleged that he took ₹11 lakh and 50 grams of jewellery from her. Pratima said she first met him in 2017. 4. Geeta: Fake marriage certificate allegedly used Geeta, a divorcee, created a profile on a matrimonial website at her mother's suggestion. Anuj allegedly contacted her in 2017 using the name Ajay Agarwal. He introduced his son Prakhar as his younger brother, ‘Aviral’. He later gave Geeta a marriage certificate dated August 27, 2018. She subsequently discovered that the certificate was allegedly fake. After the marriage, Anuj allegedly took ₹25.90 lakh and 400 grams of gold jewellery from Geeta, claiming he needed the money to complete a building project in Kolkata. He also allegedly pressured her to sell a house worth ₹35 lakh for just ₹9 lakh. Geeta became suspicious after she saw another woman, Vinita, in a mirror during a video call with Anuj. She later went to Bandra court to verify the marriage documents and allegedly discovered that the certificate was fake. She subsequently filed an FIR at Amravati police station. 5. Rachna: Anuj allegedly claimed his wife had died Rachna's husband died of cancer in 2012. She placed a matrimonial in 2016 and came into contact with Anuj. He allegedly claimed to be a widower and said his wife, Maya Singh, had died of cancer. Rachna alleged that he took ₹8 lakh, a mobile phone, a diamond ring and a gold chain from her. She later became suspicious and travelled to Mumbai in September 2018. An investigation allegedly revealed that Maya Singh was alive and that Anuj had sold her flat and taken her to Lucknow. When Rachna threatened to approach the police, Anuj allegedly threatened to circulate her photographs. Maharashtra Police recently recorded her statement. 6. Leela Nair: ₹54 lakh flat sale and 950 grams of gold Leela Nair lived alone in Mumbai while her children were settled abroad. Anuj allegedly came into contact with her in 2015-16 and gradually gained her trust. He eventually became her caretaker. Claiming to be a prominent Mumbai builder, he allegedly arranged the sale of her flat for ₹54 lakh and kept the entire amount. He also allegedly took 950 grams of her gold jewellery before disappearing. Leela later filed a case against him at Borivali police station. 7. Mahua: Engagement allegedly followed by fraud In 2016, Anuj allegedly approached a woman named Mahua in Kolkata with a marriage proposal. The two became engaged. He allegedly took money and jewellery from her before fleeing. Mahua and around 15 other women who were allegedly targeted have since married elsewhere and do not want to come forward because of concerns about social stigma. However, the Mumbai Crime Branch has so far recorded statements from 25 alleged victims. Investigation reveals alleged first wife was alive While checking Anuj's claims, Geeta reportedly went to his Bandra flat. The security guard allegedly recognised Anuj and told her that he had married a woman named Maya Singh in 2016. Maya, who reportedly weighed around 150 kg and used a wheelchair, allegedly had her Bandra flat sold by Anuj after their marriage. The property was reportedly sold for ₹2.82 crore. Anuj then allegedly took Maya to Lucknow and kept her in a house in Gomti Nagar. Father arrested, son still missing The Mumbai Crime Branch arrested Anuj in Noida on May 24, 2026. During questioning, he allegedly admitted to marrying around 40 women across several states. Police said his son Prakhar had also married four women in Mumbai and Kolkata. Prakhar is still being searched for. Anuj is currently lodged in Amravati Central Jail. Three FIRs have been registered against him in Maharashtra and one in Kolkata. On August 8, Sitapur BJP MLA Gyan Tiwari also filed an FIR against Anuj and Prakhar, alleging that his daughter was among their victims.

stories.title: Is making, selling analogue paneer not a crime in UP?:Gujarat, Maharashtra ban it; why is it still sold here, what are the rules?
stories.summary: Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra and Gujarat have recently banned the production and sale of analogue, or ‘fake’, paneer. However, making and selling it is not a criminal offence in Uttar Pradesh and several other states, provided consumers are clearly told that it is not made from milk. It is also different from adulterated paneer, which is made using harmful substances and sold as genuine milk-based paneer. So, why is making and selling analogue paneer not a crime in Uttar Pradesh? How is it different from adulterated paneer? What are the rules governing its sale? Here is everything you need to know. Q1. What is the difference between analogue and adulterated paneer? Answer: Analogue paneer is designed to resemble traditional milk-based paneer. It is generally made using ingredients such as milk powder, vegetable oil, potato or corn starch, soya protein and food additives. When made according to prescribed standards, it does not involve the use of harmful chemicals and is not banned in Uttar Pradesh. Adulterated paneer, on the other hand, may be made using substances such as detergent, urea and caustic chemicals. It is also sold by passing it off as genuine milk-based paneer. Such practices are illegal and are treated as a non-bailable offence in Uttar Pradesh. When analogue paneer is sold, the consumer must be clearly informed that it is not made from milk. It is also generally cheaper than conventional paneer. In simple terms, there are two categories: Q2. Is analogue paneer completely safe to eat? Answer: Not necessarily. Occasional consumption may not cause immediate problems, but concerns have been raised about the effects of consuming products high in unhealthy fats and additives regularly. 1. Risk of heart disease Analogue paneer may contain significant amounts of vegetable fats, including palm oil, to give it a texture similar to traditional paneer. A diet high in unhealthy fats can raise levels of bad cholesterol and triglycerides, increasing the risk of heart disease and other cardiovascular problems. 2. Liver and digestive problems Some analogue paneer products contain vegetable fats and large amounts of starch or other thickening agents. Regular consumption of foods high in unhealthy fats can contribute to weight gain and metabolic problems, while excessive starch intake may cause digestive discomfort such as bloating, gas and constipation in some people. 3. Concerns over long-term consumption Some products may also contain preservatives and other food additives to increase their shelf life. However, the health impact depends on the ingredients used, their quantities and how frequently the product is consumed. It is therefore misleading to assume that all analogue paneer products carry the same health risks. 4. Weight gain and lower nutritional value People who eat paneer as part of a weight-loss or fitness diet may not get the same nutritional benefits from an analogue product. Traditional paneer is a source of protein and calcium. Depending on how it is made, an analogue product may contain substantially less protein and calcium while containing more vegetable fat and carbohydrates. Q3. If it can be unhealthy, why is making and selling it not a crime? Answer: In Uttar Pradesh, the sale of analogue paneer that meets food-safety standards is not, by itself, prohibited. There are several legal and technical reasons for this. 1. Its ingredients are not illegal substances Food products can be banned when they contain substances that are unsafe for human consumption. However, ingredients commonly used in analogue paneer, such as vegetable oils, corn starch and skimmed milk powder, are permitted food ingredients when used within prescribed limits. Similar ingredients are also used in products such as biscuits, savoury snacks, chips and chocolates. Therefore, the use of these approved ingredients does not automatically make a food product illegal. 2. It is treated as a separate food category The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) does not necessarily treat every analogue product as adulterated food. Dairy analogues and non-dairy substitutes can fall under separate food categories. For example, margarine made from vegetable fat is sold as an alternative to butter. Similarly, analogue paneer can be sold as an alternative to traditional paneer, provided it meets the applicable food-safety and labelling requirements. The key requirement is that consumers must not be misled. An analogue product cannot simply be sold or labelled as traditional milk-based paneer. It must be identified appropriately as an analogue or non-dairy product. 3. It can serve as an alternative for some consumers Non-dairy alternatives can be used by people who avoid or cannot tolerate conventional dairy products. They may also be chosen by consumers following plant-based diets. This is one reason regulators focus on proper labelling and consumer information rather than automatically banning every non-dairy substitute. 4. The focus is on clear labelling The basic principle is that consumers should know what they are buying and be able to make an informed choice. Manufacturers and sellers cannot misrepresent an analogue product as genuine milk-based paneer. Where applicable, packaging must clearly identify the product as an analogue or non-dairy alternative. Restaurants and hotels using such products are also expected to inform customers rather than presenting them as conventional paneer or cheese. Q4. Then why have Maharashtra and Gujarat banned it? Answer: The FSSAI is the central authority responsible for setting food-safety standards across the country. State governments, however, are responsible for enforcement and inspections on the ground. Authorities in states such as Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Uttarakhand found that, despite existing labelling requirements, some hotels, roadside eateries and sweet shops were allegedly serving analogue paneer without informing customers and passing it off as genuine paneer. The states therefore used their regulatory powers to impose restrictions or bans on analogue paneer, citing concerns over consumer deception and public health. Is UP also planning a ban? Uttar Pradesh is also considering a ban on analogue paneer. According to Harishankar Singh, Additional Director of the state's Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA), a proposal to ban analogue paneer has been sent to the FSSAI. If the proposal receives the required approval, Uttar Pradesh could also introduce a ban on analogue paneer.

stories.title: Son, daughter-in-law grab ₹3 crore land using dead father’s thumbprint:Evicted in Lucknow; father wanted property given to 3 daughters
stories.summary: In Lucknow, after the death of his father, the only son usurped land worth ₹3 crores by taking his thumbprint. He also involved his cousin in this act. Before the father's cremation, the son took his thumbprint on a plain paper. Villagers had made a video of the accused son, which came to light today, Thursday. Police investigation revealed that the father, troubled by the behaviour of his son and daughter-in-law, had disinherited them from his property. He had stated that the remaining property would be given to his three daughters. The incident is from Khadauha village in Rahimabad. He started living at his daughters' homes, giving each of the three one bigha of land Chhatrapal (75), a resident of Khadauha, and his wife Shivdevi had a long-standing dispute with their son Mahendra and daughter-in-law Lakshmi. It is alleged that both elderly people were subjected to ill-treatment. In the year 2023, they were also evicted from their ancestral home. According to relatives, Chhatrapal went to the house of his elder daughter Suman, who also lives in Lucknow. He also used to visit the homes of his other two married daughters. Pleased with the care provided by his daughters, Chhatrapal had expressed his intention to give one bigha of land each to his three daughters out of his approximately six and a half bighas of land. Meanwhile, angered by his son Mahendra and daughter-in-law, he had also announced their disinheritance from his property through a public notice. Son took father after dispute, death three days later According to daughter Suman, father Chhatrapal's health deteriorated on July 7. Mahendra was also informed about this. It is alleged that Mahendra reached Lucknow with his wife and other family members and took his father with him, claiming he would get him treated. Suman alleges that her father Chhatrapal died on July 9, three days after her brother took him away. During the father's last rites, Mahendra and his family members also abused the sisters. Accusation of taking thumbprint of dead body on plain paper Family members allege that after their father's death, Mahendra took the thumbprint of his dead body on a plain paper to prepare land-related documents. During this, his cousin also helped him. Villagers secretly made a video of the entire incident. This video has now surfaced.

stories.title: Class 11 friends hang themselves at lover’s house:One dies, other survives after noose breaks; families found them in Saharanpur
stories.summary: Two friends studying in the 11th grade in Saharanpur hanged themselves on Thursday afternoon. One student died, while the other survived as the noose came loose. She was found writhing on the floor. Marks of hanging were found on her neck. She has been admitted to a hospital. Both students had left home for school in the morning, but they went to meet a boy. Their families got wind of this. They reached the boy's house. Due to this, both girls got scared and hanged themselves. According to preliminary investigation, the student who died had an affair with the boy. He fled the scene after the incident. Police are searching for him. The incident occurred in a village in the Chilkana police station area, about 30 km from the district headquarters. The incident took place around 12 noon. Details of the case According to the police, there is a girls' college in the Chilkana police station area. Two students, aged 15 and 16, study in 11th grade here. They left their respective homes in the morning to go to college but both did not reach school. The school management informed the students' families around 11 am that both girls had not come to school. The families replied that both had left home in the morning to go to school. Fearing an untoward incident, the family immediately reached the school. They inquired from the friends of the students. Then, a friend of one of the students told the family that their daughter had a love affair with a boy. She had gone to his house with her friend. Family reached the boy's house, crowd gathered outside The family came to know that the boy's house was a short distance from the school. In a short while, everyone reached there. The family started knocking on the door of the house. When the door did not open, people from the vicinity also arrived at the scene. At that time, both students were inside the house. Seeing the crowd of family members and people outside, both of them got scared. Hanged Themselves with Dupattas, The Other's Noose Came Undone Fearing exposure and disgrace, both students made a noose with their school dupattas (scarves) and attempted to hang themselves. When the house door did not open for a long time, the family members tried to enter through another way. One of the family members reached the house via the neighbor's roof and opened the door. Inside, they saw one student hanging from the noose. She had died on the spot. Meanwhile, the other student's noose had come undone, and she had fallen down. Upon receiving information, the police also reached the spot and took both students to the hospital. Doctors declared one student dead. The other is undergoing medical examination, and the police are monitoring her condition. Accused boy adult, father labourer The young man at whose house the students hanged themselves is an adult. He lives with his father at home. His father works as a laborer at a brick kiln. He goes to work at 6 AM. After his father left, he called the students to his house. CO said girl hanged herself in a dispute Sadar Area Officer Vikas Pratap Singh Chauhan said, “The young woman took this step due to a dispute in a love affair. Action will be taken based on the complaint from the family members. Further action will be taken based on the post-mortem report and evidence.”

stories.title: RPF constable suspended for chewing Gutkha:Officer catches him during speech; he says, 'My lips are naturally red'
stories.summary: An RPF constable was suspended in Gonda on charges of consuming gutkha. It is alleged that the constable was consuming gutkha during the RPF security conference on Wednesday evening. Arun Tripathi, Senior Divisional Security Commissioner of Lucknow Division, who was present at the conference, noticed the constable. He stopped his speech, reprimanded him, and ordered action. The constable's suspension order was issued on Thursday morning. RPF Inspector Anirudh Rai stated that after suspending the constable, he has been attached to Lucknow. Meanwhile, the suspended constable has denied consuming gutkha and attending the conference. He stated - he had not consumed gutkha, his lips are naturally red. Know the full story Brahmadev Kumar Dwivedi, from Saurauri village in Deoria, is a constable in the RPF. He was recruited as a constable in 1998. Before his suspension, he was posted in Gonda. On Wednesday evening, a security conference was held at the RPF barracks complex in Gonda. Many RPF officers and a large number of jawans were present. Senior Divisional Security Commissioner Arun Tripathi was addressing the jawans. During this, his eyes fell on Constable Brahmadev Dwivedi. According to officials, the constable was chewing gutkha. Seeing this, Arun Tripathi stopped his address and reprimanded him. He said that the Railway Protection Force is a disciplined force and such irresponsible behavior will not be tolerated. After the conference, considering the matter as departmental indiscipline, he gave instructions for action. Following this, the constable was suspended on Thursday morning. Officers said - Indiscipline will not be tolerated Arun Tripathi said that the Railway Protection Force is a disciplined force. Laxity or indiscipline at any level in security arrangements will not be tolerated. Constable said - My lips were red, I had not eaten gutkha Constable Brahmadev Kumar Dwivedi denied the accusation. He said, The officers were upset seeing my red lips. I had not consumed gutkha at that time. According to Brahmadev, the main reason for the action against him is taking a bike onto the platform. He said that he was going by bike to perform duty in the eastern yard, as the yard is quite long. The officers were more upset about this. RPF Inspector Anirudh Rai said- Constable Brahmadev has been suspended due to indiscipline. Consuming paan masala while on duty is wrong. He has been suspended and immediately attached to Lucknow.

stories.title: Foreigner runs sex racket across 6 states:Turkmen woman caught in Lucknow; doctor says no private-part surgery
stories.summary: Lola Kayumova, a woman from Uzbekistan arrested in Lucknow, has made several revelations during police interrogation. Police said, “She had married Lucknow resident Janak Pratap Singh, who allegedly left her around two months ago.” The investigation has also revealed that Lola owned two houses in Lucknow and was allegedly running a sex racket not only in Uttar Pradesh but also in five other states. Police had been searching for Lola for a year Lucknow Police had reportedly been looking for Lola for around a year. A few days ago, she returned to the city with a woman from Turkmenistan. The two women went to the same clinic where Lola had previously undergone cosmetic surgery on her face and private parts. FRO alerted before planned surgery This time, before the procedure could be carried out, the doctor informed the Foreigner Registration Office (FRO) about Lola’s presence. An FRO team immediately reached the clinic and arrested Lola and the Turkmenistan national accompanying her. Police said, “They recovered an Aadhaar card, PAN card and driving licence from Lola’s possession. She has since been sent to jail.” Surgeon denies performing private-part surgery Bhaskar reporter spoke to Dr Vivek, the surgeon who had treated Lola. He claimed that he had performed only a nose surgery and denied carrying out any procedure on her private parts. Dr Vivek said, “I was being defamed by claims that I performed private-part surgery on Lola.” Police are continuing to investigate the case and her alleged activities across multiple states. First see 2 pictures- Police investigation about Lola Woman from Turkmenistan gave reference details of Lola A woman from Turkmenistan came to Dr. Vivek's clinic on August 7 for treatment. A rule had already come into effect that if any foreigner comes to India for treatment, all information must be provided to the FRO (Foreigner Registration Office). As per this procedure, all documents from the doctor's clinic were shared with the FRO. The woman who came for treatment had a medical visa. Besides this, she also had several papers related to treatment in Delhi. Along with that woman, Lola had attached her Aadhaar card as her reference. Upon seeing this, the doctor's clinic immediately informed the FRO. With this help, the FRO and police took Lola into custody and after interrogation, arrested her. The person Lola claimed to have married is missing According to Lucknow Police, the person named Janak Pratap Singh with whom she claimed to have married and based on which documents were prepared, could not be traced. Lola says he abandoned her two months ago. In such a situation, it is not possible to say who Janak is. All documents have also been sent for verification. After the report comes, it will become clear whether they are completely fake or were prepared with someone's connivance in the department. Difficulty in interrogation due to inability to speak Hindi, English Meanwhile, Lola doesn't know Hindi, she knows only a little bit of Hindi. Her way of speaking English is also quite different. Due to this, the police faced considerable difficulty in interrogation. However, the investigation made it clear that Lola was running a high-profile sex racket while staying in Lucknow. Stayed in India even after passport-visa expired DCP South Mohammad Mustak informed that on June 20, 2025, information was received about helping foreign women stay illegally in India and taking financial benefits. Plastic surgery/operations were also performed to change the identity of some foreign women without necessary documentary procedures. A case was registered at Sushant Golf City police station in the matter. Based on investigation and information received from FRRO, police detained and interrogated the accused woman Lola Kyumova (45), daughter of Alimad Jamovna, resident of Tashkent, Uzbekistan. According to police, during interrogation she revealed that even after the expiry of visa and passport, she had been living in hiding in different states and districts of India for several years. It is alleged that she had also made Aadhaar card, PAN card and driving license along with other documents contrary to rules. The woman has given information about several other people being involved in her gang and conducting illegal activities with their support. Accused of running flesh trade in 6 states Police claim, “During interrogation, the woman also revealed running immoral flesh trade in different states and districts.” Information has emerged that several other women are also involved in this network along with her. Many other pieces of evidence have also been found from the woman's mobile phone. Based on these evidences, police are investigating the identification of other members connected to the gang and their roles. According to police, “Different addresses of hers have surfaced in Lucknow's Rajajipuram and Sushant Golf City areas. She has given her home address here.” Now read what the surgeon says about Lola- First came to tattoo removal clinic in 2025 Dr. Vivek Gupta says, “Lola first came to his clinic in February 2025. Lola had contacted to get a tattoo near her eye removed. She had all Indian documents. In which it was written about marriage to a person named Janak Pratap Singh.” He added, “As all documents were Indian, there was no need to inform the FRO and fill Form-C. Lola came to his clinic several times for treatment.” Nose surgery was called facial plastic surgery The doctor says, “After the treatment started, Lola later said that she had a problem with her nose, which caused her difficulty in breathing. Due to this, she underwent septo rhinoplasty of her nose.” He added, “Whenever she came to the clinic, it was for tattoo and nose surgery. But she defamed us by saying it was facial plastic surgery and private part operation. However, it is not possible that someone's face can be changed.” Dr. Vivek Gupta says, “I am a plastic surgeon and has to treat people in different ways. The rules for treating foreign nationals have changed, which the FRO department oversees, but somewhere the department has failed to make doctors aware.” He added, “Regarding how to work for the treatment of foreign people, it is difficult to fill the form on the FRO website. Later, providing patient information also becomes difficult.” This time I didn't make a mistake, I informed the FRO beforehand A year ago, an allegation was made against me that I did not provide information before treatment, whereas he had all documents of Indian origin. The second time when he brought another woman for treatment, this matter was raised again and I am being highlighted, although this time information was given beforehand. In the FIR filed a year ago, Dr. Vivek Gupta was made an accused. A case was filed against him by talking to Trijin Raj aka Arjun Rana's associate. After this, his name was removed from the investigation, whereas Dr. Vivek Gupta claims that he has neither met Trijin Raj nor does he know him. It is not known how his name was linked. Now understand the root of the entire matter- On June 21, 2025, police received information about a sex racket operating in Omex Hazratganj Apartment in Lucknow. In the raid, Holida and Nilofer from Uzbekistan were arrested. Both were staying here illegally. Police investigation revealed that the flat belonged to Doctor Vivek Gupta. Lola had brought these two young women to India. Holida and Neelofar had told during interrogation that through Lola Kayumova, they had met Dr. Vivek Gupta, who runs Minerva Clinic in Patrakarpuram and Ahimamau. Dr. Vivek Gupta had performed plastic surgery on both of them. Dr. Vivek was accused of also becoming an active member of the racket. He used to perform plastic surgery on girls associated with the racket, so that their look would appear Russian and they would look younger.

stories.title: Rahul Gandhi moves SC over disproportionate assets case:Challenges Allahabad HC order for ED-CBI probe
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi filed a petition in the Supreme Court on Thursday in a disproportionate assets case. In this, he has challenged the order of the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court, in which the court had directed CBI and ED to verify the allegations of disproportionate assets. The case will be heard on August 17. Rahul Gandhi has also filed a separate transfer petition in the Supreme Court. In this, he has sought to transfer the case from Allahabad High Court to Delhi High Court. This petition was filed on August 7. Actually, Karnataka BJP worker Vignesh Shishir had accused Rahul of disproportionate assets in the High Court. Following this, the court had said in its order in May that if the petitioner's complaint has been received, then the allegations made therein should be verified according to law. CBI or ED can take appropriate steps under the law. This news is being updated....

stories.title: Lost ₹3 lakh in PUBG, student stages kidnapping:Uses AI to fake taped-mouth photo, sends it to father and hides at friend’s house
stories.summary: A Class 11 student in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, allegedly staged his own kidnapping after losing ₹3 lakh while playing PUBG. With the help of his girlfriend, the 16-year-old created AI-generated images showing tape over his mouth and blood marks on his body to make it appear that he had been brutally assaulted. The student then sent the images to his father on WhatsApp and demanded Rs 1 lakh, threatening that he would otherwise receive his son’s body. Father alerts police after receiving threat The student’s father, a cloth merchant, panicked after seeing the photographs and immediately informed the police. Police placed the teenager’s mobile phone under surveillance and tracked his movements. Within around two hours, they located him at a friend’s house and took him into custody. Girlfriend helped create fake images During the preliminary investigation, police found that the student’s girlfriend, who lives in Delhi, had allegedly helped him prepare the AI-generated photographs. The incident took place around 8pm on Tuesday (11 Aug) in the Sikrigunj area, around 40 km from the Gorakhpur district headquarters. Police are investigating the circumstances behind the student’s PUBG losses and the role of his girlfriend in the staged kidnapping. Student stages own kidnapping after friends demand ₹3 lakh repayment The Class 11 student, identified as the son of Satyaprakash, lives with his family in the Dhanghat area of Sant Kabir Nagar. He studies at an English-medium school in Gorakhpur. According to police, the teenager had developed an addiction to PUBG and borrowed money from friends and acquaintances to continue playing. Over time, his outstanding debt reportedly reached around ₹3 lakh. Debt pressure led to fake kidnapping plan Police said, “The student came up with the idea of staging his own kidnapping after people began demanding that he repay the money.” He contacted his girlfriend in Delhi and asked her to create photographs that would make it appear as though he had been abducted and assaulted. According to the preliminary investigation, the girlfriend used AI tools to edit the student’s photographs and create images showing signs of an apparent assault. The teenager planned to use these photographs to convince his family that he had been kidnapped and demand money from them. Put mobile on flight mode, sent photo by connecting to Wi-Fi As part of the plan, the Class 11 student left home around 7pm on Tuesday (11 Aug), telling his family that he was going to Sikrigunj. After reaching the area, he switched his mobile phone to flight mode. He later connected the device to a friend’s Wi-Fi network to send the planned messages. AI-generated photo sent with threat At 9:47pm, the student sent a threatening message to his father, Satyaprakash, on WhatsApp along with an AI-generated photograph showing him as an apparent kidnapping victim. Alarmed by the message, Satyaprakash asked where he should send the money. The student responded by sending a bank account or payment number and asked him to transfer the money online. Father says he cannot make online payment Satyaprakash told his son that he did not have money available for an online transfer. The student then changed his demand and asked his father to arrange ₹2 lakh in cash. Suspecting that his son had genuinely been kidnapped, Satyaprakash went directly to Dhanghat police station and informed the police. Surveillance revealed the truth, student found at friend's house SP South Dinesh Kumar Puri informed, “The police put the student's mobile number under surveillance. The investigation revealed that the student's phone was in Sikriganj. After this, the police contacted Sikriganj police and provided complete information.” He added, “When the police team reached there around 2 AM at night, the student was found comfortably at his friend's house. The police took him along to the station. During interrogation, it came to light that the student had fabricated a false story of his kidnapping to repay a debt.”

stories.title: Ganga swells in Kanpur, children take boats to school:Floods hit 80 UP villages; ghats submerged in Kashi, cremations disrupted
stories.summary: Heavy rain in the hills has caused the Ganga, Yamuna, Sharda and seven other rivers to swell across Uttar Pradesh, with more than 80 villages affected by floods. Farrukhabad is the worst hit, with flooding reported in 49 villages. The rising water has also disrupted life in Varanasi, Kanpur and Unnao, while 48 districts are under a rain alert today. Ghats submerged in Varanasi, cremations disrupted In Varanasi, floodwater has reached the steps of the ghats and submerged more than 100 small temples. At Harishchandra Ghat, the cremation area has been flooded. Cremations are now being carried out on the upper steps, forcing families to wait for two to three hours to perform the last rites. Children take boats to school in Kanpur The Ganga in Kanpur has risen close to the warning level, with floodwater entering more than five villages. Children are using boats to reach their schools. Hundreds of bighas of farmland have also been submerged. In Unnao, Ganga water has entered residential colonies. Several residents are staying on rooftops, while boats are being used in flooded streets. Sharda swallows 70 acres in Lakhimpur Kheri In Lakhimpur Kheri, the Sharda river has already swallowed around 70 acres of land as its water level continues to rise. In Raebareli, a five-foot-long snake entered a house amid the flooding. Although most cities across Uttar Pradesh are seeing sunshine today, 48 districts remain under a rain alert. Monsoon likely to strengthen again Professor Manoj Srivastava, a weather scientist at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi, said the monsoon clouds had temporarily moved away from Uttar Pradesh. He said a low-pressure area was expected to become active over the Bay of Bengal, which could strengthen monsoon activity across the state again. “Good rainfall is expected across Uttar Pradesh in the coming days,” Srivastava said.

stories.title: Mahant kills two youths, buries bodies in temple:Was having affair with one man’s sister, went with friend to confront; case revealed after 19 days
stories.summary: A mahant in Baghpat, Uttar Pradesh, allegedly murdered two friends and buried their bodies inside the temple premises. The bodies were recovered 19 days later, after police were tipped off about the killings. Police recovered the remains of Ankit, 25, and Israr, 32, at around 3am today (13 Aug). The temple’s mahant had allegedly fled before the police reached the spot, while his two disciples were taken into custody. Bodies identified from clothes and watches The bodies had decomposed significantly by the time they were recovered. Police identified the two men with the help of their clothes and watches. According to the preliminary investigation, the mahant’s disciples confessed to the crime and helped police locate and recover the bodies buried behind the temple. Ankit allegedly went to confront mahant Initial police inquiries suggest that Ankit’s sister was allegedly in a relationship with the mahant. On July 25, Ankit reportedly went to the temple with his friend Israr to confront him and question him about the relationship. Police suspect an argument broke out during the confrontation and escalated, following which the mahant allegedly killed both men. Bodies allegedly buried with disciples’ help After the alleged murders, the bodies were reportedly buried behind the temple with the assistance of the mahant’s disciples. The incident took place in the Chandinagar police station area, around 20 km from the Baghpat district headquarters. Police are continuing to search for the absconding mahant and are questioning the two detained disciples. See pictures Know the complete case in sequence Israr, 32, and differently-abled Ankit, 25, residents of Sigoli Taga, were close friends whose houses were located directly opposite each other. Israr worked as a labourer, while Ankit was unemployed. Israr’s father Ridku told police that his son had gone for a bike ride with Ankit on the afternoon of July 25. When neither returned by the following day, their families began searching for them. From the evening of July 27, both men’s mobile phones were switched off. On July 29, their families lodged missing-person complaints at Chandinagar police station. Police then began tracing their mobile numbers, locations and other possible leads. Mahant’s disciples allegedly reveal the murders Police said, “After nearly 19 days, an informer provided information on Wednesday (12 Aug) night that Mahant Naresh Nath of the Ganesh Temple in Lahchauda had allegedly murdered the two missing men.” When police reached the temple in evening to question the mahant, he was reportedly not present and had allegedly fled. Police detained two of his disciples and questioned them. During interrogation, they allegedly revealed that the bodies of both youths had been buried within the temple premises. Bodies recovered around 3am Police returned to the temple with a team at around 3am and began excavation based on the information provided by the disciples. The bodies were recovered from the rear portion of the temple premises. As they had decomposed, police identified them with the help of Ankit’s disability and the watch worn by Israr. A forensic team was called to the scene and collected evidence. The bodies were subsequently sent to Baghpat District Hospital for post-mortem examination. Police arrested both disciples and are now searching for the absconding mahant. Brother alleges affair with mahant led friends to temple confrontation Israr’s brother Fareed alleged that his brother and neighbour Ankit had been close friends for several years. He claimed, “Ankit’s sister was allegedly in a relationship with Mahant Naresh Nath of the Ganesh Temple in Lahchauda.” According to Fareed, “The two friends had repeatedly tried to convince her to end the relationship, but she did not agree.” ‘They said they were going to Rataul’ Fareed said, “On July 25, Israr and Ankit left home saying they were going to Rataul, but allegedly went to the temple instead.” He added, “They may have gone there to confront, counsel and warn the mahant, but we do not know what happened after they reached the temple.” The family later reported both men missing after they failed to return. Fareed said, "Police called the family today morning (13 Aug) and informed them that Israr had allegedly been murdered and that his body had been recovered from the temple premises. Family earlier travelled to Ghaziabad to identify another body Israr’s brother Fareed said, “The family had earlier travelled to Ghaziabad on Monday after receiving information about an unidentified body, fearing it could be Israr.” However, the family later confirmed that the body belonged to someone else. ‘Today, we found Israr’s body at the temple’ Fareed said, “Israr’s body was eventually recovered from a pit inside the temple premises in Lahchauda.” The recovery has left the family devastated, with relatives struggling to come to terms with his death. Police have sent the body for post-mortem examination as the investigation continues. Mahant allegedly moved into temple six months ago Israr’s brother Fareed said, “Mahant Naresh Nath is originally from Uttarakhand and had been living in a rented house in Sigoli Taga village until around six months ago.” According to him, “The mahant lived next door to Ankit. After his alleged relationship with Ankit’s sister became known, a dispute reportedly arose. Following this, Naresh Nath allegedly shifted to the temple premises along with his disciples.” Police: Mahant absconding, two disciples detained Chandinagar police station in-charge Rakesh Kumar said, “The bodies of the two youths who had been missing since July 25 were recovered after police excavated the temple premises.” He added, “The bodies have been sent for post-mortem, and the exact cause and manner of death will be established through the report.” The officer said, “The temple’s mahant, who is allegedly suspected in the murders, is currently absconding. His two disciples have been detained and are being questioned.” Police stated, “Information about the location of the buried bodies was obtained from the disciples. CCTV footage from the temple and surrounding areas is also being examined, while teams continue to search for the mahant.” Israr used to work as a laborer, leaving behind wife and 3 children Family members told Israr used to run his family by doing labor work. His family includes wife Firdaus and three children. Daughter Isra is 6 years old, while son Ayan is 5 years old and Faizan is 3 years old. There is mourning in the family after Israr's death. Meanwhile, disabled Ankit was the only brother among 5 sisters. He was unmarried and unemployed. Two of his sisters are married.

stories.title: Doctor dies by suicide after jumping from 8th-floor apartment:Woman PhD con artist allegedly duped him of ₹1.40 crore
stories.summary: A doctor committed suicide in Gorakhpur on Thursday. The doctor jumped from the eighth floor of an apartment to end his life. Family members took him to a nearby private hospital in a blood-soaked condition, where doctors declared him dead. The incident took place in the Gorakhnath police station area. On August 5, the doctor had filed an FIR at AIIMS police station, accusing a female con artist and her gang of defrauding him of Rs 1.40 crore. He had been in shock ever since this incident. A case of fraud has been registered against the PhD female con artist, her officer father, her teacher husband, and others. Police have arrested the female con artist and her father and sent them to jail. The incident is reported to have occurred around 9:30 AM. Veterinarian Parmatma Singh (52) lived with his two children, a boy and a girl, on the eighth floor of Basant Enclave, located in Rajendra Nagar Colony of Gorakhnath area. His wife, Savitri Singh, is also a veterinarian. After this incident, she is inconsolable. Upon receiving information about the incident, the police of Gorakhnath police station reached the spot and are investigating. The doctor was currently posted in a block of Maharajganj district.

stories.title: Women in UP to get ₹50,000 each:₹20,000 first instalment before polls, followed by ₹10,000 each; Yogi govt plans scheme
stories.summary: The UP government may implement a major scheme to target the women's vote bank before the assembly elections. Under this, more than 50 lakh women will be given financial assistance of Rs 50,000 each. The first installment of Rs 20,000 will be given before the elections. After the elections, if the BJP government is formed, 3 installments of Rs 10,000 each will be given. Deliberations on the scheme have started within the government. In fact, after registering a big win in the Bihar assembly elections last year, BJP's focus is now on UP. Just as Rs 10,000 each was sent to women's accounts before the elections in Bihar, a similar scheme will be launched in UP. Government will target women before elections The Yogi government has geared up for the assembly elections. Amidst the Gen-Z movement, the government is considering a major scheme to woo the women's vote bank. A scheme is being considered for women's assistance, self-employment, and economic self-reliance. The scheme will be proposed through the Women Welfare Department. Under the scheme, providing financial assistance of Rs 50,000 to women is being considered. Priority to women from families below poverty line The government will prioritize women from SC, ST families, women from BPL families, and women from economically weaker families in the scheme. It may include women from families whose income does not exceed 12 lakh rupees. Women's scheme will be a game-changer People in the government believe that the scheme of cash incentives for women can prove to be a game-changer in the assembly elections. Such a scheme was first implemented in Madhya Pradesh, then in Maharashtra and Bihar assembly elections. Due to those schemes, BJP governments were formed there. Political analyst Virendranath Bhatt believes that providing cash assistance to women in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Bihar has benefited them in elections. If the government implements a similar scheme in UP, it will definitely benefit the BJP in the elections. There are about 5.67 crore women voters in the state. If women receive cash, it will impact the elections. Women can also become game-changers in UP BJP had a big victory in the Bihar Assembly elections. NDA had won 202 seats there. The unprecedented support and votes of women were considered the basis for NDA's victory, which was more than expected. The reason for women's inclination towards NDA was the 10-10 thousand rupees sent to the accounts of Jeevika Didis before the elections. Ministers of the Yogi government, BJP officials, and political analysts also believe this. That is why, after Madhya Pradesh's Ladli Behna Yojana, Maharashtra's CM Majhi Bahan Ladki, and Haryana's Deendayal Lado Lakshmi, BJP is going to implement a game-changer scheme in UP as well to secure the votes of women and daughters. Challenge of Mission 2027, Pressure of a Big Victory BJP-NDA had won in Haryana, Maharashtra, Delhi, and Bihar. After this, the UP Assembly elections- 2027 are no less than a big challenge for UP CM Yogi, BJP, and ideological organizations. Although CM Yogi has already registered the record of being CM for the longest time and running a BJP government for the longest time. However, given the results in Bihar, the pressure for a similar massive victory has increased. The assembly elections in UP will commence by the first week of January- 2027. Therefore, the government is going to launch a scheme for women as soon as possible. Understand: What is Bihar's Jeevika Didi Model? The NDA government led by CM Nitish Kumar in Bihar implemented the Mukhyamantri Mahila Rojgar Yojana (Chief Minister Women Employment Scheme). Its objective was to connect one woman from each family with self-employment. For this, one woman from each family was given financial assistance of 10 thousand rupees before the assembly elections. After starting the employment, the government will assess it. Following this, a maximum financial assistance of two lakh rupees will be provided to further expand the work. The Nitish government transferred 10-10 thousand rupees into the accounts of 25 lakh women. Approximately 500 crore rupees were spent on this. In the assembly elections, the NDA received a massive majority with 202 seats. After this, all political analysts say that the 10-10 thousand rupees transferred to the accounts of Jeevika Didis (women associated with Jeevika self-help groups) played a significant role in this massive victory. Now understand why BJP is targeting women voters? Target one, achieve all Political analysts believe - BJP strategists have understood that by targeting one woman in a family, she influences 5 votes. Especially, in families where women are given financial assistance, their votes are almost certain to go in favor of the concerned ruling party. In UP too, there are about 7.25 crore women voters. 98 lakh women in UP are engaged in self-employment The State Rural Livelihood Mission is running in UP to make women self-reliant. Under this, women's self-help groups of 10 women each are formed and linked to self-employment. Financial assistance is also provided by the government on subsidy. Currently, 98,76,389 women from 8,99,398 families are associated with these groups in UP. Women can become the counter to SP's PDA BJP leaders believe that providing significant assistance to women before the assembly elections can counter SP's PDA. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, SP's PDA issue worked. As a result, BJP's seats decreased from 64 to 34. After the Lok Sabha elections, in the BJP legislative party meeting, CM Yogi himself admitted that if elections were held today, BJP would get 188 seats in UP. That is why BJP is trying to woo women voters.

stories.title: Monsoon to remain active in Varanasi for next 6 days:Ganga water level starts receding, small temples submerged; boat operations resume
stories.summary: The monsoon has become active again in Varanasi, bringing the possibility of changing weather conditions across the city and neighbouring districts over the next six days. The Meteorological Department has forecast light to heavy rainfall at different places during this period, with thunderstorms and lightning also likely. Thunderstorms expected on Friday Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is expected in Varanasi on Friday (14 Aug), with the possibility of thunderstorms in several areas. The department has also issued a heavy rainfall alert for August 15 and 16, indicating that rain activity could intensify during the weekend. Humidity and low pressure keeping skies cloudy Today (13 Aug), Varanasi recorded a temperature of around 32°C. Wind speed was about 3 kmph, while relative humidity stood at 74%. Weather officials said, “High humidity and the influence of a low-pressure system could keep skies cloudy and favour rainfall over the coming days.” See picture Now know what lies ahead The Meteorological Department has forecast thunderstorms accompanied by rain and lightning in Varanasi and adjoining areas on Friday (14 Aug). There is also a possibility of lightning strikes during the spell, prompting officials to advise people to remain cautious during adverse weather. Heavy rain alert for August 15-16 According to the department, Varanasi and surrounding areas could receive heavy rainfall on August 15 and 16. Rain accompanied by thunder and lightning is also likely to continue on August 17 and 18. Bay of Bengal system to drive rainfall Weather scientist Prof Manoj Srivastava said, “Rainfall activity is expected to continue for the next four days due to a low-pressure area that has developed over the Bay of Bengal.” Ganga water level decreased, but the pace is very slow The water level of the Ganga in Varanasi has started receding, but the decline remains slow. Over the past 36 hours, the river level has fallen by around 11 cm and currently stands at 63.60 metres. River falling by just 1 cm in six hours The pace of decline remains sluggish, with the water level dropping by only around 1 cm in six hours and about 2 cm over 12 hours. Ghats and riverside areas hope for relief According to the Central Water Commission, the Ganga’s water level in Varanasi is expected to continue falling. The gradual decline has raised hopes of relief among people living near the ghats and riverside areas. Ban on boat operations lifted The ban on boat operations imposed during the rise in the Ganga’s water level has now been lifted, bringing relief to boatmen in Varanasi. However, the administration and concerned departments have advised people to remain cautious while travelling on the river as the water level is still being monitored. Tulsi Ghat steps emerge as floodwater recedes With the Ganga’s water level falling and floodwater receding, the steps of Tulsi Ghat have started becoming visible again. The development is being seen as a sign of normalcy gradually returning to the area. Connectivity between ghats yet to fully resume Despite the improvement, connectivity between several ghats has not been completely restored. Officials expect movement and other activities along the ghats to return to normal only after the Ganga continues to recede steadily.

stories.title: Sharpened sword for 2 days, then killed contractor:Accused’s homes locked in Gorakhpur; police care for dog, cow
stories.summary: Electricity department contractor Shiv Kumar Tripathi was allegedly killed in Gorakhpur on August 8 in an attack involving a sword and sickle. The main accused’s house in Ahiraula is around 500 metres from the contractor’s residence. Police have arrested eight accused in connection with the murder, following which their houses have remained locked. Police personnel have been deployed outside the properties as a precautionary measure. Police feed dog and cow left at locked house A German Shepherd and a cow were left at one of the accused’s houses after the family members fled following the incident. With no one to care for them, the animals were reportedly left without food and water. For the past five days, police personnel deployed in the area have been feeding and providing water to the dog and cow. Murder allegedly linked to 2024 revenge killing Police investigation indicates that the murder was not the result of a sudden dispute but was allegedly linked to an old rivalry stemming from the 2024 murder of Aadesh Chaudhary. According to police, the contractor’s cousins were allegedly involved in Aadesh Chaudhary’s killing. The latest attack is believed to have been carried out as revenge for that murder. One of the accused, a Class 12 minor from Aadesh Chaudhary’s family, allegedly attacked Shiv Kumar with a sword. Police said, “The accused told investigators that he had sharpened the sword for two days after buying it so that it could inflict deeper injuries.” The murder has left the Ahiraula village tense, with police maintaining a presence around the homes of the arrested accused. Villagers hiding in homes, afraid even to speak The Dainik Bhaskar team reached Ahirauli village on Wednesday (12 Aug). There was silence in the streets. In the afternoon, village women were huddled inside homes talking. When asked anything, people were refusing to tell. To the extent that they were even pretending to be unaware about any incident that had occurred there. At Shiv Kumar's house, his only son Advocate Aditya Tiwari is sitting in white clothes, repeatedly breaking down remembering the incident. Meanwhile, there is a continuous stream of visitors throughout the day. People are consoling Aditya. From inside the house, the intermittent sounds of crying and wailing of Shiv Kumar's mother Savitri, wife Sandhya Devi and married daughter Nidhi Tripathi can be heard. The helpless, blood-soaked face of Shiv Kumar visible in the video is haunting the family. His father has passed away. He has two brothers, Siddhanath Tripathi and Ramkumar Tripathi. Attacked with a sickle while eating at Brahma Bhoj Actually, 2 years ago in 2024, Aadesh Chaudhary, the cousin of Rahul Chaudhary from the same village, was murdered. Contractor Shiv Kumar Tripathi (52)'s son and associates were accused of the murder. All of them had gone to jail. Since then, Rahul and his family harbored hatred towards Shivkumar. According to police, “On August 8, Shiv Kumar had gone to attend a Brahma Bhoj (community feast) in the village. He was sitting on the ground eating food. Just then, Rahul Chaudhary (30) attacked Shiv Kumar on the head from behind with a sickle. He fell down seriously injured.” Officials added, “When people present there intervened, the accused fled from the spot. The family hosting the Brahma Bhoj took Shiv Kumar in an auto to the hospital. On the way, Rahul, along with his minor brother and 8 others, stopped the auto.” They stated, “The accused had sticks and sharp weapons with them. Villagers tried to stop them, but the accused dragged Shiv Kumar out of the auto and took him 200 meters away. There, Rahul's minor brother came with a sword.” Officals further added, “They chased Shiv Kumar on the road and attacked him. He fell on the road. After that, they killed him with multiple blows. Then the accused fled from the spot. During this time, some youth present there made a video of the incident.” Rival families lived just 500 metres apart The Chaudhary family lives around 500 metres from the house of contractor Shiv Kumar Tripathi. The two families had been at odds since the 2024 murder of Aadesh Chaudhary, son of Deepu Chaudhary. Aadesh was shot dead during a Hari Kirtan in 2024. Shiv Kumar’s son and some of his relatives were named accused in the case and were subsequently jailed. Release of contractor’s son fuelled resentment Deepu Chaudhary is the eldest of four brothers. Deepu, Vikas and Pramod live and work in Mumbai, while two of Deepu’s sons, Vivek and Abhishek, are studying away from home. In Ahirauli village, Pramod’s minor son Vinod, who is studying in Class 12, and his nephew Rahul Chaudhary live with the family. The Chaudharys are considered a financially well-off family in the village. However, the murder of Aadesh had created deep resentment between the two families. According to the police investigation, tensions escalated further after Shiv Kumar’s son was released from jail. Police suspect that the long-standing anger and desire for revenge ultimately led to the contractor’s murder. Rahul displayed photos with weapons Rahul Chaudhary, identified by police as the main accused in the contractor’s murder, was reportedly fond of weapons and frequently shared photographs with them on social media. Posters featured BJP leaders Rahul was also preparing to contest the district panchayat elections from Ward No. 39 of Sikrigunj. As part of his campaign preparations, he had reportedly put up banners and posters at several locations. The banners carried his photograph alongside those of the BJP state president and the Chief Minister. Murder video surfaces on social media On August 11, Betiyahata councillor and lawyer Vishwajit Tripathi posted a video purportedly showing the contractor’s murder on Facebook. Tripathi alleged that police personnel pressured him to remove the video. Police also reached the court and reportedly attempted to take him to the police station, but returned after lawyers objected. Minor allegedly chased contractor before attack The video appears to show a minor chasing the contractor on the road before attacking him with a sword. During the attack, the contractor can be seen pleading with folded hands and asking to be spared. However, the attacker allegedly continued striking him. After apparently believing that the contractor had died, the accused fled the spot. In this regards, SSP Dr. Kaustubh said, “Police have arrested all 8 accused in the case and sent them to jail. Sikriganj police station in-charge Anjul Chaturvedi has been immediately line-attached on charges of negligence. Investigation of the case is ongoing.”

stories.title: Farrukhabad floods:31 houses swept into Ganga in 14 days; life savings lost, woman says, ‘My daughter’s wedding was planned, now we have no home’
stories.summary: “Last year, the Ganga swallowed our house. I took a loan to build another one, but now the river is about to take that too. My daughter’s wedding is approaching, but we have nothing left.” Tears welled up in Gyanadevi’s eyes as she spoke. She could not continue, while her daughter sitting nearby also broke down in tears. Gyanadevi lives in Bilawalpur village, around 10 km from Farrukhabad. The Ganga is now flowing just 50 metres from her house, with severe erosion leaving the building on the verge of collapse. 31 houses washed away in 14 days The situation is particularly grim in Dilip’s Madaiya village, where 31 houses have been swallowed by the surging Ganga in just 14 days. Only three to four houses remain. Fearing they too could soon be washed away, residents have started demolishing them themselves to recover whatever belongings they can and move them to safer locations. Villagers fear entire settlement could disappear Residents fear that continued rise in the Ganga’s water level and ongoing bank erosion could destroy the remaining houses as well. If the erosion continues at the same pace, villagers fear the entire settlement could eventually disappear into the river. Embankment breached as Ganga erodes riverbank The rising Ganga in Farrukhabad has breached a section of an embankment, allowing the river’s current to flow into surrounding areas. After causing severe erosion, the water has now moved nearly 1 km from the original point. Floodwaters have surrounded 48 villages, triggering anger among residents who fear further damage to homes and farmland. Villagers question ₹7.5-crore project Residents said an embankment costing around ₹7.5 crore was constructed before the monsoon to protect the area from the river’s rising waters. However, they alleged that the structure failed to withstand the Ganga’s pressure for even a few months, raising questions over the quality and effectiveness of the project. Due to flooding, roads have been submerged, and boats are the only means of transportation left. 1 lakh people have been shifted to safe locations. The situation is such that to reach Bilawlpur village, about 10 km from the district headquarters, one has to travel by boat for 5 hours. People are taking grains and remaining household items to safe places. House completed just two months ago Gyanadevi said, “My family had earlier lived in a village around 1 km away, where we had a four-room house with a veranda.” She added, “However, as the Ganga began eroding the riverbank, floodwaters reached our home and submerged it. We then built another house, which was completed in June this year.” She stated, At the time, we had no idea that the river would eventually change course and reach our new home after eroding the banks." ‘We made a mistake by building here’ Gyanadevi now regrets choosing the location for their second home. She said, “We made a mistake by building our house here. If we had bought land somewhere else, we would not have faced this situation today.” The family had invested all its savings in the new house. Now, with the Ganga threatening to swallow it as well, Gyanadevi says they have been left with almost nothing. ‘Crops, house, everything is being lost’ Gyanadevi’s husband Hansram stood outside their house in a torn shirt, repeatedly looking at the walls and their belongings. He later began removing bricks stored on the roof, hoping they could be reused if the family manages to build another house somewhere safer. He said, “Riverbank erosion has been a problem in the area for the past three to four years, with several houses already washed away.” ₹12.5 lakh house now under threat He stated, “This year, an embankment was built in our village to stop the erosion. We trusted it and built our house here, spending around Rs 12.5 lakh. But after the rains, the embankment itself was washed away. It was made of mud. Now our house is also on the verge of collapsing.” He recalled that the area did not face flooding on this scale around a decade ago. With repeated floods, villagers are now able to grow only one crop a year. The family had built the house hoping to arrange their daughter’s wedding. They had also raised 17 cows and goats, but the floods have put their home, livestock and livelihood at risk. ‘There was going to be a wedding at home’ Hansram’s 18-year-old daughter Shalini sat quietly a short distance from the family’s threatened home. She said, “The family had been preparing for a wedding, but the flood and erosion had left them uncertain about what would happen next.” When asked where the family would go if the house collapsed, Shalini struggled to respond and became emotional. After a brief silence, she said, “No officer comes to help us. Those who did come turned back halfway through the village.” ‘There were houses here, now nothing remains’ Village resident Sarvesh said, “My house was also destroyed by riverbank erosion. My uncle’s house stood next to it, but one of the structures collapsed this morning.” He stated, “There were two to three more houses a little further from here. Where we are standing now, there were houses. But look around — nothing is left.” ‘Crores were spent, but what did we get?’ Sarvesh expressed anger over the failure of the embankment built to prevent erosion. He asked, “Officials told us that the embankment had been constructed and the village land would no longer erode. Crores of rupees were spent on it, but where did that money go?” He said the authorities could instead have provided land at a safer location. He added, “It would have been better if they had given us land somewhere else. We could have built our houses there. The money is gone, and now our houses are gone too. We are left wandering around helplessly.” ‘No ration left, we do not know where to go’ Santosh Kumar said, “Severe erosion had already caused extensive damage in the area last year, with entire settlements being washed away.” He added, “In five villages, only two to four houses are left. If the erosion continues at this pace, more people will suffer losses.” He further stated, “Many residents had already abandoned their homes in villages surrounded by floodwaters”. According to him, government assistance has remained limited. He also added, “Officials came a few days ago and distributed ration before leaving. That stock has also run out. Now we do not know where to go or what to do.” See people's troubles in 2 pictures- Ganga water level inches towards danger mark In Farrukhabad, the Ganga is flowing just 5 cm below the danger level of 137.05 metres, raising concerns over further flooding and erosion. As water levels continue to rise, 48 villages have effectively been cut off and turned into islands after connecting roads were submerged. Administration starts boat services With road connectivity disrupted, the administration has started operating boats to maintain access to the affected villages. Irrigation Department officials have warned that the situation could deteriorate further if the Ganga continues to rise at the current pace. In this regard, ADM Arun Singh said, “There is flood water in 22 villages coming under Sadar tehsil. The government is providing assistance of ₹1.20 lakh. We have prepared a list of flood victims and sent it to the government. Relief camps and cattle centers have been set up.”

stories.title: ₹50,000 earned in one night, women also humiliate them:Male sex workers in Lucknow-Kanpur see growing trend; their hidden world
stories.summary: Male escorts, or gigolos, say their work is often seen as easy because their clients are women, many of them from affluent families. However, they describe the profession as risky, with concerns ranging from police action and financial uncertainty to abuse and health risks. A Dainik Bhaskar team spoke to two men from Lucknow, aged 28 and 34, who have been working in the profession for 4-5 years. Their identities have been withheld to protect their privacy. How they enter the profession One of the men said he entered the profession through friends after the Covid-19 pandemic, when he was living in Mumbai. He initially took up the work for fun and earned ₹6,000-₹7,000 from his first assignment. He gradually became comfortable with it and continued. According to him, appearance, personality and physical fitness are important in the profession. Escorts maintain their fitness through workouts and protein-rich diets and generally avoid intoxicating substances. However, some clients pressure them to drink. Lucknow and Kanpur emerge as new markets While demand is traditionally higher in metropolitan cities, the men said the profession has expanded to Lucknow and Kanpur. They claimed that escorts and clients are familiar with specific meeting spots, particularly in areas of Gomti Nagar. They also alleged that escorts have to pay members of their network to use certain spots. The amount varies, with some locations charging around ₹2,000 and others ₹3,000 a day. The men said senior members of their networks handle external arrangements, including dealing with the police and managing access to locations. Newcomers generally depend on these networks for work. Most bookings come through referrals According to the escorts, referrals are the main source of bookings. A satisfied client may recommend an escort to other women in her social circle, which also helps new clients feel more comfortable. They said many clients come from wealthy families and include wives of officers and women whose husbands are major businessmen living abroad. Earnings can reach ₹10 lakh a month Income varies significantly depending on the number of bookings. One escort said he can earn ₹2-2.5 lakh a month when work is steady, while some others in the profession earn ₹5-10 lakh. He charges around ₹20,000 for a full night and ₹10,000-₹12,000 for 2-4 hours. More established escorts can charge ₹30,000-₹40,000, and in some cases up to ₹50,000 for a night. However, income is not guaranteed. He said there are times when he gets no work for an entire month. Clients mostly middle-aged women The escorts said many of their clients are women aged 35-40, although some are 60 or older. Younger clients are comparatively uncommon. They described most clients as belonging to affluent sections of society and said they may have to meet 10-12 clients as part of their work. Police, abuse and health risks The men described several risks associated with the profession. They said fear of the police remains a major concern, while meeting unknown clients can also be dangerous. Some clients allegedly become aggressive after drinking, abuse the escorts or refuse to pay. The men said such incidents can affect their self-respect, particularly when clients are dissatisfied despite the services provided. They also raised concerns about sexual health. Although they said they generally take precautions, some clients allegedly refuse to allow protection, creating a risk of HIV transmission. One escort said he has begun considering leaving the profession because of the emotional and practical difficulties involved. Fraud in the name of gigolo jobs The report also highlights cyber fraud conducted through fake ‘Gigolo Club’ and ‘Gigolo Job’ s. Fraudsters allegedly demand money for registration, medical tests or hotel bookings. People are therefore advised to be cautious about such offers and verify claims before making payments. What the law says Supreme Court advocate Ayush Shukla said there is no separate law specifically governing gigolos or male prostitution in India. He explained that prostitution itself is not directly criminalised, but activities covered by the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act (ITPA) can attract legal action. According to him, consensual private meetings between adults over 18 do not by themselves constitute a crime, but monetary transactions can create legal complications.
