stories.title: UP cracks down on fake dairy products:Ban imposed on making, storing and selling 'paneer', 'ghee' and 'khoya' sold as milk products
stories.summary: The government has become strict regarding non-dairy products being sold in Uttar Pradesh under the name of milk-based dairy products. The government has banned the manufacturing, storage, and sale of analogue dairy products. This includes all such products like analogue paneer, cream, ghee, chhena, and khoya, which are prepared from non-milk ingredients instead of milk and are sold as dairy products. The government has taken this action under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Its purpose is to protect people from non-dairy products being sold under the name of genuine milk-based products and to ensure the quality of food items. What are analogue dairy products? Analogue dairy is a product that looks and is used like it's made from milk. However, its main milk component is replaced with non-dairy ingredients. For instance, if a cheese-like product is prepared using vegetable fats, oils, non-dairy proteins, or other ingredients instead of milk or its main milk components, it can fall into the analogue category. This means the matter is not limited to just adding water to milk or starch to prepared paneer. Here, it will be seen whether the item being sold as paneer, ghee, cream, chhena, or khoya is actually a dairy product made from milk or an alternative prepared from non-dairy ingredients. Impact on everything from Paneer to Ghee and Khoya Products such as analogue paneer, analogue cream, analogue ghee, analogue chhena, and analogue khoya are included within the scope of the government's order. The order covers all types of analogue dairy products. However, this does not mean that the sale of regular paneer, ghee, or khoya has been banned. The sale of dairy products prepared from real milk according to prescribed standards will continue. The ban is on products that have been prepared from non-dairy ingredients, giving them the appearance of dairy products. Analogue is a separate category even in FSSAI rules In the rules and documents of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), dairy analogues are considered a separate category. For dairy analogues for which separate identity standards are not prescribed, there is a provision to declare the word 'Analogue' in their labeling. However, not every product containing ingredients other than milk is automatically considered an analog. Some composite milk products and products prepared under specific regulations fall into a different category. The main question is whether non-dairy ingredients have been used to replace any major component of milk. Food Safety Monitoring to Increase Before Festivals The demand for dairy products remains throughout the year, but during festivals, the consumption of paneer, khoya, chhena, and ghee increases rapidly. In such a situation, the monitoring and sampling by the food safety department also increase. According to officials, action will not be limited to analog dairy products only. Action will be taken against the concerned trader if any kind of adulteration is found in food products. Officials of the Food and Civil Supplies Department say that adulteration of food items with chemicals or other harmful substances is a serious matter. If adulterated food items are found at any shop, action will be taken against the shop. Also, if adulteration is found in a warehouse or factory, action can be taken to seal it. Officials said - action will not be limited to just paneer According to departmental officials, adulteration will not be seen only as an analog dairy product. If any kind of adulteration is found in food items, action will be taken under the Food Safety Act. Officials say that inspections will be carried out from shops to warehouses and factories. Where adulteration is found, action will be taken at the respective level. Special monitoring will be done of those units where large quantities of paneer, khoya, ghee or other dairy products are prepared at low cost and sent to the market. Difference between adulterated paneer and analog paneer Adulterated Paneer: Paneer was prepared from milk, but another ingredient was adulterated into it. Analog Paneer: A product in which non-dairy ingredients are used in place of the main components of milk to give it a paneer-like appearance and use. This means there is a difference in both cases. In one, an authentic dairy product is adulterated, while in the other, a dairy product-like alternative is prepared from non-dairy ingredients. What will be the impact on shopkeepers and manufacturers? After the government's decision, the path for action against the manufacture, storage, and sale of such products has been cleared. The monitoring by Food Safety Department teams can increase from manufacturers to the supply chain and the market. Shopkeepers will also have to ensure that the paneer, khoya, ghee, chhena, or cream sold by them comply with the prescribed standards. At the manufacturer and supplier level, the product's ingredients and its actual nature will also be checked. Why is the government's decision important? This will directly affect businesses that prepare and sell dairy-like products made from non-dairy ingredients at low cost in the market. The government's objective is to prevent consumers from receiving such products in the name of dairy products, where other substances have been used instead of the main components of milk. This means it will no longer be sufficient to just see if a product looks like paneer or ghee in the market. It will also be important to know what ingredients it is actually made from. Discussion on Analog Products Already Underway in the Country Discussions at the regulatory level regarding analog dairy are already underway in the country. FSSAI has conducted stakeholder consultations on Analogue in Dairy Context. Additionally, surveillance drives have also been conducted for paneer and dairy analogs.

stories.title: IAS Rinku says Bhagat Singh would be called ‘foolish’ today:Remarks made during I-Day speech in Jalaun; DM and ADM were present
stories.summary: In Jalaun, SDM (Judicial) IAS Rinku Singh Rahi commented on the freedom movement and the revolutionaries involved in it. He said Bhagat Singh, by today's standards, was a foolish and useless child. He was a rebel from his family's perspective. “When I read history, a question arises in my mind: were farmers exploited by the British or by the Patwaris of our own country? Initially, only 1 per cent of people participated in the freedom movement. The rest were engaged in rituals according to their religion and their families.” There was an Independence Day program at 9 AM on Saturday in the Collectorate Auditorium in Orai. Rinku Singh was giving a speech there. During this, DM Rajesh Kumar Pandey, ADM Finance and Revenue Rajiv Raj, ADM Namami Gange Premchand Maurya, DPRO Ram Ayodhya Prasad, and EDM Pushpendra Singh were also present. Read what Rinku Singh said ‘Farmers were exploited by our own Patwaris’ “When I read history, it seems, who ultimately exploited the farmers? Was it the British or the Patwaris of our own country? The Patwari was a man from this very country. Did the British Collector at that time tell the Patwari to exploit the farmers? Or did the Patwaris bring in farmers to prove themselves good employees in front of their British officers and to achieve paper targets?” “History is full of stories of the exploitation of common people, including farmers. There were some British collectors and high-level officials, but most of the people working in the rest of the system were from our own country. Farmers were not exploited only by the British; our own people were also involved in it.” ‘Initially, only 1 per cent of people participated in the freedom struggle’ “If a correct assessment is made, perhaps not even 1 percent of people were directly involved in the freedom struggle initially. The rest of the people were engaged in their normal daily routines. They would wake up in the morning, perform rituals according to their religion, go to work, and spend time with their families.” “This idea came to some people's minds, and gradually the movement gained momentum. They understood that something had to be done for the country. After this, some people left their homes and joined the freedom struggle. Our traditional thinking has been 'us and our family'.” “Some people thought beyond this. They believed that even though they were born by their parents, they also had a responsibility towards humanity and the country. Such people left their wives, children, and parents to come forward for the country and made sacrifices.” ‘Bhagat Singh was a foolish and useless child’ “Didn't Bhagat Singh have a family? Didn't Chandrashekhar Azad have a family? If I compare it with today's times, it seems that Bhagat Singh was the most foolish and absolutely useless child. He was a rebel from the family's perspective.” “These were the rebellious people who stood with the country. They came forward for the country without caring for their families. Freedom was an idea that people understood and fought for.” “Today, we probably need that feeling even more, which Bhagat Singh must have had in his mind. He questioned whether Bhagat Singh, when working for the country, ever thought that a biographical sketch would be made on his life later?” ‘When a 30-year-old case came up, I felt ashamed’ “Yesterday, a case came up in court. It's a 30-year-old case. I felt ashamed. Would anyone have ever thought that an SDM would sit, and a 30-year-old case would come to him? I felt ashamed that I am betraying the freedom fighters in every way.” “Perhaps if they had known that the country would be like this in the future, they wouldn't have done it. They wouldn't have even imagined that there could be incompetent people like us. A case has been going on for 30, 35 years, just for a measurement! It can be easily resolved, but it's not happening. We are the reason.” There were many good officers even among the British “We are unable to understand what freedom was and why it was taken. Perhaps we have become one of those, who were more than 99 percent of the people. When the country was enslaved, we were living then, and we are living now.” “If we leave aside the British army, its job was to win somehow, to win by killing. But if we talk about the civil services, many of the collectors or other officers were also good people. They also wanted to do a lot of good. They brought new things.” Has been in discussion over controversies before Bar Association had raised questions on Rahi's working style On August 4, the Jalaun Bar Association had announced a boycott of revenue courts from August 5, raising questions about the working style of SDM (Judicial) Rinku Singh Rahi. Omanarayan Singh, Vice President of the Bar Association, had issued a letter in this regard. According to the letter, advocates had complained about Rinku Singh Rahi to District Magistrate Rajesh Kumar Pandey three times. The Bar Association alleged that Rahi talks about passing one-sided orders in court in the absence of advocates and litigants. Lawyers also accused him of misbehaving with them in court. Accusation of pushing BJP Block Head On June 29, Block Head Ramraja Niranjan had accused Joint Magistrate Rinku Singh Rahi of assault. He had also shown a video of it. In the video, Rinku Singh was seen pushing and shoving the Block Head. In the video, Rinku Singh was seen slapping the Block Head's mobile, causing the mobile to fall to the ground. After this, he pushed the Block Head back forcefully with both hands. The Block Head had complained about this to DM Rajesh Kumar Pandey. Know who Rinku Singh Rahi is Rinku Singh Rahi was born on May 20, 1982, in Hathras, into a Dalit family. He is a resident of Usawa village in Sasni police station area. Rinku, the elder of two brothers, had a father, Saudan Singh Rahi, who supported the family by running a flour mill. Due to the family's weak financial condition, he studied in a government school. After passing 12th grade with good marks, he received a scholarship. With its help, he completed B.Tech from Tata Institute in Jamshedpur. In 2004, Rinku Singh passed the PCS examination. Shot 7 times for exposing corruption After becoming a PCS officer, Rinku Singh's first posting in 2008 was as District Social Welfare Officer in Muzaffarnagar. There, he exposed corruption in scholarships and pensions. Rinku told Dainik Bhaskar - "During the investigation, I found out that 100 crore rupees had been embezzled. Behind this was an entire gang, in addition to a political party." At that time, the BSP government was in power. On March 26, 2009, Rinku was playing badminton with a colleague. That's when two attackers fired indiscriminately at him. Rinku Rahi was hit by seven bullets. Two of them hit his face. His jaw was dislocated, and his face was disfigured. Also, one ear was damaged, and the sight in one eye was lost. During his job, he appeared for the UPSC Civil Services Examination from the disabled quota. In 2021, he secured the 683rd rank and became an IAS officer.

stories.title: MLA Pallavi Patel meets Atiq Ahmed’s son in Prayagraj:Says family is grieving the loss of a son and this is not the time for politics
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, MLA Pallavi Patel met with Ahjam, son of mafia Atiq Ahmed. She reached Hatwa village around 4 PM on Friday evening. Here, she met Atiq Ahmed's family and offered condolences on the death of his son Aban. Pallavi, an MLA from Apna Dal (Kamerawadi), spoke with Atiq's family for a long time. During this time, she also met Atiq's brother Ashraf's sons and daughters. After the meeting between Pallavi and Atiq's family, political discussions have intensified. Photos and videos of this are also being shared on social media. Some users are viewing it as an act of human compassion, while others are making political comments on it. In fact, Pallavi's meeting with Atiq's family took place at a time when there is an atmosphere of grief in the house over Aban's death. Pallavi returned from Atiq's house at 6:15 PM. Pallavi Patel said- Such a great tragedy has occurred in the family. What's the harm in meeting that family? I met Ahjam and other family members. I consoled and reassured them. This meeting should not be seen from a political perspective. Pallavi asked about the status of Umar-Ali's cases Atiq's son Ahjam and aunt Parveen Qureshi are living in Hatwa village. On Friday, Pallavi Patel, MLA of Apna Dal (Kamerawadi) from Sirathu seat of Kaushambi, reached Ahjam's house with her supporters. Pallavi inquired with Ahjam about Omar and Ali, who are imprisoned. She asked about their cases and recent status. Additionally, she asked who all attended Aban's burial at the graveyard. During the meeting, Pallavi said that Atiq Ahmed had a very deep relationship with my father, Sonelal Patel. “Atiq was our party's state president. He won elections and was a public representative. I am meeting that family in their time of trouble. This is not the time for politics,” she said. Pallavi said this is not the time for politics Pallavi said, “When my father Sonelal Patel came to hold a rally in Civil Lines Park in Prayagraj, the police lathi-charged him. My father Sonelal Patel suffered fractures in his hands and feet. At that time, Atiq Ahmed, along with his supporters, reached the spot. He admitted my father to the hospital. Later, Atiq Ahmed became the state president of our party Apna Dal. He contested the election on the party's ticket and won.” At that time, an Apna Dal MLA also won in Pratapgarh. In Prayagraj, Apna Dal councilors were elected on about 30 seats. SP MLA also reached Hatwa Aban's body was brought to Hatwa village after post-mortem. On August 7, SP MLA RK Verma from Raniganj, Pratapgarh, also reached Hatwa to meet Atiq's family members. Here, he spoke with Atiq's family. RK Verma consoled Atiq's family and offered them comfort. When people questioned this meeting, the SP MLA had said, "What's the big deal? I had relations with that family even before. A tragic incident occurred, so I went there." Imran Pratapgarhi is also being trolled On the death of Atiq's son Aban, Congress Rajya Sabha MP Imran Pratapgarhi is being trolled the most on social media. Lewd comments are being made on Imran through photos, videos, and reels. On the stage of mushairas, Imran Pratapgarhi used to call Atiq Ahmed his elder brother and father-figure. Aban died after his car hit the divider Atiq Ahmed's youngest son, Aban, was going to meet his brother Ali, who is imprisoned in Jhansi jail, on August 6. He had 4 other friends in the Creta car. Aban was sitting in the front seat of the car. His friend Zaid was driving the car, while Sonu was sitting behind Aban. About 70 km before Jhansi, in the Poonch police station area, a speeding Creta car, after overtaking a pickup, lost control and hit the divider. The impact was so strong that the car was thrown about 10 feet into the air. Aban (21) and his friend Sonu had died in the accident. According to the post-mortem report, Aban's liver, lungs, and spleen ruptured due to the high-impact collision. His ribs were also broken. He died due to excessive internal bleeding. His companion Sonu, who was sitting behind Aban's seat in the car, died due to a fractured skull. On August 8, Aban was buried next to his father Atiq's grave in Prayagraj. His three brothers, Ali, Umar, and Ahjam, carried Aban's bier. Ali and Umar had received parole from the Allahabad High Court to attend their brother's funeral. Following this, the police brought Ali from Jhansi and Umar from Lucknow.

stories.title: Caste, COVID vaccine, bank accounts, voter/aadhaar: The big changes in census 2027
stories.summary: For the first time since Independence, India’s Census will record the caste of all respondents, making Census 2027 one of the most significant demographic exercises in the country’s history. The new questionnaire expands from 29 categories in Census 2011 to 40 questions and includes information on caste, digital literacy, Aadhaar, mobile numbers, bank accounts, voter IDs, passports and more. But why is the caste question creating political debate? How will the open-column system work? And what lessons has the government drawn from the 2011 Socio-Economic and Caste Census? In this explainer, we break down the biggest changes in Census 2027, why they matter, and what they could mean for policymaking, welfare schemes and representation in India.

stories.title: Mother keeps kissing severed head of five-year-old son:Child’s head and torso found 5 metres apart in Bahraich field; wild animal attack suspected
stories.summary: In Bahraich, on Friday evening at 6 PM, the mutilated body of a 5-year-old child was found. His head and torso were lying separately at a distance of 5 meters. Seeing her son's body, the mother fainted. After regaining consciousness, the mother, in a distraught state, held her son's severed head in her hands and kept kissing his face. Sometimes she would straighten the torso's legs, and sometimes she would try to reattach the severed head to the torso. The father also repeatedly tried to lift his lifeless child by holding his hand. The child had wandered off towards the sugarcane fields while playing. It is suspected that a wild animal attacked him there. The incident is from Chamaran Purwa village in Motipur police station area, about 65 kilometers from the district headquarters. Ranger K.K. Singh stated that marks of a wild animal attack were found on the child's shoulders and chest. In the initial investigation, it is suspected that the child's death was caused by a leopard attack. See pictures Details of the case Dilip lives with his wife Preeti and three children Kamini (8), Laggi (7), and Suraj (5) in Chamaran Purwa village, about 65 km away from the district headquarters. Dilip is a farmer. On Friday afternoon around 2 PM, Suraj, playing behind a village boy named Pappu, went towards the sugarcane field. A little while later, Pappu returned, but Suraj did not. The family members asked Pappu about Suraj. Pappu said that Suraj had come behind him, but on the way, he went towards some field. Subsequently, the family and villagers started searching for Suraj. Innocent's head and torso found after 4 hours He was searched for throughout the village and surrounding fields, but he could not be found for a long time. While searching, the villagers reached about 1 km away. After about four hours, at 6 PM, Suraj's slipper was found outside a sugarcane field. After this, the villagers entered the field. There, in the middle of the field, Suraj's headless body was lying. The head was about 5 meters away from the torso. Blood was scattered in the surrounding field. Seeing the dead body, the father fainted. People somehow managed to support him. When the father reached home with his son's body, the mother also fainted upon seeing it and fell to the ground. After regaining consciousness, she kept crying, holding her son's severed head in her lap. Seeing her in this state, the villagers present there could not hold back their tears either. Action to set up a cage in the area As soon as the incident was reported, teams from the forest department and police reached the spot. The police sent the innocent child's body to the mortuary for post-mortem around 1 AM. The forest department provided financial assistance of ₹10,000 rupees to the victim's family. Meanwhile, efforts are being made to set up a cage to catch the leopard.

stories.title: Four die after tractor-trolley carrying bricks overturns in Lucknow:Tractor flipped on divider, all four trapped and crushed
stories.summary: A major accident occurred in Gosain Ganj, Lucknow, early Saturday morning. A tractor loaded with bricks overturned on the Sultanpur Highway. In the accident, four people, including the driver, died. Three died on the spot, while one succumbed to injuries while being taken to the hospital. All four were residents of Barabanki. The accident happened in Gangaganj, Gosain Ganj, around 4:45 AM. Locals informed Gosain Ganj police about the accident following which the Fire Service and National Highway Authority (NHAI) team arrived at the scene. With the help of NHAI's crane, the trolley was removed, and then four people were seen trapped under the tractor. The tractor was also removed, and all four were pulled out. All were taken to CHC Gosain Ganj by ambulance. Here, doctors declared three people dead, while one person in critical condition was referred to the Trauma Center. The injured person died on the way while being taken to the Trauma Center. 3 pictures of the accident- All four people were residents of Barabanki According to the police, all four deceased were residents of Barabanki. One of them drove a tractor, and the other three loaded and unloaded bricks. The tractor involved in the accident currently operates at Deshraj's RBF brick kiln in Achkakamau, Kothi police station area, Barabanki. The deceased have been identified as Pitambar Rawat (35), Sandeep Rawat (25), Pawan Rawat (25), all residents of Ilichpur Majre Padrawan, Barabanki, and Balram Rawat (20), a resident of Sarayandar. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem. Relatives have also reached KGMU's post-mortem house after receiving the information. 20-year-old Balram's father said he was the sole earner Among those who lost their lives, 20-year-old Balram alias Ram Kishor's house is one kilometer away from the brick kiln. Father Ram Suresh told at the post-mortem house - Around 3 AM, a call came from the kiln saying that he had to go to work in the morning. He left with his younger brother Ram Naval. Ram Naval informed about this accident around 5 AM. When we reached the spot, we saw that my son had died. The family consists of a mother and five siblings. Balram was the sole earner of the family. With his passing, the whole house has fallen apart. If the Chief Minister provides financial assistance, it will be a support for us for a few days. Driver has one daughter, two sons; Pawan had a daughter 4 months ago The deceased Pitambar used to drive a tractor at the brick kiln. His family includes mother Rama Devi, wife Neelam, one daughter Shanti, and two sons Ankesh and Leelesh. Meanwhile, Pawan Rawat used to load and unload bricks at the kiln. Pawan's brother-in-law Sonu said that Pawan had started working with the deceased Sandeep just four days ago. His family includes brother Dinesh, mother Kusuma Devi, wife Sushma, and daughter Aarohi. The daughter was born in April this year. Meanwhile, the deceased Sandeep's brother Sunil said that he was the middle child among four brothers and three sisters.

stories.title: School canopy collapses, child dies:Watching Independence Day event in Sambhal; DM-SP rush to spot
stories.summary: A six-year-old child died after a canopy collapsed during an Independence Day programme at a private school in Sambhal on Saturday (15 Aug) morning. The incident occurred around 10am in the Asmoli police station area. Two other children were injured in the collapse and were taken to hospital for treatment. Children trapped under debris after canopy collapses An Independence Day programme was underway at the school when the incident took place. Several children had climbed onto the canopy while others were watching the programme. The structure suddenly collapsed, trapping several children underneath. People at the spot immediately removed the debris and rescued those trapped. However, six-year-old Nizamuddin suffered critical injuries and was declared dead. DM and SP rush to spot after receiving information A CCTV video of the incident has also surfaced, showing the canopy collapsing during the programme. Sambhal District Magistrate and Superintendent of Police immediately left an Independence Day event at the police lines and reached the school after receiving information about the accident. Police are investigating the circumstances that led to the canopy collapse. First see 2 pictures Children climbed canopy before collapse The incident took place at Al Hasnain Public School in Madala Fatehpur village on Saturday (15 Aug). Students from the village and neighbouring areas attend the school. After the Tricolour was hoisted, students began cultural presentations while children from nearby homes also gathered to watch the programme. During the event, some children climbed onto the canopy installed at the school's main gate. Canopy collapsed under the weight of children The canopy reportedly collapsed under the weight, trapping several children underneath. Local residents immediately removed the debris and rescued those caught beneath it. Nizamuddin, 8, son of Mohammad Naeem; Saif Ali, 11, son of Sabun; and Shaidana, 10, son of Imran, suffered serious injuries. All three were rushed to a Community Health Centre (CHC), where doctors declared Nizamuddin dead. DM, SP and BSA rush to school after canopy collapse As soon as information about the canopy collapse reached the administration, senior officials rushed to the school. SDM Vikas Chandra, CO Asmoli Aman Singh and Station House Officer Sudhir Panwar reached the spot first. District Magistrate Ankit Khandelwal and SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi also left an Independence Day programme at the police lines and reached the school. Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) Alka Sharma also visited the school and gathered details about the incident. Uncle says children had gone to watch flag-hoisting programme The child's uncle, Mohammad Subhan said, “Children from our family had gone to the school to watch the Independence Day programme.” He said, “The cousins had left home carrying flags for the celebrations, while some other children were standing on the rooftops around the school.” According to him, “When the structure collapsed, the child became trapped underneath and died in the accident.” Nizamuddin was only brother of two sisters Nizamuddin was a Class 3 student at Little Children Public School. On Saturday (15 Aug), instead of attending his own school, he went to his cousins' school in Madala Fatehpur to watch the Independence Day programme. According to the family, Nizamuddin left home around 9am and told them he was going to hoist the national flag. His father is a farmer. Nizamuddin was the only brother of two sisters, Fatima and Umama. The family said it did not want to pursue any action and had no demands from the government following his death. DM says assistance will be provided to family District Magistrate Ankit Khandelwal said, “The school was a private primary-level institution where an Independence Day programme was being held.” According to the DM, “Some children from nearby houses had climbed onto the school's canopy, while an eight-year-old child was standing beneath it. The canopy collapsed under the weight of the children, killing the child underneath.” DM further said, “Two other children suffered minor injuries and are undergoing treatment.” He added that assistance would be provided to the bereaved family. SP says school building was 19-20 years old Sambhal SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi said, “The bereaved family had been assured that all assistance available from the state government would be provided.” He added, “The family had declined to pursue any further action in connection with the incident. Two children injured in the collapse are receiving treatment.” SP attributes collapse to children climbing on canopy Bishnoi said, “The school building was around 19 to 20 years old and was not considered very old.” According to the SP, “The incident was not caused by a structural failure of the school building. The canopy collapsed after children from the neighbourhood climbed onto it, placing excessive weight on the structure.”

stories.title: VIDEO | Delivery boy beaten over 5-minute delay:Man drags him inside house and punches, kicks him in Meerut
stories.summary: A delivery boy was allegedly assaulted by a young man in Meerut on Friday (14 Aug) night after his order was delayed by just five minutes. The incident took place around 9.30pm at Ganga Heights, about 8km from the district headquarters. According to the complaint, the accused dragged the delivery worker into a room and beat him with kicks and punches. The accused's wife was also reportedly present during the assault. A CCTV video purportedly showing the incident has surfaced. Delivery workers stage sit-in, stop accepting orders More than 20 delivery workers reached Bhavanpur Police Station around 8am today (15 Aug) and staged a sit-in to protest the assault. The workers have also stopped accepting delivery orders, demanding the accused's immediate arrest. They said they would continue their protest until action is taken against him. Police said, “An FIR has been registered against the accused based on the delivery boy's complaint. The accused is reportedly an ICICI Bank manager.” See 3 pictures... 3.5-minute CCTV footage captures delivery boy being assaulted A 3.5-minute CCTV video showing the alleged assault of a delivery boy at Ganga Heights in Meerut has surfaced. The footage shows the delivery worker arriving outside Flat No. 110 at around 9.31pm on Friday (14 Aug) and ringing the doorbell. When the door opens, a young man comes out and an argument breaks out between the two. Woman seen outside flat during confrontation A woman then comes out of the flat and is reportedly the young man's wife. The man allegedly slaps the delivery boy around 10 times and punches him twice before taking him inside the flat. Around six minutes later, the delivery worker is seen coming out of the room and leaving the premises. Delivery boy alleges assault and false rape case threat over delayed order Delivery worker Amit Yadav said that the customer called him after the order was delayed by around five minutes. He stated, “I told the customer that the delay was five minutes, but the customer insisted it was already 15 minutes late.” He added, “I explained that the delay shown on the customer's app could be different and assured him that I would deliver the order as soon as it gets ready. The customer then told me to come to the flat, saying he would discuss the matter there.” Worker alleges phone was snatched, threatened with false case Amit alleged, “When I reached the flat, the accused began assaulting me and snatched my phone. He dragged me inside the room and continued beating me.” He added, “The accused told me that his wife is present and accused me of misbehaving with her. He threatened to implicate me in a rape case, claiming that I have harassed his wife.” Delivery worker says he is also studying Amit said, “I have been working as a delivery agent for around a year and I am currently studying in Class 12.” He also claimed that the man who assaulted him identified himself as an ICICI Bank manager. Delivery workers stopped work Delivery workers say that until action is taken against the accused, they will keep their IDs closed and will not deliver orders. Bhavanpur Station House Officer Joginder said, “Based on the complaint of victim Amit Yadav, his medical examination is being conducted. After this, a case will be registered and action will be taken.”

stories.title: BA LLB student dies by suicide in Gorakhpur:Body found hanging in room; police launches probe
stories.summary: A 21-year-old BA LLB student was found hanging from a ceiling fan in his room in Daudpur, Gorakhpur, on Friday (14 Aug) evening. The incident triggered panic among residents in the area. Police from Gulriha Police Station reached the spot after being informed and inspected the room. The body was taken into custody and sent for postmortem examination. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the death and trying to establish the reason behind the student's decision. Student was eldest of two brothers The deceased, Kumarvasva Sahni, a resident of Kevatahiya Tola in Jangal Dumri Number One under Gulriha police station limits, was living in Daudpur while pursuing his BA LLB. He was reportedly in his room around 4pm on Friday (14 Aug). Family members and nearby residents later discovered him and informed the police. Father works in Bengaluru, family in shock Kumarvasva was the eldest of two brothers. His father, Ramani Sahni, works in the paint and polishing business in Bengaluru. News of his son's death left the family devastated, with relatives reportedly inconsolable. The reason behind the suicide has not yet been established. Police said, “Further details are expected to emerge from the investigation and postmortem examination.”

stories.title: ITBP DIG dies in Saharanpur:SUV hits divider while returning from training in Mussoorie; driver also killed

One jawan was injured in the accident and is undergoing treatment at a medical college. ITBP DIG Parminder Singh, 48, and his driver Ravi Shankar were travelling towards Ambala in a Scorpio after returning from training in Mussoorie. Another jawan was also travelling with them. Near Sarsawa, the vehicle reportedly lost balance and collided with a divider. DIG and driver die at the scene The impact killed DIG Parminder Singh and driver Ravi Shankar on the spot. The jawan travelling with them was injured. After receiving information about the accident, police reached the spot and took the injured jawan to the medical college for treatment. Doctors declared the DIG and his driver dead. The injured jawan remains under treatment.

stories.title: Mandakini River swells in Chitrakoot, floodwater reaches home:Roof collapses in Sambhal, 7 trapped; minister reaches Unnao by steamer
stories.summary: Rainfall has caused rivers to swell across Uttar Pradesh. The Ganga, Yamuna, Sharda and eight other rivers have crossed their warning levels. In Chitrakoot, the water level of the Mandakini River has started rising, with floodwater reaching colonies and homes. The steps at Ramghat have been submerged, while Mandakini water is flowing over the Arogyadham bridge alongside the river. In Unnao, Ganga floodwater has entered homes, forcing residents to stay on rooftops. Boats are operating through the streets. On Friday, Minister of State for Higher Education and district in-charge minister Rajni Tiwari reached the flood-affected areas by steamer. In Varanasi, more than 100 small temples along the ghats have been submerged. The cremation area at Harishchandra Ghat has also gone under water. Heavy rain in Lucknow and surrounding areas Rain fell in Lucknow, Barabanki and nearby areas at around 6 am on Saturday. After nearly an hour of heavy rain, sunshine returned. In Sambhal, the roof of a house collapsed during the rain, trapping seven members of a family under the rubble. All seven have been admitted to hospital, with two reported to be in critical condition. Rain alert across all 75 districts A rain alert has been issued for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh today. Very heavy rainfall is expected in Banda, Mahoba, Jhansi and Lalitpur. On Friday, 53 cities, including Ghaziabad and Meerut, received rainfall. Low-pressure system to strengthen monsoon in UP According to Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh- The low-pressure area that formed over the north-west Bay of Bengal is moving westwards. It is passing through parts of Jharkhand and northern Chhattisgarh. As it moves further, it is gradually weakening. However, its influence will strengthen the monsoon over North India once again. Its widespread impact may also be felt across Uttar Pradesh, where heavy rainfall is possible.

stories.title: Young man dies after getting trapped under tractor wheel:Was taking lift to buy boondi for children on Independence Day
stories.summary: A 25-year-old man in Kannauj died after getting trapped between the wheel and mudguard of a tractor while taking a lift to buy boondi for children on Independence Day. The incident occurred around 8.30am today (15 Aug) in the Chibramau police station area. The man was travelling on the tractor when one of its wheels went into a pothole, causing the vehicle to bounce. He was thrown into the gap between the wheel and mudguard. Police and locals take 40 minutes to free trapped youth The impact left the youth's head on one side of the wheel and the rest of his body on the other. The tractor came to a halt after the wheel became jammed, while the driver abandoned the vehicle and fled. Police and local residents spent around 40 minutes trying to free the youth. He was rushed to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Villagers protest, demand driver's arrest Following the accident, the deceased's family members and villagers gathered at the spot and created a commotion, demanding the immediate arrest of the tractor driver. The victim's brother allegedly pelted stones at the tractor and later got into a scuffle with police personnel during the protest. First see 2 pictures... Know the complete matter... The deceased has been identified as Abhishek Kumar Rajput (25), son of Raghunath Rajput and a resident of Ghusuapur village. He worked as a farmer. He had gone out on Independence Day to buy boondi after children in his family asked for it. While travelling towards Karmullapur village, he saw a tractor passing by and decided to take a lift. The tractor had a large sound system installed, with the driver playing music at high volume. the man sat on the iron plate attached to the rear of the tractor. According to the available account, the driver then began driving the tractor at high speed. Youth trapped between tractor wheel and mudguard after pothole hit Near Karmullapur village on Rajipur Road, the tractor's wheel suddenly went into a pothole, throwing Abhishek into the air. In an attempt to prevent himself from falling, he reportedly placed his hand on the moving wheel and became trapped between the wheel and mudguard. Wheel jammed after youth became trapped, driver fled As Abhishek became trapped, the tractor's wheel jammed and the vehicle stopped. The driver abandoned the tractor and fled from the spot. On seeing the youth trapped, local residents gathered and began trying to rescue him. Police were also informed about the accident. Abhishek's head was visible on one side of the wheel, while the rest of his body remained trapped on the other side. After nearly 40 minutes of rescue efforts, police and locals managed to pull him out. He was taken to hospital by ambulance, where doctors declared him dead. Victim’s brother clashes with police as family demands driver’s arrest After news of the accident spread, Abhishek’s family members and villagers reached the spot and demanded the immediate arrest of the tractor driver. During the protest, Abhishek’s brother allegedly pelted stones at the tractor, leading to an altercation with police personnel. Police are now collecting information about the tractor’s owner and the driver involved in the accident. Family agrees to postmortem after assurance of action Former Sikandarpur Nagar Panchayat chairman Rajnikant Dubey and District Panchayat member Pramod Rajput also reached the spot and assured the family that appropriate action would be taken. Following the assurance, the family agreed to the postmortem. Police prepared the panchnama and sent Abhishek’s body for postmortem examination. Youth married two years ago, leaves behind four-month-old daughter Abhishek was the youngest of five brothers. He married two years ago in Tarpurwa village under the Gursahayganj Kotwali area and had a four-month-old daughter. According to his family, Abhishek worked as a farmer. After children at home asked for boondi today (15 Aug) morning, he left to buy it. He was also scheduled to go to the fields after returning home. Police tracing tractor driver Chhibramau Kotwali in-charge Kapil Dubey said, “Police were trying to trace the tractor driver. The body had been sent for postmortem and further action would be taken based on the complaint filed by the family.”

stories.title: Postal worker dies just 6 months after marriage:Bike skids while returning with sister; sibling cries holding his head in her lap
stories.summary: Abhishek Yadav (32), the acting in-charge of Purwa Post Office in Unnao, UP, died in a road accident. He was going home with his sister at 1 AM on Friday night when his bike lost control on a sharp turn and skidded on the road. It dragged for about 10 meters. However, his sister, a Lekhpal, who was sitting on the back seat of the bike, was thrown off and fell, narrowly escaping injury. Due to not wearing a helmet, Abhishek Yadav sustained serious head injuries. He was taken to the hospital with the help of passersby, where doctors declared him dead. Abhishek Yadav was married 6 months ago. Earlier, he was posted in Agra. He had taken a transfer to Unnao due to his marriage. Abhishek Yadav's sister is also a Lekhpal in Dubepur, Unnao. The accident occurred near the Ajit Kheda turn in the Achalganj police station area on Purwa Link Road, 20 kilometers from the district headquarters. See pictures Know the full story Abhishek Yadav was a resident of Piyariya Majra Neverna. He was employed in the postal department and was currently posted as the acting in-charge at Purwa Post Office. Previously, he was posted in Agra. On July 29, 2026, he was transferred from Agra to Purwa. It had only been 16 days since his new posting. According to family members, Abhishek Yadav was returning home on his bike with his sister Divya Yadav on Friday, when around 1 AM, his bike skidded near Ajitkheda Mod on Purwa Link Road, within the Neverna police outpost area under Achalganj police station limits. His sister Divya Yadav fell off the bike and narrowly escaped, while Abhishek was dragged about 10 meters on the road along with his bike. Due to severe head injuries, he died on the spot. Passersby rushed to the scene and saw Abhishek's sister Divya weeping with his head in her lap. Marriage took place just 6 months ago Abhishek was the eldest among three siblings. He was married to Shalu Yadav on February 24, 2026, this year. Not even six months had passed since the marriage. As soon as the news of Abhishek's death in the accident was received, his wife Shalu Yadav and other family members were inconsolable with grief. Achalganj Station House Officer Subrat Narayan said Late at night, a young man died in an accident near Ajitkheda Mod due to a bike skidding. The police received information from the district hospital. The body has been taken into custody and the panchnama proceedings have been completed. Post-mortem is being conducted. The causes of the accident are being investigated.

stories.title: UP CM hoists Tricolour on 80th Independence Day:Yogi Adityanath says,'Govt to soon launch 'Youth Policy'; urges fight against anarchy
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath hoisted the Tricolour at his residence on the occasion of 80th Independence Day. After hoisting the national flag Yogi Adityanath said, ‘On the occasion of Independence Day, I extend my heartfelt greetings to the people of the entire state. We all know that on this day in 1947, our country, India, attained independence after a long struggle marked by sacrifice and immense dedication’. He further added, ‘The sense of freedom that every Indian experiences today is the result of the sacrifice, penance and dedication of the great sons and martyrs of Bharat Mata. It is true that the country was enslaved because of internal divisions and conspiracies. However, our country and its people never accepted this slavery in their hearts or minds.’ He also made a major announcement for young people on Independence Day. Speaking in Lucknow, he said, “Our resolve is to ensure that every young person has skills, innovation and employment. That is why the government will soon introduce a ‘Youth Policy’. It will take an integrated approach to accelerate skills, innovation and employment opportunities for the youth of Uttar Pradesh.” Yogi said, 'The talent of our youth is Uttar Pradesh's real strength. We are turning our demographic dividend into an engine of development. New opportunities will be opened up for Gen Z and Gen Alpha in areas such as AI, machine learning and defence manufacturing. We are providing young people with interest-free and collateral-free loans under the ‘Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Yojana’.' The CM said- Prime Minister Narendra Modi says that if we want to overcome anarchy and illiteracy, we must remain vigilant against forces that seek to divide and weaken the country. He has made it clear that there are only four main castes in the country, the poor, youth, women and farmers. Therefore, when we work for them with dedication, the results will be even better. Yogi in traditional turban, Deputy CM in dhoti-kurta Earlier, the CM hoisted the national flag at the Vidhan Bhavan. Yogi arrived wearing a traditional turban, while Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak was seen in a dhoti-kurta. Yogi concluded the Independence Day celebrations by releasing Tricolour balloons into the sky with children. Tricolour celebrations across UP Across Uttar Pradesh, the Tricolour is flying from homes, shops and large buildings. Roads, roundabouts and government offices have been decorated with Tricolour streamers and flags. Patriotic songs are being played across the state, while flag-hoisting ceremonies are being held at various locations. In Agra, children took out a grand Tricolour march, while in Kashi, the Baba Vishwanath temple was decorated in a Tricolour-themed style. Photos of Independence Day celebrations-

stories.title: IAS officer who brought down Azam’s stronghold gets no extension:Moradabad DM given charge as he goes on leave; Akhilesh had brought him to UP
stories.summary: IAS Anjaneya Kumar Singh, who took on SP leader Azam Khan in several cases, has not received an extension of his deputation. His current term ended on Friday. Singh, who was serving as Moradabad Commissioner, handed over charge to DM Dr Rajendra Pensia and went on leave. The Appointment and Personnel Department has submitted a proposal to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath seeking an extension of Singh's deputation. However, the Chief Minister has not yet approved it. If Yogi approves the proposal, it will be sent to the Central Government. The Centre's Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) will then seek approval from the PMO. Once that approval is received, the Central Government will issue the order extending Singh's deputation. Singh is a Sikkim-cadre IAS officer. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav brought him to Uttar Pradesh at the request of then Union Home Minister Rajnath Singh. Since then, Singh has received seven consecutive extensions. Spent 8 years in original cadre, completed 11 years in UP Interestingly, 2005-batch IAS officer Anjaneya Kumar Singh spent only eight years in his original cadre, Sikkim. Meanwhile, he has completed 11 years of service in Uttar Pradesh. Counted among CM Yogi's trusted officers In 2015, on Rajnath Singh's recommendation, then Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav, who was heading the SP government, wrote to the Centre seeking Singh's deputation to UP. Later, on the recommendation of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, Singh continued to receive extensions to his deputation. Singh is among the prominent bureaucrats in Uttar Pradesh and has been regarded as one of CM Yogi's trusted officers. This is why the Centre granted him seven extensions on the recommendation of the Yogi government. Singh was the officer whose action following a controversial speech by Azam Khan in 2019 contributed to the SP leader's disqualification as an MLA. At the time, Singh was the District Magistrate of Rampur. During the 2019 Lok Sabha election campaign, Azam had said, "Don't be afraid of collectors and such, they are salaried employees... we don't fear salaried employees. If Allah wills, I will make them clean shoes." The remark proved costly for him. While serving as DM, Singh took several strict actions against Azam. Azam was sentenced to three years in prison, his first conviction in any case. Following this, the Uttar Pradesh Assembly Speaker cancelled his membership. Now read about Anjaneya Kumar Singh Anjaneya Kumar Singh is originally from Salahabad village in Mau district of Uttar Pradesh. After the Yogi government came to power, he was appointed Rampur DM on February 19, 2019. He remained in the post for two years. After his promotion, the state government appointed him Commissioner of the Moradabad division. He has remained posted there ever since. How the IAS officer took on Azam Khan's stronghold Singh became Rampur DM on February 19, 2019. He had told Dainik Bhaskar: "The elections were announced on March 11 itself. After becoming DM, some cases came before me in which I took action in the public interest. I will tell you about them one by one." First case — It concerned an unauthorised Urdu Gate built on a PWD road in Rampur. The illegal gate blocked the road. Singh retrieved the file and found that the previous DM had already ordered its demolition after completing the hearing in the matter. He called the SDM, PWD officials and police force and ordered its immediate demolition. The gate was subsequently demolished. Second case — This concerned a government electricity substation at Jauhar University. The public could not access the substation, which had been built on government land using public funds, because it had been enclosed within the boundary wall of Jauhar University. Singh had the power station freed from the alleged illegal occupation. Third case — This involved freeing Unani Hospital land from encroachment, on which Azam Khan's Rampur Public School was operating. During the investigation, it was found that, officially, the Rampur Public School was being run on land leased from Madrasa Alia. However, in reality, the school had been built on Unani Hospital land. Singh sent a police force on a holiday, had the school vacated and freed the Unani Hospital land, which he said had been deliberately shut down, from encroachment. Anjaneya also played a role in cancellation of Azam's son Abdullah's MLA election In the 2017 Assembly election, Azam Khan's son Abdullah was elected as an SP MLA from the Suar Tanda seat. Nawab Kazim Ali Khan, who contested the election against Abdullah on a BSP ticket, had sought cancellation of his election at the nomination stage, claiming that Abdullah was under 25 years of age. When the case came before Singh in 2019, he conducted an investigation. It found that Abdullah had contested the election using an allegedly false age certificate and was not 25 at the time of filing his nomination. The DM sent the report to the Election Commission, following which Abdullah's election was cancelled. IAS officers can normally remain on deputation for a maximum of 5 years An IAS officer normally cannot remain on deputation for more than five years. IAS officers can also change their cadre only under special circumstances and with the approval of the Central Government's Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT). Cadre changes may be considered to keep spouses together after marriage or in cases involving serious personal circumstances, such as illness or other significant reasons. A formal request for a cadre change is required, followed by the consent of both states and approval from the Central Government.

stories.title: No LPG cylinder without e-KYC in UP:Domestic consumers may have to pay double; know deadline and complete process
stories.summary: In UP, domestic gas cylinders will no longer be available without e-KYC. Nor will the subsidy come. This rule applies to both old and new customers. Ujjwala connection holders also need to get e-KYC done. No final date has been set for this yet. But if e-KYC is not done for a long time, the connection may also be blocked. The good thing is that there is no need to go to the gas agency for e-KYC. You can do e-KYC from home in a few minutes using a mobile app. How to do this, which app is needed, and what things to keep in mind? Let's find out e-KYC will be done from mobile in 5 minutes at home For e-KYC, download the official app of the gas company you are using. Indane, HP or Bharat Gas app can be found on Google Play Store. Complete the process by selecting the e-KYC option given in the app. If face authentication fails, don't panic There is no need to panic if face authentication fails. Reopen the app and repeat the face verification process. Ensure that there is sufficient light on your face and keep the mobile stable. After face scan, be sure to check the 'e-KYC Success' status in the app. Do not assume that merely by completing the face scan, e-KYC is complete. If the status does not show 'Success', then confirm the e-KYC status in your consumer record with the gas agency. 2 options for offline e-KYC If any customer is facing problems completing the process through the mobile app, then they also have other options - 1. By visiting the gas agency: You can get biometric authentication done by visiting your nearest gas agency. 2. By cylinder delivery man: When the delivery person comes home to deliver the cylinder, biometric authentication can also be done through the official device available with them. e-KYC's last date is not August 16 News reports stating August 16 as the last date for e-KYC are incorrect. Such news is circulating on social media and at the local level, but according to gas agency representatives and departmental guidelines, no final date for e-KYC has been set. The e-KYC process will continue. Both old and new customers can update their information. However, rules are in place regarding receiving cylinders without e-KYC, so customers should complete e-KYC as soon as possible. Focus on removing fake gas connections The government aims to identify and remove fake gas connections from the system. Through biometric and Aadhaar verification, it is being ensured that the subsidy money reaches the correct beneficiary and is not misused. The entire e-KYC process is completely free. Do not pay any person or agent for it. Rules related to gas cylinder delivery also changed The central government has also changed the rules related to cylinder booking. According to the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, in cities, a second cylinder can now be booked only 25 days after taking the first one. Earlier, this gap was 21 days. Whereas, in villages, the second booking can be done only after 45 days. For the delivery of a 14.2 kg domestic gas cylinder, merely showing the booking or receipt will no longer be sufficient. An OTP will be sent to the registered mobile number at the time of booking the cylinder. This OTP will have to be told to the gas agency employee at the time of delivery. The cylinder will be given only after the OTP is verified. The purpose of this is to prevent hoarding and black marketing of gas.

stories.title: Azam’s wife says, ‘They branded me as dacoit overnight’::No rules broken to build university; 'Are DM-SSP homes’ maps approved?
stories.summary: After retiring as a professor, when I started looking after the university's affairs, 60–70 cases were filed against me overnight. I was suddenly branded a thief and a dacoit. Every crime committed by criminals was linked to me. Saying this, SP leader Azam Khan's wife, Tanzim Fatima, became emotional. She said that as far as the approval of the building map was concerned, even the maps of the DM and SSP's houses were not approved. She added that Jauhar University was built before the Rampur Development Authority was established, so no rules were violated. Will Azam Khan contest the election? Tanzim Fatima says, "I have never advised Azam Sahab to leave politics." She added that Jauhar University is a greater achievement for him than politics. In an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Tanzim Fatima also responded to questions about the allegations that Akhilesh Yadav has not fully supported Azam Khan. Read the full interview. You have received a notice to demolish 38 buildings of Jauhar University. What would you say? The Rampur Development Authority (RDA) was established in 2005. At that time, Singankheda village, where the university is located, was outside the RDA's jurisdiction. In 2015, a new notification was issued bringing Singankheda under the RDA's jurisdiction. When the university was built, the area was not under the RDA's jurisdiction. So how could the Authority have approved the building map for the area? If the court's decision goes against you, what would you consider to be the shortcoming? This is purely a political issue. Hundreds of people live in Singankheda village apart from the university, and no one's house has an approved map. Look at Rampur or other cities, even the official residences of the DM and SP do not have approved maps. If the administration takes action, it will be seen as an attempt to destroy an educational institution. Dozens of cases have been registered against your family. How do you view this? This is purely political vendetta. Before entering politics, I was a professor at a degree college. No one questioned my honesty until I retired. But after retirement, when I took over the university's affairs, 60–70 cases were registered against me. Overnight, I became a thief and a dacoit. It is alleged that Akhilesh Yadav did not fully support Azam Khan. Is that true? No, this is incorrect. Akhilesh Yadav and the entire SP have stood by us. The party has provided us with full support in every way. Shivpal Singh Yadav himself went to meet Azam Sahab in jail and also held a press conference. Mulayam Singh Yadav also made a major contribution to the construction of this university. If the administration considers a police camp necessary on the university campus for security, what will you do? Around two or three years ago, the police entered the campus without permission. They neither sought permission from the Vice-Chancellor nor from anyone else. The police ransacked our rooms and records and took away whatever items they wanted. At the time, we approached the High Court. The court ordered that the police could not enter the campus without permission. If there is a police camp on every university campus, then we have no objection. Many obstacles arose during the construction of the university. How much cooperation did local people provide? Yes, it was a test because some people continuously created problems. But local people provided a great deal of support in building the university. Children and students from Rampur worked here themselves. They helped construct the university by carrying bricks, stones, cement and soil on their heads in the scorching heat. Is children's education being affected by the action taken against the university? Yes, education is definitely being affected. There are many expensive schools in Rampur where the fees are very high. People from poorer sections of society cannot afford such fees. Azam Sahab established Rampur Public Schools keeping in mind the poverty, illiteracy and economic condition of the people of Rampur. At present, an RPS school is operating, although its building is under a stay order, and some children are studying there. The fees can be compared with those of other schools. This will show how beneficial these schools were for children from poor families. What is Azam Khan's biggest achievement — politics or Jauhar University? Certainly, Jauhar University is his biggest achievement. Rampur was a very backward district in terms of education. While serving as an MLA and MP 10 times, Azam Sahab gave priority to education alongside development. He opened Rampur Public Schools for orphaned children from poor and labouring families, where CBSE education was provided for just ₹20 a month. The government had those schools vacated, which harmed the orphaned children. Will Azam Khan contest elections again or distance himself from politics? Whether Azam Sahab will contest elections again or not, only time will tell. At present, our effort is to secure his release from jail. I have never advised him to leave politics. However, politics 20–25 years ago was not like it is today. Back then, during Eid and Bakrid, leaders of opposition parties and government officials would visit each other's homes. That era is now gradually disappearing from politics. Stay on demolition of 38 university buildings maintained A hearing was held on August 13 in the Commissioner's Court in Moradabad against the order to demolish 38 buildings of Jauhar University. After the hearing, the court of Divisional Commissioner Anjaneya Kumar Singh upheld the interim stay imposed on July 27 against the Rampur DM's demolition order.

stories.title: Ganga changes course, school submerged in Badaun:Villagers say they had to relocate 2–4 km after every flood; now no land is left
stories.summary: The rising Ganga river in Badaun is becoming dangerous. In just five minutes, strong currents engulf the entire government school building in Kadmanagla village, leaving only a few walls. Students have been transferred to a primary school in another village, but families trapped by the flood are unable to send their children to school. Standing crops across around 1,000 bighas are submerged after the Ganga changes course. Villagers move to safer places as their homes and fields go underwater. Villagers say the river is rapidly eroding the land, and this is not the first time. The village has been washed away and merged into the river three times before. Residents rebuilt their homes in fields after moving away from the river, but there is now not enough farmland to accommodate so many families. This time, the village itself is on the verge of disappearing. People in panic, did not put roofs on their houses Kadmanagla village is about 40 km from Badaun district headquarters. Nearby are several villages including Raipura, Damnagla, and Jata. Currently, all these villages are in the grip of floods and erosion. There is no paved road left to reach these villages. People are commuting through unpaved and pothole-filled roads. Even these are filled with 1 to 2 feet of water. There are about 100 houses in villages like Kadmanagla, Damnagla, and Raipura, none of which are two-storied. Most people haven't even put roofs on their houses. When asked the reason, they say, There is always a fear that the flood in the Ganga might wash away our houses at any time. That's why we have only built enough to shelter our heads. Village washed away twice We met Ram Singh in Kadmanagla village. He says their earlier settlement, Kheda Pukhta, was submerged in a Ganga flood in 1965. The river receded after eroding the land but changed its course, forcing villagers to settle on the other side, where they named the village Kadmanagla. They lived there for 10 years before another flood reached their homes and eroded the land again. The villagers then moved to their own fields, where they have lived for around 20 years. Now, the Ganga has changed its course for the third time, flooding the entire village and rapidly eroding the land. The strong current has once again left residents frightened. 'Grandfather, father and we saw floods, now we won't let our children suffer this' Villager Ram Singh says, Until now, we kept moving towards our fields, but now behind us are the villages of Farrukhabad, our field has also been cut, now we don't understand where to go? My grandfather, father, and we have seen the crisis of floods, now we don't want our children to suffer it, we just want them to go anywhere and work as laborers, but leave this place. ‘This is all Ganga’s grace’ Ninety-year-old Kripal Singh Yadav, the oldest resident of the village, says, ‘This is all the grace of Mother Ganga.’ When asked how he could call it a blessing after losing both his home and farmland to erosion, he says, ‘What else can I say? What is destined is happening.’ He says villagers have no basic facilities and are somehow making a living. Government officials visit, inspect the situation and leave. With their farmland disappearing, many residents have also started going out to work as labourers. 'We just think that if a dam is built, then the lands will be saved' 38-year-old Amit Yadav's house is currently just 100 meters away from the river. He says that we studied outside, kept looking for a job, when we didn't get a job, we came back here. After all, even if we leave, where would we go? Regarding the future, we only think that if the government builds a dam here, and our fields are saved, then our situation will improve. Flooded school shifts 41 students The Upper Primary School in Kadamanagla village is now submerged in the Ganga. Its 41 students are shifted to Damangala Primary School, 2 km away, which already has 43 students and two teachers. The same teachers now teach students from Classes 6 to 8. The school is also affected by flooding, with only around 20 children attending. Teacher Dilshad Hussain says Kadamanagla had no permanent teacher even earlier, with a teacher from another school assigned there. After the school collapses, the remaining students are taught by him and the principal. Only 2–3 children from Kadamanagla attend because of the flood, and teachers sometimes drop them home on bikes. Dilshad says he was earlier posted in Sonbhadra, where even village roads were paved, but Kadamanagla has no proper roads. After explaining the situation, he rides through 3 feet of floodwater on his bike towards the nearest town, with the bike barely able to move. 'Officials came, but no one did anything' Village head Rakesh Kashyap says, Hundreds of bighas of land in our village have been submerged in the river this year. Now, 10 to 15 meters of land are eroding and submerging into the river every day. There are currently about 25 houses in the village. All are under threat. The SDM came twice, and officials from the flood division also came. They also said that if the water level decreases, we will consider building a dam. Jitendra, standing next to the head, says, Officials do come, but they look and then leave. It would be very good if there was a system to stop the erosion. We don't have jobs, if the land is saved, we will be able to feed our children.

stories.title: Bride flees on fifth day of marriage:Runs off with ₹11 lakh in jewellery and cash; middleman threatens to frame groom’s family in case
stories.summary: A bride fled from her in-laws’ house in Agra just five days after the wedding, taking jewellery and cash worth ₹11 lakh with her. The husband and his family contacted the matchmaker, hoping he might know where she had gone. However, the family alleges that instead of helping them, the middleman threatened to implicate them in a case for allegedly making the woman disappear. According to the family, matchmaker had portrayed the woman as being from a financially weak background and persuaded them to agree to the marriage, saying it would help her build a better life. After the bride disappeared, the husband and his family approached the police to lodge a complaint, but alleged that their complaint was not initially accepted. An FIR has now been registered following a court order. Now, complete matter in detail Guddi Devi, a resident of Awas Vikas Colony Sector-14 in Agra, said that I have three sons. My youngest son Rahul is already married. The search for a match for my eldest son Vishnu's marriage was ongoing. The elder son does flower decoration work. She was looking for a girl for his marriage. She met Jawahar Singh, a resident of Shamsabad. He told her - There is a poor girl named Preeti who lives in Prayagraj. She doesn't have a father. I know her brother. You just have to bear the expenses from both sides. She agreed to the marriage after being convinced by his words. Wedding took place on 27th June Guddi Devi alleges that the young woman's brother, Dhara Singh, demanded ₹1.5 lakh in the name of buying wedding items. The family transferred ₹1 lakh in cash and ₹50,500 online. On 27th June 2026, the wedding rituals were completed at the woman's house, and Preeti started living in the house as a daughter-in-law. Bride suddenly disappeared after 5 days 5 days after the wedding, on the morning of 3rd July, the mother-in-law called her daughter-in-law Preeti for tea. But she was found missing from the house. Guddi Devi said that she searched for her daughter-in-law everywhere. But nothing was found. When checked at home, 4 tolas of gold and 1 kg of silver jewelry were missing. These include two mangalsutras, three gold rings, a silver waistband, and anklets. She also stole ₹16,000 from the ‘Muh dikhai’ ceremony and the younger daughter-in-law's gold ring, mangalsutra, payal, and ₹15,000. The matchmaker Jawahar, said on the phone that you people should not complain to the police. I will bring the girl back. For many days, there was no response from him. Then, he started threatening that he would implicate them in a case of making the girl disappear. After this, the family went to Sikandra police station to file a complaint, but said that the police did not hear their case. An FIR was eventually registered following a court order. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said, “Action is being taken based on the evidence. Efforts are underway to trace the bride, who is accused of theft. The matchmaker who arranged the marriage is also being traced.”

stories.title: Yogi tells athletes, 'Win medals, we’ll give jobs':Those who chant 'youth-youth' have no agenda for youth, only mafias
stories.summary: CM Yogi Adityanath arrived at Gorakhnath Temple to watch the wrestling competition organized on the occasion of Nag Panchami in Gorakhpur on Monday afternoon at 3 PM. CM Yogi told the players that we are directly giving jobs to those who win medals for the country. So far, 500 players have been given jobs. The CM said- Today some people are shouting youth-youth, but youth is not in their agenda. They just want to use you. When they were in power, they did nothing for the youth and handed everything over to the mafia. Before this, CM Yogi performed worship of Guru Gorakhnath at Gorakhnath Temple. He went to the samadhi site of Brahmaleen Mahant Avaidyanath and took his blessings. After this, he watched the wrestling matches of the wrestlers. He honored the winning wrestlers. In the presence of the CM, the title matches of Uttar Pradesh Kesari, Uttar Pradesh Kumar and Uttar Pradesh Veer Abhimanyu were held. More than 300 wrestlers participated in this two-day state-level competition. See 2 pictures CM said- If you engage in sports, you will stay away from drugs CM Yogi said that the more youth engage with sports, the more they will stay away from addiction. There are two forms of addiction. One is drugs and intoxicating substances, while the other is smartphone addiction. Today, 90% of the time youth spend on smartphones is wasted. If even one hour from the time spent on smartphones is dedicated to the body, then the body will remain healthy. If the body is healthy, then the mind will also remain healthy. This will enable youth to contribute to making the nation stronger. The first rule for an athlete is self-discipline. They wake up and sleep on time. They follow dietary rules. Old coaches prepared athletes by tempering their lives even with limited resources and without incentives. Today, all kinds of facilities are available for athletes. Government will also help private sports academies; new youth policy soon The CM said that the UP government is soon bringing a new youth policy. Under this, many events and programs will be started for the youth. 'Abhyudaya Coaching' for youth preparing for competitive exams will be extended to every college and university. This facility will be available through both physical and virtual mediums. A 'Skilling and Employment Zone' is being created in every district of the state. Here, under one roof, along with skilling of youth, employment facilities will also be available. If the private sector cooperates in any field of sports, then full support will be provided to it under the state government's sports policy. Strictness against those who play with the future of youth Yogi said that if the copying mafia or education mafia plays with the future of any youth, strict action will be taken against them. Action is also being taken to confiscate the property of such people. He mentioned the sports talents of Ghazipur, saying that Olympic medal winners Lalit Upadhyay and Rajkumar Pal have progressed from Ghazipur's private stadium. He said that this shows that better sports facilities and private academies can play a crucial role in advancing youth. Education, sports and protecting youth from drug mafia is necessary The CM said that old players, wrestlers and coaches dedicated their lives to sports with limited resources and without encouragement. If they had received adequate facilities and encouragement at that time, they could have taken the country's name even further at the international level. He said that sports and youth were not on the agenda of previous governments. Today some people are shouting youth-youth, but while in power they did nothing for the welfare of youth. They handed over the youth power to the mafia. 'Mafia mentality is the biggest enemy of youth power' CM Yogi said that mafia mentality is the biggest enemy of youth power. Whether it is education mafia, sports mafia, drug mafia, or professional criminals, youth suffer the most because of this. To protect youth from this, it is necessary to promote sports and sports culture. The double engine government under the leadership of PM Narendra Modi is working to create a positive environment for sports and youth. He said that a wrestler follows discipline and a sattvic lifestyle. He is also a devotee of Bajrangbali, from whom strength, intelligence, and knowledge are sought..

stories.title: Woman cop who arrested Muskan in 'blue drum case' suspended:Shared videos promoting QR code, was posted at Meerut SSP office
stories.summary: The female inspector who arrested Muskan, accused of dismembering her husband in Meerut, has been suspended. A video related to the officer surfaced on social media on Sunday, following which action was taken against her. The officer, Anu, is originally from Prayagraj and belongs to the 2023 batch of Sub-Inspectors. At the time of the Blue drum case, she was posted at Brahmpuri police station. She was later transferred to the SSP’s office. Anu’s first posting in Meerut was at Rohta police station. Pictures related to the female inspector on social media... YouTuber complained about inspector Anu, says, Yogiji, please A YouTuber had complained about female inspector Anu's objectionable posts on social media. He also released a video to make his point. In which he says- Yogi ji, namaste. Yaar, you can say whatever you want; you are the cutest person. Yogi ji is my most favorite Prime Minister. I mean, it came out wrong from my mouth, but you think about it, I'm going in the right direction, right? Not 29, so what, 34. You'll have my full support, sir. Sir, I wanted to show you a video. Look at this video. I know, Yogi ji, it's the wrong video, and you have a right to be angry. You basically don't pay any attention at all to all these things. This video is of Annie Collis, who is a Sub Inspector in the Uttar Pradesh Police. She has Instagram and YouTube channels. She posts reels on them. Some objectionable videos also appear on the YouTube channel. A QR code is also visible along with it. Basically, for donations. You understand the purpose, don't you? This uniform of Uttar Pradesh- if something could be done about its dignity. Now, our DGP sahab, Rajeev Krishna ji. I mean, our country's most important state. One of the most important states is Uttar Pradesh, and its police. If someone sees it, sir. I'm saying, if Haryana police see that, brother, QR codes of Uttar Pradesh police are running at night. I mean, they make a lot of fun on WhatsApp groups internally. You have rules and regulations, right? Steps should be taken against them. There is power; I mean, I don't have it, that's why I allow everything. Do it on Instagram, do it on YouTube too. Just what happens is that the dignity of the uniform falls a little. Yogi ji, Rajiv Krishna ji, let me tell you one thing. Just issue a simple circular, a notification, that police personnel or bureaucrats who are in high positions, who are in good important, significant positions. They should not be allowed to do such dramas on social media or do all this on social media. It looks wrong. It's disrespectful. Whether you believe it or not, dignity falls. Respect falls.
