stories.title: 16-year-old kills father, then dies after jumping before metro:Angry over restrictions; mother lived separately in Noida
stories.summary: A 16-year-old boy allegedly killed his father while he was asleep in Noida and later died by suicide after jumping in front of a Metro train, police said. After the alleged killing, the teenager changed his blood-stained clothes, placed a photograph of his father in the room and offered a garland as a tribute. He then locked the room, took his father's mobile phone and bag, and went to a Metro station. After spending some time at the station, he jumped in front of a train. Police found his father's mobile phone and the room key in the teenager's bag. They contacted his mother, who arrived at the spot along with the boy's uncle. During questioning, the family told police that the teenager lived with his father, while his mother lived separately in Noida. Father found dead inside locked room The police took the boy's mother and uncle to the room on Thursday night. They opened the door with the key and found the body of 45-year-old Raju Sharma inside. Initial investigation suggested that Raju had imposed several restrictions on his son's movements. He had also stopped the boy's studies after Class 11. Police suspect that the teenager was distressed by these restrictions and allegedly killed his father early on Wednesday, August 12. He died by suicide at around 7am the same day. The incident took place in the Phase 3 police station area of Noida. Raju was a private tutor. He had divorced his wife 12 years ago and had been living with his only son. Raju lived in Noida for 21 years Raju was originally from Bokaro Steel City in Jharkhand. His father had worked for SAIL. Raju moved to Noida with his wife in 2005. He later lived with his only son in a rented room in the Ajnara Society area. He held an MCom degree and taught children through private tuition and online classes. Blood stains found inside room Police said the teenager's body was found near a railway line on Wednesday. During a search, officers found his father's mobile phone and the room key in his bag. Police used the mobile phone to contact his mother, who arrived and identified her son's body. Raju's brother, Arun Sharma, also reached the spot and told police that his brother was missing. The police questioned the mother, who said Raju had a short temper and had imposed several restrictions on his son. She said the teenager was often upset by them. This led police to suspect that the teenager might have killed his father before taking his own life. Police then took the mother and uncle to Raju's room. A strong smell was coming from inside. When they opened the door, they found Raju's body. Blood-stained clothes believed to belong to the teenager were found inside the room, along with blood stains on the walls. A forensic team collected samples from the scene, while the blood-stained clothes were sent to a laboratory for examination. Neighbours noticed little interaction between father and son Neighbour Kaushal said he rarely saw the teenager outside the house. The boy mostly stayed indoors and was only occasionally seen when he went upstairs to dry clothes. Ram Avtar Tiwari, another resident of the building, said the father and son rarely spoke to each other. He said the teenager prepared his own food and collected water himself. The father and son would generally exchange things only when necessary.

stories.title: Computer operator beaten to death:Names attackers in video before dying; FIR against 6, including former block chief and ration dealer
stories.summary: A computer operator with the Supply Department in Pratapgarh was beaten to death. At around 7 pm on Thursday, he was returning home from work when the accused, who were lying in wait, attacked him with sticks, iron rods and the butt of a revolver. The attackers fled after leaving him, believing he was dead. Family members reached the spot after being informed by local residents and took him to hospital. Doctors declared him dead. Before his death, the computer operator named six attackers, including a former block chief. A video of his statement has also surfaced. The incident took place in the Lilapur police station area, around 15 km from the district headquarters. Based on a complaint by the family, police have registered an FIR against six named accused, including the former block chief and his brother, who is a ration dealer. The 32-year-old computer operator, Saurabh Vishwakarma, got married a year ago. He has a four-month-old daughter. His wife, Aanchal, broke down after seeing her husband's body. Here is the full case in sequence Saurabh Vishwakarma (32), a resident of Sindhora village in the Lilapur police station area, worked as a contractual computer operator in the Supply Department. He was the youngest of three brothers. His elder brother Sushil Vishwakarma drives a taxi, while his other brother Sonu Vishwakarma is a farmer. According to the family complaint, Saurabh was returning home from the Supply Office in Lalganj between 7 pm and 7.15 pm on August 13. When he reached around 150 metres beyond Gajadhar Inter College, Saurabh Tiwari (32), Daroga Tiwari (30), Sonu Tiwari (30), Anuj Tiwari (32) and others surrounded him. The accused brutally assaulted him. Hearing Saurabh's cries for help, local residents reached the spot. They informed Saurabh's friends Sonu Upadhyay and Shubham Pandey about the incident. Both reached the spot and took Saurabh to the Medical College for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. As soon as the incident was reported, ASP Brijnandan Rai reached the spot with a police team and took details of the incident. Police have been deployed in the area in view of the tension. Read full news in chronological manner Before dying, he said: They hit me with a gun butt and broke my leg Before his death, the computer operator said, "Daroga Tiwari and the son of his brother Bade Tiwari, along with 8-10 people, beat me with sticks. They hit my neck with the butt of a gun and also broke my leg." Family says accused had opened fire at their house four months ago The family said Sanjay alias Bade Tiwari is the former block chief of Laxmanganj, while his brother Sonu Tiwari is a ration dealer. The accused allegedly developed a grudge after Saurabh refused to approve a ration card-related work for Sonu. Four months ago, the accused had also allegedly fired 6-7 rounds at their house. The family said Saurabh was killed because of this dispute. Father-in-law demands encounter of accused Saurabh's father-in-law, Sajjan Vishwakarma, said, "Our demand is that all the accused should be arrested. After their arrest, they should be killed in an encounter and their houses should be demolished with bulldozers. Saurabh's wife should be given a government job. The government should also provide financial assistance for his four-month-old daughter." Friends took him to the hospital Hearing Saurabh's screams after the attack, people from the vicinity reached the spot. They informed his friends Sonu Upadhyay and Shubham Pandey about the incident. Both reached the spot and took Saurabh to the medical college for treatment, where doctors declared him dead. A video from before Saurabh's death has also surfaced. In it, he has also named the accused and said- Daroga Tiwari and his brother Bade Tiwari's son, along with 8-10 people, assaulted me with sticks. They hit my neck with a rifle butt and also broke my leg. Firing at home four months ago Family members said that Sonu Tiwari, brother of former block head Bade Tiwari of Laxmanpur, who is a ration dealer. The accused had harbored enmity after Sonu's ration card work was not approved. About four months ago, the accused had also fired 6-7 rounds at their house. Due to this animosity, the accused have murdered Saurabh. Police force deployed, body sent for post-mortem Considering the tension in the area after the incident, police force was deployed. ASP Brijnandan Rai reached the spot with the police team and gathered information about the incident. The body was taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. Brijnandan Rai informed that a case has been registered based on Saurabh's complaint. It is a case of old enmity. The accused are being searched for. One accused, Daroga Tiwari, was arrested on Friday morning.

stories.title: Student reaches police outpost over no teaching at school:Says, 'Ma’am keeps using phone, what will happen to our future?'
stories.summary: In Kanpur Dehat, a 12-year-old seventh-grade student reached the police outpost with a complaint about not being taught. He told the outpost in-charge, "Teachers don't teach, they use their phones all day. Older students beat younger children, and children keep playing in the ground." He asked, What will happen to our future? The policemen were surprised to hear the student's words. A head constable took him to the school. In front of the police, the female teacher started scolding the student and threatened to beat him. The police explained to the teacher and advised her not to do so. The incident took place on August 10, around 12 noon. The video of the incident surfaced on Thursday. The student studies in the seventh grade at a government school in Rasdhan, about 30 km from the district headquarters. On the instructions of the BSA, a notice has been issued to the headmaster and the accused teacher. See pictures Know full story Sanjeev Mishra, a resident of Rasdhan, is a farmer. He has five children - four sons and one daughter. 12-year-old Madhav is the fourth child. He studies in the seventh grade at the government composite school in the village. On August 10, Madhav reached the Rasdhan police outpost in his school uniform. The policemen were surprised to see him. When asked the reason for coming to the outpost, he said that he had come to complain about his school. Madhav said that there is no studying in school. Teachers are busy using their phones. Children keep playing in the ground all day. Older students beat him up frequently. No action is taken even after complaining. I am very troubled. He said that when he left school for the outpost, the madam was still talking on the phone. After hearing the student's complaint, the head constable of the outpost took him to the school. In front of the police, the teacher threatened the student A conversation took place between the student and teacher Saima Khan in the presence of policemen at the school. The police asked the teacher about the student's complaint. During this, the teacher started scolding the student and threatening to hit him. The policemen made a video of the incident. Read conversation between the student and the teacher Teacher: Why did you go to the police? Whatever the problem is, tell me directly. Student: You don't listen. Who should I tell? Teacher: We don't listen? I will hit you so much right now, I will beat you until your mind is set straight. When the teacher flared up, policemen stopped her from talking to the child in that manner. After pacifying both of them, the policemen returned. Investigation on BSA's instructions, Notice to Headmaster and Teacher After the video surfaced, on the instructions of BSA Ashish Pandey, the Block Education Officer (BEO) reached the school and investigated. He spoke to students and school staff and submitted his report to the BSA. Based on the report, the BSA issued show-cause notices to Headmaster Anupam Kumar and teacher Saima Khan. Both have been summoned to the BSA office for clarification. According to the BEO, some students had beaten the complainant student. He went to the teacher to complain about it, but at that time the teacher was talking on the phone and did not listen to him. Annoyed by this, the student reached the police outpost. Outpost In-charge said - The complaint was about lack of studies Rasdhan Outpost In-charge Prashant Singh said- A child had come to the outpost with a complaint. The outpost's constable took him to school. The child was complaining about the lack of studies in school. The matter was not serious, but the way the teacher scolded the child in front of the police personnel was wrong. BSA said - There was a dispute among children Basic Education Officer Ashish Pandey said- There was a dispute among the children. The police post is right next to the school, so the child went there. The Block Education Officer went to the spot and investigated. The child's parents were also called to the school. According to them, the child becomes a bit aggressive. For now, he has been counselled.

stories.title: Auto driver's Son files murder FIR:Body found floating in Varuna River on 6 August; acid found in vehicle
stories.summary: On the night of August 6, 2026, an abandoned auto-rickshaw was found on the Varuna Bridge in the Cantt police station area of Varanasi. The auto-rickshaw number was UP65 ET8037. During the investigation, the police found the auto-rickshaw belonged to Gyanchand Sonkar, a resident of Ardali Bazar, Cantt police station. A bottle of acid was found in the auto-rickshaw. Upon searching, Gyanchand's body was found floating in the Varuna River below the bridge. In this regard, on the night of August 13, the police registered a murder case based on the complaint. The deceased's son, Satish Sonkar, filed a murder complaint with the Cantt police. Based on this, the police have registered a case and started action. Murder on 6 August Satish stated in the complaint given to the police, My father Gyanchand Sonkar used to drive his private auto-rickshaw. He had no enmity with anyone, nor did he have much to do with anyone at home. When he did not return home by 11 PM on the night of August 6, I called his number.When I called, the police answered the phone and asked who I was, so I explained everything, upon which they called me to the Varuna Bridge. Body found floating in Varuna Satish said, Upon reaching there, the auto was found abandoned, and a half-empty bottle of acid was found further ahead. After this, we and the police started searching for father. When searched in the Varuna river below, father's body was found floating there, upon which he was pulled out. Someone has murdered my father. In such a situation, a complaint has been lodged with the police today. In this regard, Cantt Police Station in-charge Raj Kishore Pandey said, Based on the complaint of the deceased Gyanchand's son, a case has been registered under BNS Section 103(1) and the search for the murderer is underway. He will be apprehended soon. Had said a constable was following On August 6, upon finding the body, Satish had said that father had been troubled for a long time and was repeatedly saying that a constable was following him. In such a situation, the police are also investigating that angle. Currently, the search for the murderer is being conducted using CCTV footage.

stories.title: CCTV shows doctor jumping to death from 8th floor:Note blames conwoman Garima; sister breaks down, daughter says, ‘Papa, come back’
stories.summary: A doctor in Gorakhpur died by suicide after jumping from the eighth floor of his apartment on Thursday. A CCTV camera captured his final moments, while a note found in his pocket named alleged fraudster Garima Singh and her gang as responsible for his death. Dr Paramatma Singh left his flat at around 9.10 am, went to the basement and took a lift to the eighth floor before reaching the terrace. He jumped from the building shortly afterwards. Residents took him to a nearby private hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Daughter returns from school, says ‘Papa, please come back’ Singh’s 12-year-old son Arihant and seven-year-old daughter Parnika, known as Binni, were called home from school after the incident. When Binni saw her father’s body, she broke down and repeatedly said, “Papa, please come back.” She later clung to her elder brother and cried. Singh’s wife, Dr Sumitra Singh, also works as a government veterinary doctor. His younger sister Ranjana Singh said Sumitra had called her two days earlier, telling her that Paramatma was under severe stress over a loan-related matter. Ranjana said she had planned to visit and speak to him but could not reach him in time. Post-mortem finds multiple fractures A post-mortem examination found multiple fractures and serious internal injuries. The report said his neck, ribs, legs, spine and arms had suffered fractures. His body was taken to his ancestral home in Mau after the post-mortem. His last rites are scheduled for Friday. Who is Garima Singh? According to the police, Garima Singh, who holds a PhD, allegedly ran a loan fraud operation with her father Dhruv Narayan Singh and others. Police said she targeted railway officials, doctors and teachers by promising to arrange loans or help them close existing loans. Four cases have been registered against her so far this month, while six more complaints have been received. Police allege that around ₹10 crore may have been taken from 10 people. Garima and her father have been in jail since August 3. Seven days before his death, Dr Paramatma Singh had filed a complaint alleging that Garima had cheated him of ₹1.40 crore. Doctor allegedly took loans from six banks According to the complaint, Garima contacted Singh in February 2026 through a relative. She allegedly claimed that she could help close his existing home loan through a new personal loan. Police allege that Singh was made to take loans from six banks and transfer the money to accounts linked to Garima. She initially paid two instalments but later allegedly stopped making payments and threatened his family. FIR filed against Garima and associates Based on a complaint by Singh’s cousin Dileep Singh, Gorakhnath police registered a case of abetment of suicide against Garima Singh and her alleged associates on Thursday evening. Police may question Garima in jail as part of the investigation. SSP Dr Kaustubh said police would also invoke the Gangsters Act against Garima and other members of the alleged gang. Their financial activities are being investigated, and police are examining their bank accounts and properties allegedly linked to the fraud. Paramatma Singh, originally from Mau, had settled in Gorakhpur several years ago. He lived with his wife and two children in a two-bedroom flat at Basant Enclave in Rajendra Nagar. He was posted as a government veterinary doctor in Nautanwa, Maharajganj, while his wife was posted in the Siswan block of the same district.

stories.title: 'He called me his daughter, we only took a photo':Sister denies any relationship with Mahant; 2 friends buried in Baghpat temple
stories.summary: My brother left home on the 25th. Everyone searched for him a lot, but he was not found anywhere. Today it was revealed that he was killed and buried in the Ganesh temple. I have no relation with the Mahant. He used to say that I consider you my daughter. He had taken a photo with me in Haridwar, but I have no connection with him. This is what Ankit's sister said, who is rumored to be having an affair with the Mahant. In Baghpat, Mahant Naresh Nath of Ganesh Temple killed and buried 2 friends, then plastered over it and installed tiles. On Thursday (August 13), the police arrested 2 disciples of the Mahant. One disciple made several revelations in his confession. The case is from the Chandinagar police station area, 20 km away from the district headquarters. Know the full case In Sigoli Taga village, Ankit (25) lived with his mother and 5 sisters. He was the only son of the house. 2 sisters are married. Ankit was unmarried and unemployed. Israr's (32) house is right in front of his house. Israr used to support his family by working as a laborer. His family includes his wife Firdaus and 3 children. On the afternoon of July 25, Ankit and Israr left on a bike. When both did not return until the next day, their family members started looking for them. But, nothing was known about either of them. Calls were made to both their phones, but the mobiles were not picked up. From the evening of July 27, both their mobiles were switched off. Missing person report filed 4 days later On July 29, a missing person report was filed at Chandinagar police station. When both did not return even after 8-10 days, the police became active. The police checked call details, last known locations, and questioned villagers. In this, the name of Mahant Naresh Nath of Ganesh Temple located in Lahchaura came to light. Both were last seen near the Ganesh Temple. The police also learned about an affair between the Mahant and Ankit's sister. Accused Mahant absconded upon getting a hint Police raided the temple on Wednesday (August 12) night, but Mahant Naresh Nath (40) got wind of it and fled. Police found his disciple Ujjwal in the temple. Initially, he tried to mislead the police, but broke down under strict interrogation. Later, police also arrested another disciple, Krishna Yadav. Now read the confession of accused Ujjwal Ujjwal told the police - On August 25, Ankit and Israr came to the ashram very angrily. At that time, Mahant Naresh Nath, his 14-year-old son, I, and Krishna Yadav were present in the ashram. The Mahant calmed Ankit and Israr. He said that I will solve your problem, but first, have tea as prasad. Mixed intoxicant in tea and gave it to them The Mahant had already mixed an intoxicating substance in that tea, which made both of them unconscious as soon as they drank it. After that, the Mahant took out a poisonous injection from his car and administered it to both of them. When I asked that they would die, the Mahant told us to remain silent. Engaged minor son in watch duty Naresh Nath had told me that I charge 40 thousand for performing a marriage, but I will get your marriage done for free. Meanwhile, Krishna Yadav was lured with the promise that I would teach him tantra vidya (occult knowledge). After this, Krishna and I together dug a 6-foot deep pit. The Mahant's 14-year-old son had also come to the ashram. He was made to stand at the gate for watch duty. Phone thrown 10 km away to mislead Upon their death, they were buried in a pit. Tiles were installed over that pit. To mislead the police, Israr's phone was thrown 10 kilometers away in the jungle. When the police removed the tiles, the decomposed bodies of Ankit and Israr were found. They were identified by their clothes and watches. The bike Ankit and Israr used to reach Ganesh Temple has not yet been recovered. Sister was living at her maternal home after marriage One of Ankit's sisters had come to live at her maternal home after marriage. Earlier, the mahant used to live in Ankit's neighborhood and performed worship. However, his conduct was not good. Because of this, the villagers had expelled him from the village. After this, he started living with his two disciples at Ganesh Temple, 2 km away from the village. There had been fights many times before It is believed that Ankit and Israr had gone to convince the Mahant regarding his affair with their sister. There had been fights over this many times before. When the sister was asked about her affair with the Mahant, she denied it. The sister says that the Mahant used to call her his daughter. She had no relationship with him. A month and a half ago, we went to Haridwar with our family. The Mahant told me that I was like his daughter. During that time, he took a photo with me. All the talks about an affair are just rumors. I have no relationship with him. Baghpat SP Suraj Rai said that The dead bodies of both youths have been recovered from the temple. The Mahant's disciples, Ujjwal and Krishna, have been arrested. The search for the Mahant and his son has been intensified. 6 police teams are involved. The accused Mahant is originally from Uttarakhand. A police team has also been dispatched to Uttarakhand.

stories.summary: Since its inauguration on 13 July, the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway has been sinking somewhere or the other every day. In a month, more than 100 instances of sinking have been reported. The opposition is continuously making it an issue. Akhilesh Yadav is highlighting the features of the Agra Expressway from his time, and Akash Anand is praising the Yamuna Expressway from the BSP era. At the same time, questions are also being raised about the quality of Purvanchal Expressway, Ganga Expressway, and Gorakhpur Link Expressway. Meanwhile, the BJP government, which boasts of building the most expressways in UP, is on the back foot. In today's UP Explainer, find out if the opposition will be able to capitalise on this issue in the assembly elections and draw votes to its side? How will the BJP avoid this damage? Why is the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway sinking repeatedly? Is this the most sinking expressway till date? Yes, in terms of scale and duration, this is the most sinking expressway. However, the government or NHAI has not officially stated this. But, based on the number and duration of incidents recorded in media reports, this is the picture that emerges What loss will the BJP suffer due to the poor construction of the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway? Political experts say that this has dealt a blow to BJP's development model and good governance image. Even before this, the issue of poor construction of several expressways in UP has been raised, but there were no elections then. So everything was managed. But, it doesn't seem to be happening here. This can be understood as follows How big an issue will the Lucknow-Kanpur Expressway become in the elections? Political analysts are divided on this. Some talk about its widespread impact. Meanwhile, some experts say that this issue will cool down by the elections. How important are expressways for the development of a state? stories.title: Farrukhabad-Budaun highway submerged, barricades installed:44,000 people from 62 villages forced to leave their homes; evacuation announcement made
stories.summary: After the surge in the Ganga river, the Farrukhabad-Badaun highway has been submerged. At two places, two to three feet of water has accumulated for 100 to 150 meters. Traffic has been stopped by putting up barricades. Due to the flood, more than 44 thousand people from 62 villages have been forced to leave their homes. Floodwater has started reaching some of the relief camps that were set up. Children and women have been sent to other camps. The Ganga river is continuously eroding its banks. It is flowing 1.5 km away from its original course. As a result, 32 houses have collapsed so far. Seeing the deteriorating situation, NDRF (National Disaster Response Force) has been called in. PAC personnel are transporting people stranded in the water to safe places with the help of boats and steamers. Having to travel 14 km extra to go to Badaun Among the villages in Farrukhabad that are affected by floods, the highest number, 27 villages, are in Amritpur tehsil. The people there say - 'This is the sign of Amritpur, water on both sides of the road.' Every year, as the water level of the Ganga rises, this road is bound to get submerged. In 2025, the State Highway remained blocked for 15 days. Until now, vehicles going from Farrukhabad to Badaun used to go via Rajepur Tiraaha to Badaun. However, currently, the State Highway near Chitrakoot village has been submerged. Police duty has been assigned on the highway to prevent people from going onto the submerged road. Police are diverting vehicles from the Dabra area towards Badaun. People have to travel about 14 km extra. No shelter in relief camps, they are living on house roofs Chitrakoot village is near the State Highway. The entire village is submerged. We met Rajpal amidst the water. He says - the village is filled with water all around. There is also a risk of snakes and scorpions. People have to commute through these paths. A relief camp has been set up near the village. Only 10 to 20 people come here, because only that many names have been registered. Many people's names were not registered. They are forced to live on the roofs of their houses, waiting for the water to recede. Some have gone to their relatives' homes. This situation has persisted for 10 days. Last year's flood lasted for 30 days. Lost homes, set up tents by the roadside, then removed from there too Sukhdev, standing near us, says- Many houses in the village were submerged. Distressed people started living in tents by the roadside. Just 2-3 days ago, the administration announced (by beating drums) that this place is also dangerous and must be vacated. People were asked to go to relief camps. Those who are trapped on the roofs of their houses are not even getting clean drinking water. Ration and water are being delivered by boat, but the fear persists. People are somehow making ends meet. Tehsildar flared up when asked about water filling in the camp To understand the atmosphere of the relief camp, we reached the Pharmacy College in Chitrakoot village. The relief camp was set up here. The government school in the village was flooded. Because of this, a part of the school was also running in a section of the relief camp. Water has slowly started filling up outside the relief camp as well. SDM Shweta Sahu and Tehsildar Shashank Singh had arrived here. We asked the Tehsildar - "Floodwater has started filling up here, what are the preparations?" He angrily said - "Those who come to the camp will stay inside or will they roam outside? There is no water inside, is there?" We asked - "They will go outside for other needs." The Tehsildar said - "You tell us what we should do, because we don't know anything." Ration dealer said - A dam was built after 14 years, but it didn't even last a few months 12 villages in Farrukhabad Sadar Tehsil are flooded. Due to erosion in Rampur Dafarpur, several houses were swallowed by the river. On the boat going towards this village, the village's ration dealer, Subhash Chandra, was met. He says - Since 2012, it happens every year that after the water level in the Ganga rises, floods occur. People asked officials to build a dam so that the entire village could be saved from erosion. The Irrigation Department built a dam, but it didn't even last a few months. Some grain was sent by the government, which is being distributed among the people trapped in the flood. 'One house washed away, the other is saved so we are demolishing it' About 50 meters away from the strong current of the Ganga river, Meerawati was getting the debris of her broken house loaded onto a boat with her relatives. She says - We had an old house in this village. It was submerged in the river just 4 days ago. We were building another house here, but now this one is also going to be submerged. We are demolishing it and taking the bricks. Everyone here is troubled. Food and drink are not available. We have lost everything from our farm to our home. Now we don't understand where to go? House filled with water, cows and goats are on the road 56-year-old Jabar Singh lived his entire life in the village and did farming. He says - we have cows and goats, the house is submerged in water. The animals are on the road. The fields are also flooded. Now, when the water recedes, we will return. We will rebuild our house here again. Every year there is a flood, and there is a lot of talk about help, but the truth is that people like us don't even get a penny. Who does the administration help, I wonder? Santosh from Madaiya village says, In our area, it's not just the problem of floods, the current of the Ganga is also eroding the land. Last year, the situation was very terrible. The entire Prithvipur village was eroded. These people did build a dam. But, it could not withstand the current of the Ganga. People are distressed, they are just surviving. 3 situations of flood, see in pictures 1. Erosion of Ganga river People are demolishing their houses themselves Crops submerged

stories.summary: A Nebraska bridge is using 52 slabs of conductive concrete that can heat its surface and melt snow and ice during winter storms. Developed by University of Nebraska-Lincoln professor Chris Tuan, the technology uses steel shavings and carbon particles to carry electricity through the concrete. The system could reduce the need for de-icing chemicals at bridges, airport tarmacs, intersections and other icy areas.

stories.title: Mexican man arrested with 200 lizards hidden in socks at Tokyo airport
Ram Mandir donation theft case: SC asks SIT to submit status report, take probe to logical end
Scientists found genetically unusual avocados in Nicaragua that may preserve clues of migration
Mark Cuban helps heart transplant survivor access drug after insurer stops covering it
stories.summary: At 11, Payton Herres received a donated heart after years of health problems caused by Ebstein’s anomaly. Fifteen years later, she faced a fight to access everolimus, the anti-rejection medicine she had relied on since 2013. After her insurer stopped covering the drug and its cost rose sharply, Herres turned to social media. Her story went viral and reached Mark Cuban, whose pharmacy began supplying the medicine at a lower cost.

After 25 years at Adobe, engineer laid off; now he is a driver
stories.summary: A senior software engineer with twenty-five years at Adobe was laid off last year. He struggled to find new tech employment for a year after his dismissal. This led him to pursue a new career as a school bus driver for his local district. While his new role pays less, he finds contentment and supportive colleagues. His experience highlights challenges faced by experienced tech professionals in the current job market.

stories.title: An 18-year-old construction worker in Belgium uncovered a €9 million gold hoard
California student turned pickleball fundraiser for St. Jude into a sports platform that raised more than $90,000
stories.summary: Olivia Shekou has successfully generated over ninety thousand dollars through her innovative sports philanthropy platform, known as Netting Miracles. Her initiative empowers students to spearhead fundraising events. Currently, she is gearing up for an exciting new fundraiser aimed at helping women and children in Uganda, scheduled to take place at Flyte Racquet Club in San Rafael. Her platform has now broadened its support across seventeen states, backing various charitable causes.

stories.title: California startup JetZero is building a $3 billion aircraft that promises to cut fuel consumption by 50%, carry 250 passengers
stories.summary: JetZero is unveiling a cutting-edge 'manta ray' aircraft aimed at revolutionizing the future of commercial aviation. This groundbreaking design is expected to yield impressive fuel savings and significantly lower emissions. With a full-scale prototype scheduled to take flight by 2027, Japan Airlines is on board to provide operational insights, paving the way for expected commercial operations in the early 2030s.

stories.title: Teacher leads 2,800 students in 29-year effort to restore New Zealand coast
stories.summary: Retired teacher Janet Pottinger spent 29 years helping Buller High School students restore native vegetation at Tauranga Bay and Cape Foulwind in New Zealand. Since 1997, around 2,800 students have planted 12,425 native plants across 108 trips. The project has transformed former grassland into habitat supporting birds, seals, lizards and other native wildlife.

stories.title: Chidambaram says he is 'proud to be a dimaagi Naxal'; BJP hits back
2 more Air India pilots fail to clear dope test after Phuket-Delhi flight scare; taken off duty
stories.summary: Air India's recent pilot screening revealed two non-negative dope test results, leading to these pilots being grounded while awaiting confirmatory tests. In response, the aviation ministry has instructed the DGCA to revise current dope testing protocols. The intended policy overhaul aims to impose stricter penalties for pilots found using illegal drugs, while also distinguishing between accidental use of medication and intentional substance abuse.

stories.title: Supreme Court declares August 22 full working day in place of holiday on August 27
Disproportionate assets case: SC asks Allahabad HC not to proceed with case against Rahul Gandhi
Florida couple bought a swamp to protect wildlife; then 275 wood storks nested there
Two pairs of North American raccoons were released in Germany's Kassel, today their population is around 30,000 and are known as 'bandits' by public
stories.summary: Intriguingly, German raccoons, previously thought to have ties to Hermann Göring, were dispersed through administrative action. Research uncovering archival documents traces their onset to Kassel in 1934. Moreover, genetic studies have pinpointed several other deliberate releases across eastern Germany. These highly adaptable creatures have proliferated throughout Europe, raising alarms over potential property destruction and threats to indigenous wildlife.

stories.title: 'We owe them our solidarity': Rahul Gandhi writes to ally Hemant Soren over Jharkhand student protests
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has thrown his weight behind students protesting against the irregularities in Jharkhand's recruitment exams. He has called on Chief Minister Hemant Soren to engage with student representatives amid an ongoing indefinite hunger strike by some. Gandhi emphasized that the Congress party stands in complete solidarity with the students, voicing concerns over the exploitation of the Indian education system by certain factions.

stories.title: Prashant Kishor takes oath as Bankipur MLA after first Jan Suraaj victory
Florida introduced rhesus macaques for tourism in the 1930s, now they carry a potentially fatal virus
stories.summary: Wild rhesus macaques in Florida carry herpes B virus, posing a potential human health risk. A study found about a quarter of sampled macaques had been infected with the virus. Some animals actively shed the virus, especially during the breeding season. The circulating virus strains are genetically similar to dangerous laboratory versions. No human cases have been confirmed from these wild populations yet.

stories.title: Sweden’s Söderåsen went from deforested plateau to one of northern Europe’s largest protected forests
stories.summary: The Söderåsen plateau in southern Sweden has transitioned from its historical grazed heathland, significantly impacted by intensive grazing in the 18th and 19th centuries. Today, Söderåsen National Park encompasses over 1,600 hectares of lush broadleaf forest, showcasing the impressive capacity for natural regeneration and ecological restoration over time, while preserving a landscape shaped by both natural processes and human activities.

stories.title: NMC proposes central tracking of doctors’ disciplinary records
Vande Mataram 'disruption' row: Delhi Police probes complaint against Sonia Gandhi, Rahul
stories.summary: The Delhi Police have launched an investigation into a complaint against Sonia and Rahul Gandhi, alleging that they disrupted the singing of Vande Mataram at an Independence Day celebration. Advocates supporting the complaint have referenced video evidence and media reports documenting the incident. Currently, the police are scrutinizing alleged gestures and remarks made during this national song, and an FIR has yet to be filed as the inquiry continues.

stories.title: 'Modi ji, look at what your NTA has done': Rahul Gandhi after fresh NET ordered for 3 subjects

Europe wildfires: 2 dead, 500 evacuated as twin blazes hit Greek island near Athens
Lakshmi Mittal's Ukraine steel plant hit by Russian missile; 2 killed
Tropical Storm Lala moves away from Hawaii, leaves trail of damage and lakhs without power
stories.summary: As Tropical Storm Lala departed from Hawaii, it left a trail of destruction in its wake. Over one hundred homes were either damaged or completely destroyed by the relentless winds and heavy rains. In addition, approximately one hundred eighty-four thousand residents found themselves without power across the islands. Rescue operations are ongoing, with floodwaters and landslides making it difficult to reach isolated communities.

Breakup Status Unclear: Suki Mellow addresses Kanel Joseph on stream; fans speculate
stories.summary: Suki Mellow’s recent comments about Kanel Joseph have sparked fresh breakup rumors among fans. The Twitch streamer praised Kanel as a great person while admitting she wished she had handled her emotions better. She also suggested they may be at different stages of life with different priorities. Although Suki has not confirmed a breakup, her emotional remarks and fans’ reactions have fueled speculation about the status of their relationship.

stories.title: Owens-Wilson Debate Clip Fallout: Candace Owens grills Andrew Wilson; Utah judge weighs capital case
stories.summary: Candace Owens has reignited controversy surrounding her debate with Andrew Wilson after challenging him to name a charge against Tyler Robinson. Owens later argued that the question was not intended as a “gotcha,” but reflected her desire to discuss Utah’s law and the case’s aggravating factor. She accused Wilson of wasting viewers’ time and questioned his preparation, while the viral exchange sparked renewed debate over Robinson’s charges and the broader case.

In 1993, Chile adopted an Indigenous Law that enabled land restitution; by 2023...
stories.summary: Since 1993, over 510,000 acres have been returned to Mapuche communities in Chile under the Indigenous Law. A study revealed minimal changes in forest cover on the restituted lands. It observed a decline in commercial plantations and a slight rise in agricultural pastures, emphasizing the importance of traditional economic practices alongside conservation. This situation illustrates the need for distinct strategies in managing land rights and environmental restoration efforts.

stories.title: In 1988, an English farmer stopped cultivating his entire 377-acre wheat farm
stories.summary: An abandoned wheat farm in England has been transformed into a thriving nature reserve after decades of neglect. Following a dedicated public campaign, £1.5 million was raised to acquire the land, ensuring its protection for future generations. This 377-acre area now boasts a rich variety of wildlife, including numerous endangered bird species, and will be overseen by the Wildlife Trust as a cherished habitat.

Punjab Congress faces fresh rift as Randhawa challenges Warring's 'one family, one ticket' rule
Ferrari’s first all-electric car sells for $40M, nearly 40 times initial estimate of $1.1M
stories.summary: Ferrari’s first all-electric car, the bespoke Luce “Chassis 0,” has sold for a record $40 million at a charity auction in Monterey, nearly 40 times its initial $1.1 million estimate. The sale makes it the most expensive new car ever auctioned, while the buyer will have to wait until 2027 for delivery.

stories.title: At 15, Lynne Cox broke the English Channel record for men and women; at 30...
stories.summary: In 1987, endurance swimmer Lynne Cox made waves by crossing the Bering Strait, swimming from Alaska to Soviet territory during a tense Cold War period. This monumental swim was more than a personal triumph; it represented a bridge of peace and understanding between two divided nations. Her bravery earned accolades from leaders in both the US and the Soviet Union, emphasizing the potential for cooperation in the Bering Strait region.

stories.title: 3,000 hectares up in flames: Belgium battles its biggest wildfire on record
UP CM Yogi pays tribute to Atal Bihari Vajpayee, recalls his 'Nation First' politics
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday paid tribute to former Prime Minister and Bharat Ratna Atal Bihari Vajpayee on his death anniversary at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Convention Centre in Lucknow, recalling his six-decade-long political career and his commitment to public service, democratic values and national interest.

stories.title: Influencer Talks Baby Plans: looksmaxxer says couple trying for child; past infertility claims surface
stories.summary: Clavicular says he and Lily Snyder are trying to have a baby after stopping birth control. The 20-year-old influencer previously claimed he was unable to have children because of testosterone use. During a recent Kick livestream, he said he plans to take testosterone while trying for a child. The couple also spoke about the relationship problems they have faced.

stories.title: 'They were Indian, so we didn’t count them': US cleaning business owner faces scrutiny over racial profiling
Princess Iman welcomes twin daughters Talia and Rania with husband Jameel Alexander Thermiotis
stories.summary: Princess Iman of Jordan and her husband Jameel Alexander Thermiotis have welcomed twin daughters, Talia and Rania. The newborns were born on August 14, bringing a double celebration to King Abdullah II and Queen Rania, who are now grandparents to four granddaughters. The couple’s older daughter, Amina, has also become a big sister.

stories.title: ‘Future of students at stake’: CJP's Dipke seeks re-test after alleged technical glitches in Bombay HC clerk exam
NTA admits errors, orders fresh NET for 3 subjects
stories.summary: National Testing Agency acknowledged extensive errors in UGC-NET English, Commerce, and Sociology papers. Fresh examinations for these three subjects have been ordered by the agency. These re-tests are scheduled to take place on September 9 and 10. The decision came after multiple complaints regarding factual and typographical errors were received. Results for the other 84 subjects will be declared as scheduled.

stories.title: In 1953, Emma tried hiking the Appalachian Trail, got lost and was rescued; two years later...
stories.summary: Emma Gatewood etched her name in history in 1955 as the first woman to conquer the Appalachian Trail solo at the remarkable age of 67. With minimal equipment, she bravely journeyed over 2,190 miles, transforming the narrative around long-distance hiking for women. Her perseverance and spirit culminated in two additional hikes, serving as an inspiration for countless adventurers seeking freedom and adventure.

stories.title: Centre orders corrective measures after CAG flags unsafe drinking water at railway stations
'They are as good as dead': Jharkhand protester shaves head for CM Soren, Rahul Gandhi's 'last rites'
stories.summary: The protest by students and job aspirants over alleged irregularities in Jharkhand recruitment examinations entered its 23rd day on Sunday, with the protesters, under the banner of JPSC-JSSC Reforms Manch, accusing the ruling JMM-Congress alliance of failing to take “concrete action” on their demands. They have also announced plans to gherao Soren's residence in Ranchi on August 20 and demanded his resignation.

stories.title: Iran moves to criminalise interviews with US, Israeli media, with prison terms up to 30 years
In 1933, Lincoln's Crooked House was marked for demolition; work revealed a hidden...
stories.summary: In the midst of a demolition in 1933, builders stumbled upon a remarkable 16th-century timber-framed structure known as the Wonky House. This architectural gem narrowly evaded obliteration and has since undergone conservation efforts to rectify damage caused by death-watch beetles and previous poor repairs. Thanks to significant funding, extensive restoration will soon provide unique holiday accommodations and community spaces, welcoming visitors to enjoy its rich history.

8-year-old boy catches a piranha while fishing with dad at Pennsylvania lake
stories.summary: While fishing near Philadelphia, an eight-year-old boy made an unusual catch: a piranha. Officials identified this tropical fish as non-native to Pennsylvania, raising alarms over the potential dangers of exotic pets being set free into local waters. Releasing such species is illegal and can jeopardize public safety. Following their unexpected encounter, the boy and his father took responsible action to humanely dispose of the piranha.

stories.title: Beyond bloodline: How donated milk is saving India’s most vulnerable newborns
stories.summary: Human milk banks in India serve a critical purpose by delivering much-needed nourishment to at-risk infants. Generous lactating mothers donate their surplus milk, helping those newborns who can’t receive it from their biological mothers. Every donation undergoes thorough screening and pasteurisation to ensure safety, highlighting the significant impact these banks have on the health of premature and sick children.

stories.title: Four Renaissance masterpieces stolen from Sicily museum in art heist
A Maine oyster farm is testing a floating conveyor that moves oyster baskets through water and air
stories.summary: Engineers in Maine are developing an innovative solar-powered floating system tailored for oyster farming. This unique platform incorporates a vertical conveyor that efficiently transports oyster baskets from underwater to above, aiming to enhance production while significantly lessening the labor demands on farmers. Additionally, it aids in shaping the oysters and cleaning their shells from unwanted marine growth.

Got a secret you can’t tell anyone? Visit this ‘grave of secrets’
stories.summary: A unique art installation in Brooklyn offers a place for visitors to anonymously share their deepest secrets. French artist Sophie Calle created a marble obelisk where people can deposit written confessions. This project, which began in 2017, will continue until the year 2042. Secrets deposited will be exhumed and cremated in a ceremonial service periodically. The installation provides a moment of catharsis and a chance for reflective unburdening.

Government seeks stakeholder comments on nuclear rules and regulations
stories.summary: In a significant move towards enhancing its nuclear energy capabilities, the Indian government has introduced revised regulations aimed at facilitating atomic power growth. These new guidelines establish comprehensive licensing and safety protocols for the engagement of private sector operators. Companies can now obtain preliminary approvals prior to selecting sites or technologies, with financial security measures in place to cover potential nuclear damage.

stories.title: CEA notifies new regulations to protect power sector from cyber attack
San Diego student develops red-light therapy to help heal wounds in space
stories.summary: An 18-year-old San Diego student has been named a finalist in the 2026 Regeneron Science Talent Search for developing a low-cost red-light treatment to improve wound healing in microgravity. Leanne Fan built a $200 device to simulate microgravity and found that the treatment accelerated tissue regeneration in flatworms by 95.2%. Tests with human cells also showed faster cell movement during wound closure.

Meet Connor Hill, 17-year-old Pennsylvania student who wrote a computer program to...
stories.summary: Connor Hill triumphed in the competition with his exceptional algorithm for classifying noble polyhedra, discovering two infinite families alongside 146 distinct shapes. Edward Kang's AI tool for autism screening claimed the second position, and Iris Shen's innovative blood cancer research involving clams took third place. Additionally, Regeneron expressed their commitment by extending sponsorship for another ten years, ensuring continued support for emerging scientific talent.

stories.title: SAD chief Sukhbir Badal’s wife seeks NIA probe into Aug 13 attack, writes to Amit Shah
JNU recruitment row: VC rejects irregularities charges, calls allegations ‘fake propaganda’
stories.summary: The university administration said more than 400 faculty interviews had been conducted and over 200 positions filled since February 2022. It claimed that nearly 70 per cent of those appointed belonged to reserved and marginalised categories. The administration said it had received no complaints from candidates about interview process. According to the university, selection committees include three domain experts, a nominee of the Visitor, concerned dean and the vice chancellor.

stories.title: From burnt cash to possibly the first impeachment of a judge: The Yashwant Varma saga explained
stories.summary: Justice Yashwant Varma's residence was engulfed in flames, leading to the shocking discovery of burnt currency notes. A subsequent parliamentary inquiry confirmed serious charges against him, prompting his resignation. The Centre's pursuit of impeachment aims to set a strong precedential framework for judicial accountability. This case also poses critical questions about the interplay between a judge's resignation and ongoing disciplinary proceedings, potentially impacting future cases of judicial misconduct.

stories.title: Evening newswrap: Flyer’s pistol ‘accidentally’ goes off at Varanasi airport; Netanyahu's litmus test in Israel election & more
'Human cost of relentless political hostility': Mamata Banerjee on TMC leader's suicide
stories.summary: The former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee claimed that Asish Banerjee was "repeatedly maligned, falsely accused and subjected to relentless pressure". She said: The harassment and mental pressure he faced, despite his long record of public service, should make all of us pause and reflect on the human cost of relentless political hostility". Meanwhile, West Begal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari said he would ensure probe into suicide.

stories.title: Rolex sues Canadian jewellery store Bijoux Medusa over customized watches, claims trademark infringement
Inde Navarrette Cast As Rogue: Ex-streamer lands MCU’s new X-Men role; Obsession paved the way
stories.summary: Inde Navarrette’s career has reached a major milestone after she was cast as Rogue in Marvel’s upcoming X-Men reboot. The actress first gained recognition through roles in 13 Reasons Why and Superman & Lois before earning critical praise for her intense performance in Obsession. Her journey also includes a past as a Twitch and YouTube streamer. Now, Navarrette is stepping onto Marvel’s biggest stage as one of its iconic mutants.

stories.title: China launches 24th batch of low-orbit internet satellites from Hainan site
stories.summary: The launch took place from the southern island province of Hainan, which has become an important location for China's commercial space activities. The latest mission is part of China's ongoing effort to build large networks of low-orbit satellites that can provide internet connectivity from space. The rocket lifted off at 12.10 pm Beijing time and successfully placed the satellites into their designated orbits.

stories.title: Bangladesh PM's proposed India visit conditional on Hasina extradition, officials say
Virginia re-wet a swamp across 150 miles of old ditches; peat traps 200,000 tonnes of carbon
stories.summary: North Carolina is restoring its coastal peatlands by bringing water back to areas damaged by drainage, farming and timber activities. The projects aim to reduce the risk of severe peat fires while keeping carbon stored in wet soils. At Pocosin Lakes National Wildlife Refuge, 37,000 acres have been restored, with water-control structures helping recreate natural water movement. Similar work at Angola Bay Game Land is restoring ditched peatland and wetland habitat. The efforts also support wildlife, improve resilience to flooding and sea-level rise, and involve local communities and landowners in managing water across the coastal landscape.

TMC leader's suicide case: CM Suvendu Adhikari vows probe into possible 'threat' angle
stories.summary: Asish Banerjee Banerjee was found dead on Sunday morning at a Trinamool Congress office in Rampurhat, Birbhum district. Police said his body was found hanging and was sent for post-mortem examination. The exact circumstances surrounding his death remain unclear. A teacher by profession, Banerjee had represented the Rampurhat Assembly constituency five times. TMC legislator Kunal Ghosh called for an impartial probe.

Manhattan’s got a hairy situation! Tumblehair rolls through NYC
stories.summary: A giant hairball rolled through Manhattan streets as a marketing stunt. This installation aimed to highlight hair loss and premature aging concerns. Pedestrians reacted with disgust and curiosity to the unusual sight. The campaign sought to break the quiet shame surrounding hair loss issues. It successfully generated conversation about a topic people often avoid.

A 13-year-old crawled into a Tennessee cave and found a hidden lake
stories.summary: In 1905, a 13-year-old boy stumbled upon America's largest underground lake in Craighead Caverns, Tennessee. This expansive chamber, referred to as the Lost Sea, showcases traces of Indigenous habitation and mining activities from the Civil War. Nowadays, visitors have the opportunity to navigate the vast cavern and embark on a captivating boat ride over the hidden waters. The total size of this geological marvel continues to spark intrigue and investigation.

stories.title: Cauvery water row: Supreme Court to hear Tamil Nadu plea against Karnataka on August 17
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu approached the top court on August 3, arguing that it was not receiving its allocated share of Cauvery water despite the state facing a rain-deficient year. The state government has alleged that both the quantity recommended for release by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee and the actual water supplied by Karnataka were far below its requirement.

Hawaiʻi’s eucalyptus forests could help build the islands’ future
stories.summary: Hawaii's heavy reliance on imported building lumber may soon change, thanks to promising research into local eucalyptus. Scientists are evaluating the strength and durability of this homegrown resource to establish engineering design values necessary for structural uses. By successfully validating these traits, this initiative aims to lessen dependence on foreign materials and invigorate local industries, ensuring that communities' construction needs are met sustainably.

stories.title: BJP lodges complaint against Sonia Gandhi as Vande Mataram row intensifies
Arctic foxes brought for fur transformed Alaska’s grasslands into tundra
stories.summary: Arctic foxes introduced to more than 400 Alaskan islands for fur had an unexpected impact on the ecosystem. By preying on seabirds, they reduced the flow of nutrient-rich guano from the ocean to land. Researchers found that fox-free islands had far more seabirds, richer soil and much more grass, while fox-infested islands shifted towards shrubs and forbs.

How a holiday in Alaska led Mahala Dickerson to claim 160 acres and become its first Black lawyer
stories.summary: Mahala Ashley Dickerson broke several barriers during her six-decade legal career. Born in Alabama in 1912, she became the state’s first Black female lawyer in 1948 before moving to Alaska. In 1958, she became Alaska’s first Black homesteader and later its first Black lawyer. Her career included major discrimination cases, legal honours and an autobiography.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Friedrich Nietzsche: "The higher we soar, the smaller we..."
‘Congress should feel ashamed’: Amit Shah targets Sonia Gandhi over Vande Mataram row
stories.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah criticized the Congress party for allegedly disrespecting the national song Vande Mataram. He accused Sonia Gandhi of asking for the rendition to be stopped during an event. The Congress rejected these allegations, stating the full song was sung. Party leader Jairam Ramesh cited historical context for their stance on the song. The controversy follows recent legislation on national song disrespect.

stories.title: 'Apologise': Bankim Chandra descendant writes to Sonia Gandhi over Vande Mataram 'insult'
Mississippi’s termite swarms are here: A single treatment can cost up to $1,750
stories.summary: Termite swarms in Mississippi signal developing colonies that require prompt homeowner attention and professional inspection. Eastern subterranean termites swarm from winter into early summer, while Formosan termites appear later. Spotting swarmers indoors strongly indicates an active infestation needing immediate professional treatment. Preventive measures and early intervention significantly reduce costly structural damage from termites. Homeowners should recognize signs and consult licensed professionals for effective termite control.

stories.title: US man on the ‘worst part’ of living in India: ‘It's so cheap'
stories.summary: A Seattle creator's video sarcastically lists India's worst aspects, which are actually its strengths. Affordable and high-quality healthcare is a significant advantage for residents. Rapid e-commerce delivery services provide convenience for daily needs. Strong community ties and neighborly relationships are a notable aspect of Indian life. The video sparked diverse reactions, with many agreeing and some disagreeing with his points.

stories.title: 160 plus fractures found in Scottish castle skeleton may be first confirmed trebuchet death
stories.summary: A 14th-century skeleton found beneath Scotland’s Stirling Castle may be the first confirmed archaeological evidence of a person killed by a trebuchet. Researchers found more than 160 fractures, including 61 breaks in the skull and nearly 60 in the ribs. The injuries suggest the man was struck from behind by a high-speed boulder during the 1304 siege of the castle.

stories.title: In 1898, 17 years after surviving the O.K. Corral gunfight, Virgil Earp claimed 160 acres in Arizona; two years later, he earned title to the land
stories.summary: Virgil Earp, known for surviving the infamous O.K. Corral gunfight, embraced a new beginning as a homesteader in Arizona. Claiming 160 acres near Prescott through the federal homesteading process, his prior service in the Civil War lessened his residency obligation to just two years. By 1900, he secured his property title, stepping into a life that diverged significantly from his days as a frontier lawman.

stories.title: Jharkhand protests continue: Students to gherao CM residence on August 20 if demands not met
Hungary bus crash: 12 killed, 10 injured after Polish bus overturns on M3 motorway
stories.summary: Twelve people died and ten were seriously injured after a Polish bus overturned early Sunday. The bus ran off the M3 motorway and tipped into a ditch near Mezokeresztes. Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar announced the tragic casualties on Facebook. He also expressed his sincere condolences to the families of the victims. The exact cause of the accident remains unknown at this time.

Raabi’atul remains married to Prince Abdul Malik, with no divorce announced, while their four daughters retain their titles.

stories.title: President Murmu approves 78 gallantry awards
stories.summary: President Droupadi Murmu has approved a total of seventy-eight gallantry awards, including nine Kirti Chakras and nineteen Shaurya Chakras, recognizing the exceptional bravery of defence personnel and central armed police forces. Many of these awards are awarded posthumously. This recognition underscores the remarkable commitment and courage displayed by individuals across the Army, Navy, and Air Force, emphasizing the nation's deep respect and appreciation for their service.

stories.title: Male redback spiders somersault directly towards a female’s fangs during mating
stories.summary: Recent research uncovers that a singular genetic region governs the intricate somersaulting behavior of male redback spiders during mating rituals. This fascinating behavior, crucial for reproduction, is inherited through the X chromosome. Experimental hybrids indicate that this somersault characteristic is not only recessive but also X-linked. Conversely, abdominal narrowing seems influenced by a combination of multiple genes and environmental conditions, challenging traditional views on the complexity of genetic traits.

stories.title: Pew survey: What US, UK and others think about India at 80
stories.summary: India's standing on the global stage reveals a mixed bag of perceptions among nations, with only 45% viewing it favorably. While Pakistan's outlook remains critical, Sri Lanka showcases significant support. Since 2025, favorability has waned in several countries, yet noteworthy improvements have emerged in Germany and the UK, highlighting the complexities and challenges of India's international reputation.

In 1870, a former slave and Union soldier staked a homestead in Nebraska
stories.summary: Escaping the bonds of slavery, Robert Ball Anderson became a proud soldier in the Union Army. Despite facing significant obstacles in farming caused by severe weather and pests, he dedicated himself to saving money through various jobs, including cooking for railroads. His efforts culminated in owning more than two thousand acres of fertile land, exemplifying the strength and resilience of African Americans in achieving landownership across the Great Plains.

The list also includes three Nao Sena Medals (Gallantry) and five Vayu Sena Medals (Gallantry). The awards have been approved to recognise gallantry among personnel of the Defence Forces and Central Armed Police Forces.

stories.title: 'Greatest threat': How India, Pakistan view each other; data lays bare deep animosity
stories.summary: A recent survey by Pew highlights that Indians and Pakistanis regard each other as their principal geopolitical adversaries. Unfavorable opinions dominate across the border, with India marking Pakistan as the major threat while Pakistan responds in kind. There is a notable distrust regarding the other’s dedication to peaceful relations, amplified by contrasting global alliances influencing each country’s strategic outlook.

stories.title: 'Cannot imagine': Rajnath Singh's sharp 'Gandhi surname' attack on Rahul Gandhi over PM hug jibe
stories.summary: Rajnath Singh said he was particularly upset that the comments came from the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha. He accused Gandhi of lowering the dignity associated with the post and questioned whether such conduct was appropriate for someone holding a key constitutional position. The defence minister also defended Modi's record as Prime Minister and his standing abroad.

stories.title: In 1968, a California landowner demanded $100 an acre for land that officials valued at $17
stories.summary: The US government's lengthy legal struggle with Dean Brimhall culminated in a $400,000 buyout. The resolution saw the demolition of commercial facilities, including a lodge and petrol station, adjacent to Capitol Reef National Park. The agreement also put an end to quarrying operations on the land. This settlement balanced private ownership with conservation needs in southern Utah, allowing for the restoration of native vegetation managed by the park.

Gandhi's letter to India, as told through TOI
stories.summary: From his South Africa years to the freedom struggle, Mahatma Gandhi repeatedly used newspapers to address India’s public. Alok Sharma sifts through letters Gandhi wrote to TOI, illuminating his positions on Satyagraha, the Rowlatt Act, Dalit representation, Hindu-Muslim unity and the hardships faced by Indians in South Africa.

Karnataka BJP MLA's daughter booked for 'assaulting' woman cop over temple entry queue
stories.summary: During temple festivities, B Suresh Gowda's daughter, a Karnataka BJP MLA, was accused of assaulting a woman police sub-inspector. The altercation began over access to the queue, leading to allegations of abuse and physical confrontation by the officer. In response, the MLA's daughter filed a counter-complaint currently under investigation. The MLA expressed regret for the incident and emphasized the need for appropriate legal action.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Delhi HC gets bomb threat; US loses 45 Reaper drones in Iran war, & more
stories.summary: A bomb threat email targeted the Delhi High Court ahead of Independence Day celebrations. Reports indicate the US military lost forty-five Reaper drones in its conflict with Iran. The Supreme Court disapproved of the Bar Council of India's action against NALSAR students. Congress questioned the Centre's approach to the caste census format. Former Manchester United and Aston Villa goalkeeper Jimmy Rimmer has died at seventy-eight.

stories.title: Pakistani minister in Balochistan province escapes armed attack on convoy
stories.summary: .The attack took place in the Khad Kocha area as Langove was travelling from Quetta to Kalat, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said. "Six people were injured in the attack, but the minister remained unhurt and the convoy has returned to Quetta," Rind said. All six injured people suffered bullet wounds, according to a senior police official. Three of them were police personnel, with two reportedly in serious condition.

stories.title: London river was declared 'biologically dead' in 1957; decades later it is filled with sharks and seals
stories.summary: The River Thames in London has made a remarkable recovery, evolving from a biologically barren stretch to a vibrant ecosystem full of life, such as sharks and seals. This revitalization is attributed to decades of pollution management and enhanced sewage systems. The Thames Tideway Tunnel plays a crucial role in minimizing sewage discharge. However, challenges like warming waters and nitrate pollution still pose threats.

stories.title: UK heatwaves help bananas fruit, experts explain why it’s unusual

GOBARdhan scheme: How India plans to turn cattle dung, crop waste and garbage into fuel
stories.summary: India's GOBARdhan scheme targets ten-fold growth in compressed biogas production. This initiative aims to convert agricultural residue and cattle dung into valuable fuel. The government provides capital assistance and assured demand for producers. This framework seeks to build a national bioenergy industry from organic waste. The scheme intends to enhance energy security and rural development.

stories.title: Nigel Farage beats ‘space warrior trashcan’ rival in UK by-poll he triggered
stories.summary: Nigel Farage claimed a decisive win in the Clacton parliamentary by-election, following his resignation amid controversies surrounding his financial dealings. His nearest rival, the comedic character Count Binface, surprisingly garnered a considerable share of support. Meanwhile, prominent parties in Westminster chose to abstain from the election, deeming it a mere political ploy. This by-election stemmed from Farage's prior resignation and his ambition to retake his seat.

stories.title: Bernie Marcus' foundation gives $28.7M for heart-repair stem cell research
7,000-year-old ‘Stargazer’ statuette from ancient Turkey raises mysteries
stories.summary: A 5,000-year-old marble statuette called "The Stargazer" originates from ancient Turkey. This rare figure, dating to 3000 BCE, is remarkably whole and unbroken. Its oversized head and upward gaze create a distinctive, stylized human form. The statuette's original purpose remains a mystery due to its ancient origins. Similar figures have been found across Western Anatolia and nearby regions.

stories.title: 'Not said, but presented as if it was': CJI Surya Kant says 'cockroach' remark 'misquoted'
Quote of the day by Martin Luther King Jr: 'There is some good in the worst of us and some evil in the best of us. When we discover this, we are less prone to hate our enemies'
stories.summary: Martin Luther King Jr. eloquently illustrates the dual nature of humanity and our collective imperfections. By acknowledging our flaws, we foster empathy, which diminishes hostility and paves the way for productive conflict resolution. This understanding of shared vulnerabilities encourages dialogue and reconciliation, transforming resentment into compassion and commitment to understanding one another.

stories.title: Massachusetts residents sue data centre over 27 diesel generators near homes
Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
stories.summary: The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks. Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.

stories.title: Why has Britain's grass turned yellow? Scientists warn about the future of the island after 'driest month ever'
stories.summary: After experiencing the driest July on record, England's picturesque green fields have succumbed to a fading yellow hue. This alarming trend of increasing heatwaves significantly affects lawns and public parks. While native grasses possess resilience during droughts and can deepen their roots to conserve water, extended dry periods inevitably lead them to enter a dormant state, awaiting rain.

‘Congress responsible for Partition’: CM Yogi says India would be different if Modi were PM in 1947
stories.summary: Speaking at an event in Lucknow marking Partition Horrors Remembrance Day, CM Yogi said the Congress had failed the country by prioritising political power and alleged that the consequences of Partition continue to affect India. “Had Narendra Modi been the Prime Minister of India at the time of Independence, nobody would have been able to damage India in the slightest,” he said.

stories.title: 'First time we did something like this': Former women Naxalites share their Raipur ramp-walk experience
stories.summary: The women, all from Sukma, took part in a Swadeshi fashion show organised as part of rehabilitation efforts for former Naxalites. Sukma SP Mayank Gurjar said the event also gave them an opportunity to promote Swadeshi products. For some of the women, the experience was unlike anything they had done before. One former Naxalite said she surrendered in 2026 and travelled to Raipur for six days of training.

stories.title: Surrogacy dispute escalates after McKenna West gives birth to baby with heart defect
stories.summary: The surrogacy dispute escalated significantly when McKenna West delivered a newborn with a critical heart condition. This infant is currently under the care of intended parents Nausheen Gilkar and Omar Ahmed. Meanwhile, West is fighting against the custody agreements and claims over parental rights in Texas, where the intricate web of contrasting state laws complicates the situation, leading to ongoing legal battles as all parties await further judicial rulings.

Colorado’s 2024 restoration efforts for Preble’s mouse gain momentum with new habitat project
stories.summary: Colorado is taking significant steps to ensure the survival of the endangered Preble's meadow jumping mouse. Efforts focus on restoring essential streamside ecosystems and linking them to floodplains. Landowners are invited to join this initiative through voluntary conservation measures and financial support. A conservation bank was established in 2024 to facilitate these vital restoration projects, with new initiatives rolling out in 2026 to enhance habitat safeguarding.

stories.title: 'Astronauts' land on road craters: Over 100 Jaipur residents stage unique protest against potholes
stories.summary: Gokulpura residents staged a protest on Pratap Circle Road, highlighting poor road conditions. Two individuals dressed as astronauts entered water-filled potholes, simulating a lunar landscape. This unusual demonstration aimed to draw attention to neglected infrastructure and drainage issues. Residents have sought attention from local officials for several months regarding these problems. Tenders for road and drainage work have been awarded and will commence after the monsoon.

stories.title: Iran president Pezeshkian to visit India for BRICS summit amid Middle East tensions
stories.summary: Iran has signalled that it sees India as a potential partner in efforts to ease tensions in West Asia, with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi saying New Delhi could play a greater role in de-escalating the ongoing crisis. Araghchi made the remarks during his visit to India in June. He said Tehran did not see a military solution to the conflict and believed that negotiations offered only viable way forward.

stories.title: BCI action, U-turn and SC rebuke: How NALSAR students' protest against CJI kicked up a row

SC quashes all FIRs against Samay Raina, Ranveer Allahabadia in ‘India’s Got Latent’ case
stories.summary: Along with Raina, the court quashed the FIRs and related proceedings against comedians Vipul Goyal, Balraj Paramjeet Singh Ghai, Sonali Thakkar and Nishant Jagdish Tanwar. The proceedings stemmed from jokes made by the five, which were flagged by the M/s SMA Cure Foundation, an organisation working with people affected by Spinal Muscular Atrophy and other rare diseases.

stories.title: Indian-origin man rejected for H-1B three times, spent $13,000 and formed 700 pages of evidence to stay in US
stories.summary: Sohan Sethi faced multiple H-1B visa rejections after arriving in the United States. He then pursued an O-1 visa, requiring extensive documentation and lawyer fees. Sethi demonstrated extraordinary ability through achievements and industry recognition to secure his stay. This path highlights the challenges faced by skilled professionals seeking to remain in America. He now manages a team, sharing his experience to guide others through the process.

Shakespeare's birth home was nearly shipped to US in 1847; it was saved from a showman's fantasy with a payment of £3,000
stories.summary: In the 1840s, Shakespeare's birthplace in Stratford-upon-Avon faced the threat of sale, as American showman P.T. Barnum aimed to move the historic home to New York. A dedicated committee formed, rallying public donations and support from notable figures like Prince Albert to save the site. Their efforts culminated in the successful acquisition of the house at auction in 1847, ensuring the preservation of this cherished cultural landmark.

stories.title: Egyptian archaeologists uncover 3 tombs, 5 mummies, and Roman remains
stories.summary: An Egyptian archaeological mission has uncovered three tombs at the Sheikh Sobi site. These burials include mummies and sarcophagi from the Late and Roman periods. One tomb contained five mummies, dating to the Late Period. The other two tombs are believed to be from the Roman period. These discoveries offer insights into the Bahariya Oasis's ancient communities.

Morocco is testing a 'sponge' pavement that stays 16°F cooler by itself, aims at replacing black asphalt
stories.summary: Morocco is pioneering a novel sponge pavement designed to enhance water management and mitigate heat effects. Unlike conventional black asphalt, this innovative surface enables water to seep through, promoting natural cooling through evaporation when moisture exists. This initiative aims to bolster urban climate resilience and elevate the comfort of residents, with pilot projects underway in Marrakech and Agadir as part of a larger sustainable city initiative.

This order had previously struck down the Tamil Nadu government's decision for stampede victims' relatives. The Supreme Court questioned the challenge to the government's policy for affected families. The High Court had quashed appointments, citing existing guidelines and potential demands. The Supreme Court's stay provides interim relief to the Tamil Nadu government.
