stories.summary: Over one thousand personnel received Gallantry and Service Medals this Independence Day. Gallantry Medals recognized exceptional courage and actions in critical situations. Many gallantry awards went to personnel serving in Left Wing Extremism-affected areas. President's Medals for Distinguished Service honored special records in their respective fields. Meritorious Service Medals acknowledged valuable service marked by devotion to duty.

German startup Voodin swaps fibreglass for wood turbine blades, aiming for recyclable blades at commercial scale
stories.summary: A pioneering startup in Germany is crafting wind turbine blades using laminated veneer lumber, presenting a sustainable solution to the prevalent fiberglass composite problem. The initial prototypes are currently being tested in the field, demonstrating their potential. This innovation seeks to tackle the increasing challenge of waste generated by conventional wind turbine blades, with plans for larger models aimed at commercial projects on the horizon.

Known for challenging superstition, she had more than 1.28 million Douyin followers. Her controversial videos, including one showing her destroying a Guanyin statue, resurfaced after her death. However, there is no evidence linking her accident to supernatural punishment, despite speculation circulating online.

stories.summary: Candace Owens has opened up about how her feelings changed following Charlie Kirk’s assassination. She said she has moved beyond the initial trauma and no longer feels haunted, instead believing Kirk is spiritually “fighting alongside” her. Owens connected her optimism to her belief that truth will prevail and said she feels Charlie is still with them. She also encouraged viewers to support her show by purchasing merchandise.

stories.title: Amazon AI Opt-Out Backlash: Twitch auto-enables training on streams; creators must change privacy settings
stories.summary: Twitch is facing criticism over a new setting that allows Amazon to use streamer content for generative AI training by default. Streamers can opt out through their privacy settings. Quote by Karl Popper: 'Those who promise us paradise on earth never produced anything but a hell'
stories.summary: Karl Popper highlighted the dangers of striving for a perfect society, warning that such aspirations frequently lead to disastrous outcomes. He pointed out how leaders driven by utopian dreams tend to accumulate excessive power, often resulting in brutality. The French Revolution and several authoritarian regimes serve as stark illustrations of this trend. In the current era, technological advancements and corporate ideologies can echo these same pitfalls.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Zeno: 'We have two ears and one mouth, so we should listen more than we say'
stories.summary: Zeno of Citium, originally a Phoenician trader, established Stoicism in the heart of ancient Athens. He advocated that true listening is an intentional skill rather than simply a precursor to responding. This timeless philosophy champions the value of understanding prior to action. Contemporary studies validate that active listening boosts trust and mitigates conflict, emphasizing the age-old design of our auditory and vocal apparatus.

stories.summary: Exploring vintage postcards reveals a fascinating glimpse into coastal life in early New Jersey. Historian John Joseph Patrick Mulhern recounted his experiences on Sandy Hook, describing the thrilling days of tracking ships and conducting groundbreaking radio experiments. He vividly portrayed the operations of the Navesink lighthouses and the evolving landscape, showcasing the rich maritime heritage and community growth of the time.

Mohuya Khan made about $130,000 from nine income streams while living in Queens, after taxes she...
stories.summary: Mohuya Khan, a dynamic 27-year-old content creator, skillfully juggled nine diverse income streams from her cozy one-bedroom apartment in Astoria, Queens. Her hard work paved the way to financial independence, allowing her to eliminate debts. Yet, the toll of her bustling schedule led to considerable burnout. Recognizing this, Khan has now implemented healthier boundaries to prioritize her overall well-being.

James, 18, Earl of Wessex, passes A-levels, to study at Royal Agricultural University
stories.summary: James, 18, Earl of Wessex, has passed his A-levels and will study rural land management at the Royal Agricultural University in Gloucestershire. Prince Edward and Sophie’s son spent part of the summer working as a farmhand at King Charles III’s Sandringham estate, where he was reportedly seen driving tractors and embracing hands-on work.

She spent 10 months restoring a 160-year-old house; now Lauren Iraeta is reconnecting families...
stories.summary: Lauren Iraeta approached her home renovation as a journey through time, merging creativity with historical inquiry. By delving into neglected family records and tales from earlier occupants, she uncovered names etched within the widow's walk. This captivating endeavor brought descendants closer to their ancestors' cherished childhood narratives, illuminating the profound history woven into these aged abodes.

stories.title: CAG finds 98% shortfall in Green India Mission forest cover targets, red-flags multiple lapses
stories.summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General raised concerns about the inadequacies within the Green India Mission program, noting that the goal of increasing forest cover was far from realized over a decade. The audit pointed to significant issues in planning and financial oversight, which severely undermined the mission's objectives. Key vulnerable areas were neglected during afforestation, diminishing efforts to combat climate change.

stories.title: In June 2026, Washington began restoring 270 acres across two river islands; the project will...
stories.summary: In June 2026, heavy machinery commenced work on a significant coastal restoration initiative. The plan involves the dismantling of outdated sea defenses and the breaching of river levees on two islands, aiming to transform 270 acres of previously cultivated land into natural intertidal wetlands. This restoration will create critical habitats for juvenile Puget Sound Chinook salmon, with the completion date set for autumn 2028.

stories.title: 'Majority of students innocent': BCI reverses ban on NALSAR 2026 batch over CJI invite row
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India has revised its previous directive concerning NALSAR graduates. Students from NALSAR's 2026 cohort can now pursue enrollment with state bar councils. This update followed significant backlash against the original ruling, which prevented these students from becoming advocates due to their association with a protest. The regulator emphasized that the majority of the students were uninvolved and innocent.

stories.summary: At just 18 years old, James Chilimigras has achieved remarkable academic milestones, having graduated from Loyola University New Orleans College of Law, where he ranked in the top two percent of his class while earning five certificates. Displaying an exceptional intellect, he completed both his bachelor's and master’s degrees by the age of 15 and became the youngest Certified Public Accountant in history.

stories.title: 'No clear information': Nepal ‘loses’ papers of centuries-old treaty defining borders with India
stories.summary: Nepal's foreign minister announced that the country might have misplaced the original Sugauli Treaty papers, which played a critical role in establishing its borders with British India after the Anglo-Nepalese War. This comes at a time when border disputes with India have intensified. The government plans to systematically assess numerous international agreements, seeking to amend or renew any that are no longer pertinent.

Meet Scarlett Tiani, the Connecticut student whose dog-safety invention reached US Nationals
stories.summary: In a remarkable achievement, Connecticut student Scarlett Tiani has garnered national attention for her inventive pet safety solution, Tail Wag Warning. Designed to enhance safety during unexpected dog interactions, Tiani's creation received numerous accolades at the prestigious national Invention Convention. With legal support at her side, she is now set to embark on the journey of securing a U.S. patent for her groundbreaking invention.

stories.title: 2027 UP assembly elections: How parties are vying for Dalit votes amid Mayawati’s shrinking base
stories.summary: A notable evolution in Dalit politics is unfolding in Uttar Pradesh, marked by a decline in the Bahujan Samaj Party's dominance. The Bharatiya Janata Party and the Samajwadi Party are actively courting Dalit voters ahead of elections, and the Congress party is also working to regain its historic connections. Meanwhile, Chandrashekhar Azad is establishing a distinct political identity, foreshadowing a significant shift in the Dalit electoral landscape.

stories.title: 'No NALSAR 2026 graduate will be enrolled as advocate': BCI amid CJI convocation invite row
stories.summary: The Bar Council of India has put a pause on NALSAR's enrollments for the 2026 law graduates. This decision comes in the wake of an alleged smear campaign against Chief Justice Surya Kant's presence at the convocation. The Council demands a comprehensive report from NALSAR within three days, requiring identification of those behind this campaign. The situation will be reviewed on August 19, 2026.

stories.title: Elizabeth Hird bought Outer Island in 1964; in 1995, she donated it for wildlife, research and education
stories.summary: Outer Island, once a charming summer getaway, has been transformed into a vital protected wildlife refuge. The island was generously donated to the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service by Elizabeth Hird in 1995, with the intention of preserving its natural resources and fostering education and research. Today, it serves as an invaluable living laboratory for students and researchers alike, ensuring a sustainable conservation legacy for generations to come.

stories.title: New Jersey begins restoration work to bring back forest and wetland habitat along Raritan river
stories.summary: A 112-acre restoration project has begun along New Jersey's Raritan River to restore floodplain forest, wetlands and wildlife habitat affected by past contamination linked to the American Cyanamid Superfund Site. The project will plant about 50,000 native trees and shrubs, create three acres of vernal pools, control invasive plants and protect new vegetation with deer fencing. The restored site will be monitored and managed for 15 years.

stories.title: Michigan's historic Ford House is replacing concrete shoreline with natural habitat
stories.summary: A groundbreaking initiative along Michigan's Lake St. Clair is reshaping the shoreline into thriving natural wetlands. By dismantling decades of concrete barriers, this project endeavors to create essential habitats for local fish populations. The transformation revolves around the historic Edsel and Eleanor Ford Estate, aiming to revitalize coastal marshes while boosting biodiversity and community education on ecosystem preservation.

stories.summary: A Ukrainian passenger train in the Odesa region fell victim to a Russian drone strike, leading to the unfortunate demise of the driver and assistant. Simultaneously, Ukrainian military forces conducted a successful operation against a large oil refinery in Bashkortostan, causing extensive fire damage. This series of events serves as a stark reminder of the ongoing hostilities plaguing the region.

stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi firmly asserted that the Congress party's primary function is to enhance the expression of India’s citizens. stories.title: Carmela Chillery-Watson became the youngest MBE recipient after raising funds for muscular dystrophy
stories.summary: Carmela Chillery-Watson became the youngest MBE recipient at eleven years old. She received the honour for her extensive fundraising and awareness work. This recognition celebrated her dedication to Muscular Dystrophy UK and the disabled community. Carmela's journey began after her diagnosis with a rare muscle-wasting condition at age four. Her continued advocacy aims to promote accessibility and support for those affected.

stories.title: In 2022, Buffalo completed the first emerald shiner passage on the Niagara River; four years later...
stories.summary: The city of Buffalo is enhancing a fish passageway to facilitate the journey of emerald shiners to Lake Erie. By installing steel baffles along the seawall, this initiative aims to mitigate strong currents. This effort is part of a significant multi-million-dollar restoration project for the Niagara River Area, alongside transforming nearby industrial slips into crucial shallow-water habitats, all geared towards rectifying historic environmental harm in western New York.

stories.title: 'This is your last chance': SC ultimatum to Centre over delay in front-of-pack food warning labels
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has expressed strong disapproval towards the government's procrastination regarding food warning labels, specifically calling out the FSSAI. The justices mandated that the Centre has a fortnight to cement its decision, prioritizing public health, particularly for children. The court dismissed claims surrounding traditional foods and foreign standards, signaling that judicial actions could follow if a definitive choice remains absent.

Amondawa tribe does not use weeks, months or years to describe time
stories.summary: The Amondawa tribe structures their daily living around significant events and life phases rather than fixed numbers of weeks or years. Their language features an absence of abstract units of time, showcasing a unique relationship between age and identity rooted in transitional life stages. This inquiry prompts a reevaluation of conventional beliefs regarding human perceptions of time.

stories.title: Washington launches project to restore 270 acres of Skagit estuary habitat
stories.summary: In a significant environmental effort, the restoration of 270 acres of estuary habitat in the South Fork Skagit River is underway, starting from June 2026 and set to finish by fall 2028. This initiative focuses on enhancing the habitat for the endangered Puget Sound Chinook salmon, ensuring a sustainable ecosystem by reconnecting islands to tidal flows, and supporting various wildlife, including waterfowl and shorebirds.

stories.title: 70 million years ago, Earth had 372 days a year, with days lasting 23 hours
stories.summary: Research into ancient shells has unveiled that Earth experienced a 372-day year around seventy million years ago. During the Cretaceous period, each day was approximately twenty-three hours and thirty-one minutes long. This study also examined the ancient Earth-Moon distance and revealed warmer ocean temperatures, with evidence of photosymbiosis. The mollusc fossil indicates it thrived for over nine years on a tropical seabed.

stories.summary: In response to alarming low levels of the Danube river, Romania's energy sector is on high alert. Unit one of the Cernavoda nuclear power facility has ceased operations due to water scarcity. To maintain unit two's functionality, emergency measures including river dredging have been implemented. Authorities have also undertaken the blasting of rock formations to facilitate better water flow. Residents are urged to conserve electricity during high-demand evenings.

stories.summary: As climate change enhances grape-growing conditions, Irish winemakers foresee a bountiful harvest. stories.summary: In a groundbreaking initiative, scientists are working to revive deep-sea coral ecosystems that were harmed by an oil spill. Utilizing corals grown in laboratories along with advanced tools, they have successfully deployed these corals at great depths. This project focuses on rejuvenating delicate habitats in the Gulf of Mexico, with ongoing monitoring set to evaluate both the survival rates of the corals and the overall restoration of the ecosystem.

If vivid dreams leave you exhausted, experts say the problem may not be the dreams but disruptions that prevent deep sleep

During REM, the brain remains highly engaged, which prevents achieving deeper rest. If dreams are recalled, it signals that you woke while dreaming, interrupting the crucial restorative stages of sleep. This interference obstructs clearing adenosine, a natural sleep-inducing byproduct, making tiredness arise from your awakening moment rather than the dreams themselves.

In 1942, Crazy Horse’s sacred bundle was buried in Nebraska; decades later, it vanished
stories.summary: Fast Thunder was given Crazy Horse's sacred medicine bundle before 1877, which then became a closely guarded family heirloom for many years. In 1942, Theodore Means buried this bundle in Minatare, Nebraska, but due to significant landscape alterations in the area, its burial site has remained undiscoverable. The details of the bundle's contents and its precise location continue to be a puzzling enigma.

Why is Chud The Builder finally out of jail after two months? Here’s what we know
stories.summary: Dalton Eatherly, known as Chud The Builder, has been released from jail after two months. He posted a $1 million bond, securing his freedom from Montgomery County Jail. Eatherly faces attempted murder charges linked to a May courthouse shooting incident. He is also involved in a separate Davidson County case for alleged restaurant theft. Both cases are now proceeding to a grand jury for further review.

A buried river was uncovered in Yonkers; 6 months later, wildlife had a 14,000 sq ft habitat
stories.summary: In 2012, Yonkers, New York, completed a project to uncover a section of the Saw Mill River that had been buried beneath a downtown parking lot since the 1920s. The former Larkin Plaza was turned into a three-acre public park. Within six months, the restored river supported 14,000 square feet of new aquatic habitat and several species.

stories.title: California built beaver-like dams in coho creeks; survival rose from 8% to 60% after restoration
stories.summary: Innovative restoration initiatives that emulate beaver dams have drastically enhanced coho salmon survival rates, boosting juvenile survival in a specific creek from eight percent to sixty percent. By generating cooler, slower water environments, these structures are essential for nurturing young salmon. Furthermore, these revitalized areas bolster resistance to drought conditions within the Scott River watershed, underscoring the necessity of reinstating vital wetland habitats for at-risk salmon species.

stories.title: New Haven landfill turned into solar farm now powers about 200 homes and pays the city $72,000 a year
stories.summary: New Haven is transforming a decommissioned landfill into a major solar energy project, installation of 1,920 solar panels that will produce a significant amount of clean energy every year. With anticipated revenue exceeding $1.4 million over two decades, this venture supports New Haven's dedication to enhancing its renewable energy initiatives, ultimately benefitting both the environment and the local economy.

stories.title: QTCinderella’s homophobic friends controversy explained: Streamer under fire over past comments
stories.summary: QTCinderella has responded after renewed criticism over claims that she associates with “homophobic people.” The streamer explained that she believes kindness and personal relationships can help people reconsider harmful beliefs. She also admitted that her comments from a year ago were poorly worded and said she is not friends with bigots. After more confusion online, she shared a longer explanation on her main X account.

In 1977, a Saudi prince towed an Alaskan iceberg to Iowa; now engineers are exploring the idea as freshwater scarcity worsens
stories.summary: In a bold venture back in 1977, a Saudi prince attempted to tow an iceberg to address a water supply dilemma. This audacious project confronted considerable engineering hurdles and substantial expenses. With current desalination methods proving both expensive and environmentally taxing, the growing issue of iceberg melting has rekindled interest. Engineers are now revisiting the practicality of transporting icebergs as a viable source of freshwater.

stories.title: Meet Zac Waters, the 13-year-old who spent 300 hrs 3D-printing wheelchair for a 21-month-old
stories.summary: A 13-year-old boy from Lehi, Utah, spent about 300 hours during his summer designing, printing, testing and assembling a custom mobility chair for a 21-month-old girl. Zac Waters found MakeGood, a nonprofit that provides free 3D-printed mobility devices, and used his interest in 3D printing to build a chair tailored to the toddler’s needs.

Plastic found in Amazon fish as particles become trapped in river plants
stories.summary: Plastic pollution is alarmingly prevalent among fish in the Amazon, leading to serious complications in their gills and digestive systems. The surrounding aquatic vegetation along the river captures plastic waste, forming hazardous exposure hotspots. Certain fish species can breathe air, but this adaptation makes them more susceptible to microplastics, as their smaller gills limit their capabilities to filter out harmful pollutants.

stories.title: Faulty Ola scooter, no proper service: Consumer panel orders Rs 1.04 lakh refund, compensation
stories.summary: A Kerala consumer commission found Ola Electric guilty of service deficiency and unfair trade practices. The commission ordered Ola Electric to refund the scooter's full purchase price. This decision followed repeated scooter defects and a lack of proper after-sales support. The customer experienced significant financial loss and mental stress due to these issues. Ola Electric must now pay compensation and complaint costs within thirty days.

America poisoned prairie dogs for decades, but scientists found they sustain healthy grasslands
stories.summary: Prairie dogs were once viewed as pests but are now recognized as ecological assets. Their burrowing and grazing improve soil and water infiltration significantly. These small mammals help prevent grasslands from turning into shrublands. Areas with prairie dogs also provide more forage for livestock and store more carbon. The loss of prairie dogs diminishes crucial ecosystem services for both nature and people.

Meet Red Handfish, the endangered 'walking' fish that became Photo Ark's 18,000th species
stories.summary: For 20 years, photographer Joel Sartore has been documenting animals through his Photo Ark project, which has now reached its 18,000th species. The latest addition is the critically endangered red handfish, a tiny marine fish that uses its fins to move across the seafloor. Sartore hopes the project will raise awareness about threatened species and help preserve a record of animals that could disappear.

stories.title: In 1868, an eclipse in India revealed an element found on Earth 27 years later
stories.summary: During the solar eclipse of 1868 in India, astronomers stumbled upon an enigmatic yellow spectral line, initially observed by Pierre Jules Janssen. Although its significance was not immediately recognized, Norman Lockyer soon named the unidentified element helium upon further analysis. Eventually, William Ramsay verified helium's presence on Earth in 1895 by extracting it from a mineral, solidifying Janssen's pioneering approach to studying solar prominences.

stories.title: Discarded salon hair is being transformed into an oil-absorbing barrier that protects mangroves from oil spills in Rio de Janeiro
stories.summary: Discarded human hair is now preventing oil pollution in Rio de Janeiro's Guanabara Bay. Each gram of hair absorbs approximately five grams of oil, repelling water effectively. These hair barriers, made from salon waste, can remain in the water for four months. The initiative protects vulnerable mangrove ecosystems from chronic and everyday oil leaks. This innovative project aims to aid the recovery of the bay's marine life.

California’s Shasta Dam flooded Kennett, a copper-mining town beneath Lake Shasta
stories.summary: Once a bustling northern California mining hub, Kennett was swallowed by the depths of Shasta Lake following the construction of the Shasta Dam. This ambitious federal project aimed at water management inundated the town, which thrived on copper mining and railroads. Today, only historical accounts and the lake itself hint at the vibrant community that once existed in this submerged landscape.

The Netherlands built new islands from 37 million tonnes of lake sediment
stories.summary: In an innovative move, Dutch engineers have fashioned new islands from lake sediment to rejuvenate a fragile freshwater ecosystem. These manmade structures have swiftly drawn an array of flora and fauna, notably various bird populations. The initiative has revitalised an ailing lake, transforming it into a bustling habitat for marine life and migratory birds alike.

Nasa's New Horizons reached Arrokoth in 2019, revealing the early solar system
stories.summary: NASA's New Horizons spacecraft made an astonishing visit to Arrokoth, a remote Kuiper Belt object, uncovering vital clues about the solar system's early formation. This ancient body exhibits a fascinating two-lobed structure, hinting at a gentle collision between two distinct entities. Furthermore, its strikingly red surface is indicative of complex organic materials, giving scientists a rare window into our cosmic origins.

stories.title: Doc Revisits EDP445 Controversy: film tracks rise, sting and new claims; proceeds go to RAINN

The film revisits the 2021 sting that ended his YouTube career and includes Moreland’s claim that God saved him from arrest during another alleged incident. It also introduces his girlfriend, Marissa, and discusses their relationship.

stories.title: Knowles Rejects Debate Role: commentator refuses Kirk murder clash; urges trial over podcasts

He also criticized the growing industry of Charlie Kirk murder content, while acknowledging that Owens’ series has attracted significant attention and views.

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella is actively overseeing emergency response and recovery efforts.

North Carolina dam tested three flows to balance wildlife and power
stories.summary: For two decades, the Roanoke Rapids Dam has been diligently analyzing water flow levels. Scientists observed the effects on fish and mussel populations, discovering that a medium flow rate supports wildlife while optimizing power generation. This significant finding permits greater water diversion to enhance electricity production, as the dam commits to using this medium flow strategy for an additional eighteen years.

stories.title: No Proof Of YouTube Split: Fans speculate about Dalton and Sako; arrest claims stay unverified
stories.summary: YouTuber Dalton Ain't Worried recently posted a heartfelt video that has triggered speculation about a potential split with his wife Sako. Observers have pointed out the couple's scarce public appearances lately, fueling rumors of marital strife. Additionally, unverified reports of an arrest in West Virginia from February have emerged, though no verified details are available. Despite this, their joint videos continue to showcase a united front as a married couple.
